subzone:agmond-s-end.text: Agmond's End. Stonevault troggs overrun Agmond's End, the ruined dwarven dig in the southern Badlands. Prospector Agmond led the search until the creatures killed him and his miners. Dwarven prospectors came to Agmond's End in search of ancient relics and the earth's buried history. Then troggs surged from nearby crevices and overwhelmed the miners. Agmond fell in the attack, and the site took his name. Stonevault troggs now infest the ruined dig, among shattered crates and abandoned tools. Near the ruined excavation, Theldurin the Lost lives at a solitary camp. The dwarf's sanity has long since frayed. Yet he remains one of the few souls willing to brave the southern desert near the doomed site.

subzone:aku-mai-s-lair.text: Aku'mai's Lair. Beyond the Moonshrine Sanctum, Aku'mai's Lair lies beneath Blackfathom Deeps. Cultists and naga gather in its flooded depths to honor Aku'mai, a hydra they call a servant of the Old Gods. Behind the Moonshrine Sanctum's sealed double doors, four braziers flank a naga statue. Light them, and guardians sworn to defend the threshold awaken. Beyond the doors, a sunless grotto rests beneath the water. Twilight's Hammer cultists and invading naga gather there to honor Aku'mai, an ancient hydra with three heads. They believe the beast serves the Old Gods. To Twilight's Hammer cultists, Aku'mai is an omen of a promised age of darkness. They believe the beast's emergence and continued sustenance will herald the breaking of the subterranean prisons that hold their ancient deities. Sacrificial offerings feed Aku'mai, while dark magic guards the pool where it dwells. The cult's plans center on the hydra as ancient evil claws its way back into Kalimdor.

subzone:altar-of-storms-burning-steppes.text: Altar of Storms (Burning Steppes). Blackrock warlocks perform fel rites at the Altar of Storms in the Burning Steppes. The dark monument draws those seeking demonic power. Blackrock warlocks hold the Altar of Storms, where they perform rites to channel fel magic and seal dark pacts. The monument was built during the earlier wars. Nearby, the hermit Gorzeeki Wildeyes and his master, Mor'zul Bloodbringer, keep an encampment overlooking the altar. Renegade practitioners study its violent energies and devise demanding rites for spellcasters who seek greater dark power.

subzone:alterac-mountains-classic.text:
Alterac Mountains (Classic). In the Alterac Mountains, ogres, outlaws, and armies fight over the highlands. North of Hillsbrad Foothills, rain darkens the slopes beneath snowbound peaks. Once home to Alterac and Dalaran, the region now lies largely in ruins. Rain falls over the Alterac Mountains, where pine forests climb toward snow at the highest reaches. Three human powers once held these heights: the mountain kingdom of Alterac, the magocracy of Dalaran, and the fortified town of Strahnbrad. Betrayal and war brought them low. Crushridge ogres occupy Alterac's ruined capital, and outlaws hold Strahnbrad. Among Dalaran's shattered remains, surviving wizards labor to restore their ruined sanctuary. Mountain lions and yeti stalk the frostbitten ridges, while desperate factions fight for the uplands. The Syndicate are dispossessed human nobles turned brigands. From old estates and foothill camps, they strike with blades and ambushes. They clash without end with the advancing ogres.

Deep passes into the high crags hold staging camps for the bloody war between the Stormpike Expedition and the Frostwolf Clan. Both fight over the hidden reaches of Alterac Valley.

subzone:andorhal.text:
Andorhal. In Andorhal, the Scourge still holds the ruined town. Once northern Lordaeron's thriving agricultural heart, it became the place where Kel'Thuzad tainted the grain with the Plague of Undeath. During the Third War, that harvest carried horror across the region. Before the Third War, Andorhal gathered grain from across Lordaeron and sent it east to Hearthglen and Stratholme. As the Eastweald's prosperous granary, it fed a vast network. Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned chose the town to begin their plot. They tainted crates of grain with the Plague of Undeath, turning the kingdom's breadbasket into a source of sickness. Countless citizens were infected before the Crown understood the danger. Prince Arthas Menethil and Jaina Proudmoore first faced Kel'Thuzad in Andorhal and slew him. His death did not end the danger. After returning from Northrend as a champion of the Scourge, Arthas marched back to claim Kel'Thuzad's remains.

Uther the Lightbringer and the remaining Silver Hand paladins made a desperate stand to defend King Terenas's ashes. The paladins fell, and Arthas slew Uther, his former pupil. Now the once grand settlement is a blight-choked Scourge stronghold.

subzone:ariden-s-camp.text:
Ariden's Camp. In Deadwind Pass, Ariden's Camp lies abandoned north of the road from Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows. Travelers pass beneath Karazhan's shadow and wonder who pitched a tent there. North of the road from Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows, weathered cloth and cold ashes mark Ariden's Camp. It may once have been an ordinary stop, long abandoned by living men.

Dark sorcery has left its mark across Deadwind Pass. No one knows who named the camp for Ariden or what fortune its owner sought near Karazhan. The pass's lingering horrors have swallowed the answer.

subzone:bal-lal-ruins.text: Bal'lal Ruins. Bloodscalp trolls guard Bal'lal Ruins on Stranglethorn Vale's northwestern shore, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. The old Gurubashi stones overlook the Vile Reef. Bloodscalp trolls keep watch among the weathered stones of Bal'lal Ruins above the Vile Reef. The site lies on Stranglethorn Vale's coast, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. These stones remain from the Gurubashi Empire, the troll civilization that once ruled southern Azeroth. Cracked walls mark the ruins' long decay, and Bloodscalp trolls defend these ancestral relics against intruders.

subzone:balia-mah-ruins.text: Balia'mah Ruins. Skullsplitter warriors hold the Balia'mah Ruins in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Across the river east of Grom'gol Base Camp, the old Gurubashi settlement's stone tiers crumble under the jungle. Balia'mah's stone terraces recall the Gurubashi Empire, which once ruled much of the southern Eastern Kingdoms. When its ancient capital fell, Gurubashi lands split among warring factions. Now the Skullsplitter tribe holds the ruins. They defend them from beasts, ogres from the Mosh'Ogg mound, and outsiders crossing the river.

subzone:bay-of-storms.text: Bay of Storms. Storms churn along Azshara’s eastern cliffs, where sailors face a hazardous coast. Ancient ruins, submerged caverns, and dangerous sea beasts fill the bay. The Bay of Storms opens onto the Great Sea from Azshara’s eastern coast. Turbulent waters and rocky outcrops shelter dangerous wildlife and ancient aquatic threats. The sunken Temple of Arkkoran lies beneath the waves. Hetaera’s Clutch reefs and Scalebeard’s Cave mark the shore. Casual sailors keep away, leaving the coast to its monsters.

subzone:bear-s-head.text: Bear's Head. On Bear's Head in southeastern Azshara, Timbermaw furbolgs keep their outposts beneath the cliffs. Their settlements link to larger homes farther north, while Archmage Xylem studies in a tower above. Timbermaw furbolgs keep outposts on Bear's Head, the high ground of southeastern Azshara. Their camps connect north to the larger dens at Ursolan and Timbermaw Hold. Above them, Xylem's Tower stands on the cliffs. Archmage Xylem studies arcane magic there in seclusion with his apprentices and high elven associates. The coast around them remains troubled.

subzone:beezil-s-wreck.text: Beezil's Wreck. East of Tabetha's Farm, Beezil's Wreck draws scavengers to its broken zeppelin and scattered cargo. East of Tabetha's Farm, the goblin zeppelin lies split apart in the muck. It carried cargo south across Kalimdor before plunging into the swamp. Captain Beezil is gone from the marsh. Crates and ticking machinery lie among the reeds, rotting in the brine. Beasts prowl around the crash site, but scavengers still brave them for the cargo that survived. The zeppelin carried volatile goods, including Seaforium boosters and heavy crates. They risk their lives to salvage what remains before marsh water corrodes it.

subzone:bitter-reaches.text: Bitter Reaches. Along Azshara’s northeastern cliffs, the Bitter Reaches rise above the Great Sea. Predators roam the heights, and mountain giants hold the northern ridges. The Bitter Reaches rise above the Great Sea along Azshara’s northeastern cliffs. Feral hippogryphs and two-headed chimaeras nest among the heights. Acidic oozes seep through the cold ground, while colossal mountain giants claim the high northern ridges. They drive lesser creatures away and make the frozen approaches perilous for a lone traveler. Mountain Silversage grows in sparse clusters on the crags. The rare herb clings to high rock faces and windy perches. Herbalists must avoid the giants and territorial chimaeras to gather it.

subzone:black-channel-marsh.text: Black Channel Marsh. Raptors prowl Black Channel Marsh beside the road to Menethil Harbor. In the southwestern Wetlands, travelers and couriers face danger along the coast. Black Channel Marsh covers the low ground southwest of the main road to Menethil Harbor. Caravan drivers and couriers know to beware. The raised road may look safe, yet territorial raptors lurk among the still channels and thick reeds. Hungry beasts often stray onto the road and ambush recruits or weary travelers who wander even a little from the path.

subzone:blackchar-cave.text: Blackchar Cave. In southwestern Searing Gorge, rubble seals Blackchar Cave against the crags. Blackchar Cave sits among the crags near the approach to Blackrock Mountain. Rubble and scorched slag seal its entrance, closing every tunnel beyond. Ash and magma scar the barren ground around it.

subzone:blackfathom-deeps.text: Blackfathom Deeps. Naga, satyr, and the Twilight's Hammer hold Blackfathom Deeps beneath Ashenvale's northwestern coast. Flooded halls that once honored Elune lie in ruin beneath the Zoram Strand. Beneath Ashenvale's northwestern cliffs, flooded halls remain from an ancient temple. Before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the temple honored Elune and held its own moonwell. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the shrine sank beneath the waves and was thought lost forever. Over millennia, the shorelines receded and the ground shifted, leaving the temple partly flooded beneath the cliffs.

subzone:blackrock-mountain.text:
Blackrock Mountain. In Blackrock Mountain, rival armies fight above depths scarred by fire and war. Ragnaros's summoning raised the volcano between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge, and its roots now hold dwarven halls. Blackrock Mountain rose from the War of the Three Hammers two and a half centuries ago. The united armies of Ironforge and the Wildhammer clan threatened to destroy the Dark Iron dwarves. So Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan reached into the earth for a weapon, and his spell broke the barriers between worlds. It brought Ragnaros the Firelord to Azeroth.

The blast tore apart the Redridge range, carved out the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes, and hurled a vast volcano into the sky. Thaurissan died in the destruction. The surviving Dark Iron clan was bound to serve the Firelord forever. They carved Shadowforge City deep among the mountain's roots. Blackrock Mountain claimed a grim place in history during the First and Second Wars. After Stormwind was sacked, Orgrim Doomhammer purged the Shadow Council and made Blackrock Spire the Horde's fortress capital. The mountain remains a battlefield.

Dark Iron dwarves and their elemental master hold the fiery depths. Above, rogue Blackrock orcs, dragonkin, and their dark masters occupy the spires.

subzone:blackrock-pass.text: Blackrock Pass. At Blackrock Pass, a heavy iron gate marks the road from Redridge Mountains into the Burning Steppes. The corridor runs north beneath the cliffs, from human heartlands to the war grounds of Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs. Travelers on foot cross a harsh frontier. Blackrock Pass cuts through the mountains between Redridge Mountains and the Burning Steppes. A heavy iron gate marks the rocky boundary, beyond the forests and lakes of the southern valleys. South of the gate, Lakeshire's beleaguered militia protects pastoral lands. North of it, fire elementals, dragonkin, and hostile orc warbands fill an open wasteland. Few cross on foot unless bound for the shadow of Blackrock Mountain itself.

subzone:blackrock-stronghold.text: Blackrock Stronghold. Dark Horde orcs hold the approaches to Blackrock Mountain from Blackrock Stronghold. Their fortified camp is a field garrison in the Burning Steppes. Blackrock Stronghold spreads across the scorched foothills below Blackrock Mountain. The Blackrock clan keeps its main base here in the Burning Steppes. These orcs cling to the old ways of war. They follow Rend Blackhand and the dragonkin lurking above in the spire, not Thrall's Horde. Blackrock Stronghold guards the mountain's southern approaches. Its forces gather for attacks into the Redridge Mountains and neighboring human lands. The watch is constant, and anyone crossing the blasted wastes meets its challenge.

subzone:blackwood-lake.text: Blackwood Lake. In southern Eastern Plaguelands, a small Argent Dawn camp watches Blackwood Lake. Its waters teem with hostile, corrupted elementals and hold memories of tragedy and war. The plague that poisons much of the Eastweald has reached Blackwood Lake. Diseased water elementals churn beneath its murky surface and attack anyone who comes near the shore.

subzone:bloodfen-burrow.text: Bloodfen Burrow. Bloodfen raptors now crowd the cavern and clearing in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh. They have overrun the ruins of a settlement that once struggled to survive the wetlands. Bloodfen raptors crowd the cave and hollow in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh. The sheltered crevice and rich hunting grounds draw the pack. Outside the entrance, scattered debris and splintered remains mark an unidentified settlement. Travelers also whisper that Cortello, an adventurous buccaneer, left one of his hidden riddle clues somewhere in the den.

subzone:bloodvenom-falls.text: Bloodvenom Falls. Toxic water pours over Felwood’s northern cliffs at Bloodvenom Falls. It feeds the Bloodvenom River, carrying demon-spawned rot down the mountains and beyond. Bloodvenom Falls pours over the bluffs in Felwood, a vivid wound in Kalimdor’s ancient forests. Once pristine, the water was warped by demonic magic and the Burning Legion’s remnants during the Third War. The falls feed the Bloodvenom River, which winds through the heart of Felwood. Then the tainted torrent rushes down the mountain slopes and becomes the foul Wildbend River in Darkshore, carrying blight beyond Felwood’s borders. Runoff from Bloodvenom Falls stains the riverbed and warps all it touches. Twisted treants, sickening beasts, and aggressive slimes breed along the swampy banks around its spray. To druids and wardens trying to contain Felwood’s rot, the falls show how deeply northern Kalimdor’s waters remain sickened at their source.

subzone:bloodvenom-post.text: Bloodvenom Post. At Bloodvenom Post, Horde guards watch Felwood’s high cliffs above Darkshore. Their tauren-style settlement stands amid demonic taint and corrupted wildlife. Bloodvenom Post clings to Felwood’s high cliffs above Darkshore. A narrow trail follows the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River from the main road. Traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts give Horde wanderers a base in the dying forest. Scouts watch demonic forces advancing through the region and study the corruption in the waters. They also track wildlife changed by the Burning Legion’s lingering power. From the cliffs, Bloodvenom Post overlooks Felwood’s tainted wilds and northern Darkshore. Its remote position lets Horde forces watch night elf movements along the western coast. The camp also lies well beyond easy reach of Alliance patrols on the forest’s central road.

subzone:bloodvenom-river.text: Bloodvenom River. In central Felwood, Bloodvenom River bears the forest’s demonic corruption downstream. Its waters cross the mountains into Darkshore and continue as the tainted Wildbend River. Bloodvenom River cuts through Felwood’s corrupted heart, carrying the forest’s decay. Vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul runoff line its banks, left by the Burning Legion’s invasion. The corruption flows west through the mountains into Darkshore. There, the river continues as the Wildbend River.

subzone:bluefen.text: Bluefen. Bluefen’s marsh paths put travelers between swamp predators and Theramore scouts. The bog lies in northern Dustwallow Marsh, just east of Brackenwall Village. East of Brackenwall Village, home to the Stonemaul ogres, Bluefen’s wet ground teems with danger. Raptors, giant spiders, carrion-feeding birds, and crocolisks prowl the marsh. Theramore Infiltrators also move through the bog, watching Horde movements and carrying human influence deeper into the swamp.

subzone:bluegill-marsh.text: Bluegill Marsh. Bluegill Marsh lies in western Wetlands, where the Bluegill tribe claims the shallows. Gobbler guards their huts and waterways, and travelers risk being surrounded. Bluegill murlocs crowd the muddy flats and reeds of western Wetlands. Their tribe has built crude camps in the stagnant water and claims the marsh. They live and hunt in close-knit packs. Travelers and scouts from Menethil Harbor risk ambush from every side when they wade into Bluegill territory, where chieftain Gobbler prowls the shallows.

subzone:bolgan-s-hole.text: Bolgan's Hole. In southern Desolace, the Gelkis keep their power and sacred crystals within Bolgan's Hole. Their khan and shamans guard the cavern. Above the Gelkis encampment, the khan holds court in a cavern cut into the bluffs. Veteran guards and influential shamans gather around their ruler. The cliffs defend the clan from its rivals, especially the Magram centaur to the east. Blue crystals gleam in the damp stone walls of Bolgan's Hole. The Gelkis call them the tears of Theradras and honor them as sacred blessings. Their shamans harvest and guard the crystals. They believe the stones bring protection from Princess Theradras, the primal earth elemental mother of the centaur race.

subzone:bones-of-grakkarond.text: Bones of Grakkarond. Across central Silithus, Grakkarond's bones lie beneath the sun. The bronze dragon fell in the ancient War of the Shifting Sands, and the Anubisath keep his remains sacred. Grakkarond's skull and ribcage lie across the dunes of central Silithus. A thousand years ago, he fell in the War of the Shifting Sands. In that great clash, Ossirian the Unscarred struck him down. Ossirian was an Anubisath warrior, empowered by the dark powers of the city-kingdom. The Anubisath leave the bones where Grakkarond fell, a sacred mark of their might against the dragonflights.

subzone:booty-bay.text:
Booty Bay. In Booty Bay, goblins keep a neutral port open to Alliance and Horde alike. The Steamwheedle Cartel's Blackwater Raiders hold this harbor in southern Stranglethorn Vale, where travelers enter by land through a giant shark's jaws. Booty Bay began as the human settlement of Blackwater Cove. Jungle trolls took it, then goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel captured it. Now merchants, outcasts, and scoundrels come here from many lands. Baron Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn watch the port from the balconies of the Salty Sailor Tavern.

The harbor may seem lawless, but the cartel keeps order. Anyone may drink, trade, or hire mercenaries, so long as they respect the cartel's peace and pay the harbor fees. Booty Bay's docks link the Eastern Kingdoms with ratchet across the Great Sea. Trade and travelers pass between the continents here. Such wealth draws enemies. The Bloodsail Buccaneers are a hostile pirate fleet that raids Blackwater shipping and prowls the Stranglethorn coast. They plot to destroy and plunder the goblin port.

subzone:boulder-gor.text: Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor commands western Arathi, north of Stromgarde, where Boulderfist ogres and Witherbark trolls share an encampment. North of Stromgarde Keep’s crumbling ramparts, Boulder'gor rises above the central roads of Arathi. The Boulderfist Outpost mound stands among its shadows, a stronghold of ogre power across the highlands. Boulderfist ogres share fires and fortifications with Witherbark forest trolls. Their shadowy spellcasters add dark magic to the clan’s brute force, and together they endanger travelers on the roads. From Boulder'gor’s slopes, you can look across the open highlands of western Arathi. The hill lies between Stromgarde’s Syndicate-infiltrated ruins and the plains’ wild elemental sites. Heavily guarded and hostile, Boulder'gor remains a tribal stronghold against Alliance and Horde wanderers.

subzone:boulderfist-hall.text: Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist ogres hold the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, north of Thandol Span. Under Kor'gresh Coldrage, they threaten the nearby roads and valleys. Boulderfist Hall shelters the Boulderfist clan in the southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands. Its earthen walls and deep caverns house ogre brutes and magi, near Witherbark Village and the bridge at Thandol Span. Kor'gresh Coldrage leads the clan from deep within the mound, with enforcers such as Phalanax at his side. The ogres hold the surrounding roads by force, making travel between Arathi and the Wetlands dangerous for travelers and supply caravans.

subzone:boulderfist-outpost.text: Boulderfist Outpost. Deep within Boulder'gor, Boulderfist ogres hold a fortified mound and its inner halls. A few Witherbark trolls dwell among them in the Arathi Highlands. Boulderfist Outpost lies at the heart of Boulder'gor in western Arathi. Brute enforcers rule the settlement above, while the clan's strength gathers inside the mound. Carved from earth and stone, its dark halls serve as a den and a holding place. A few Witherbark troll witch doctors live among the ogres, a sign that the tribes sometimes share this ground.

subzone:brackenwall-village.text:
Brackenwall Village. In the northwest marsh, Brackenwall Village shelters the Stonemaul ogres. Black dragonkin drove them from their southern home, and spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight now threaten the refuge. Overlord Mok'Morokk led the Stonemaul survivors north after black dragonkin drove them from their ancient home at Stonemaul Village. Successor to Rexxar, he gathered the clan in the swamp to build Brackenwall. Earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower give the battered ogres a refuge they can defend.

Brackenwall is allied with the Horde, but Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoards supplies, and refuses to face the draconic threat. The ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries give the clan spiritual and tactical guidance.

subzone:broken-hall.text: Broken Hall. Beneath the Pool of Tears, Broken Hall lies flooded at the Temple of Atal'Hakkar's outer edge. Ysera and her green dragons dragged the ziggurat beneath the waters, driving the Atal'ai into deeper chambers. Murky swamp water covers the floor of Broken Hall. When the green dragons dragged the Atal'ai ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outer hall suffered most. Its floor collapsed, and the Atal'ai zealots left the flooded chamber for deeper parts of the temple. You must wade through the ruins before climbing the stairs to the Hall of Masks.

subzone:broken-pillar.text: Broken Pillar. South of Gadgetzan, Marvon Rivetseeker studies artifacts buried in Tanaris’s sands. His research camp stands beside the ancient troll ruins of the Broken Pillar. South of Gadgetzan and east of the Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar rises from the desert. Tanaris has swallowed much of its ancient troll stonework. Desert beasts roam nearby, yet the ruins still offer clues to the continent’s earliest civilizations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher from Ratchet, has made his camp beside the shattered stones. There he examines Gahz'ridian relics scattered across the waste.

subzone:bronzebeard-encampment.text: Bronzebeard Encampment. In southern Silithus, Bronzebeard Encampment keeps a dwarven foothold east of the Scarab Wall. Explorer's League researchers study ancient silithid glyphs and mysteries buried beneath the desert. Bronzebeard Encampment stands near Silithus's southern bluffs, within sight of the Scarab Wall. Ironforge founded the camp for archaeological work. Researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge study inscriptions and monuments left by forgotten civilizations. Scorching heat, scorpids, and silithid swarms make their work dangerous. At Bronzebeard Encampment, study goes hand in hand with survival. Silithid threats spread from underground hives, and the monstrous scorpid Deathclasp prowls nearby. Researchers rely on visiting adventurers to bring back rubbings of obscure glyphs, decipher ancient insectoid tongues, and find companions lost in the desert.

subzone:browman-mill.text: Browman Mill. Undead now crowd Browman Mill, north of Light's Hope Chapel. Once it served Lordaeron's timber trade; now Stephen Browman remains trapped in death within his ruined workshop. Before the Third War, Browman Mill worked timber from the Eastweald for nearby towns and homesteads. Then the Scourge plague swept across Lordaeron, and the mill fell with the province. Now rotting timbers and shattered wheels lie idle while abominations, banshees, and skeletal warriors patrol the grounds. So close to Light's Hope Chapel, the ruins show how near the undead horde has come to the Argent Dawn. Stephen Browman owned Browman Mill before the Scourge overran his estate. The Scourge killed him and raised him as a ghoul, bound to the Lich King's will. He remains in the dark mill, guarding the broken remains of his life's work.

subzone:bulwark.text: Bulwark. At Tirisfal's edge, Bulwark keeps watch over the Western Plaguelands. Forsaken and Argent Dawn forces hold the outpost together, and Horde expeditions set out from there into the tainted east. Forsaken guards hold Bulwark's palisade where Tirisfal Glades meets the Western Plaguelands. The outpost bars the road from blighted lands where the undead roam. Here, Forsaken forces work with the neutral Argent Dawn. Together, they call on seasoned Horde champions to strike at the Scourge and keep the Lich King's minions from reaching Tirisfal.

subzone:caer-darrow.text: Caer Darrow. Phantoms haunt Caer Darrow above Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. House Barov once ruled from its keep, now sold to Kel'Thuzad and remade as Scholomance. Caer Darrow guarded Lordaeron and held an ancient elven runestone long before the Scourge. During the Second War, the Horde sacked the fortress and broke the stone apart for Gul'dan's Altars of Storms. Lord Uther the Lightbringer sailed to aid the survivors, but Alterac privateers ambushed his fleet. Their treachery exposed Alterac's betrayal to the Alliance.

subzone:camp-e-thok.text: Camp E'thok. In northwestern Thousand Needles, caravans risk ambush below Camp E'thok. Galak centaur hunt travelers in the canyon. Galak centaur hunt travelers in the canyon at Camp E'thok. Their camp lies in northwestern Thousand Needles. From there, the clan ambushes merchant caravans crossing the riverbed below. One caravan carried the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner. The centaur seized its goods, but Wizlo's fierce pet panther kept his prized gadget beyond their reach.

subzone:camp-kosh.text: Camp Kosh. At Camp Kosh, Dustbelcher ogres prey on caravans crossing the northern Badlands. They scavenge abandoned gear from roads leading toward Kargath and the Searing Gorge. In the northern Badlands, Dustbelcher ogres make their northernmost camp at Camp Kosh. Their tribe also holds nearby camps called Boff, Cagg, and Wurg. From these camps, they strike vulnerable supply lines bound for Kargath or traveling west into the Searing Gorge. When dwarven prospectors led by Sigrun Ironhew fled the excavation at Uldaman, the ogres raided their abandoned wagons. They carried food rations and weapons back into Camp Kosh.

subzone:camp-mojache.text: Camp Mojache. At Camp Mojache, the Horde holds a foothold in eastern Feralas beside the stream that feeds Wildwind Lake. The tauren outpost offers provisions and flight connections amid dangerous wildlife and ancient ruins. In eastern Feralas, Camp Mojache gives Horde travelers shelter beside the stream that feeds Wildwind Lake. Deep forest surrounds the camp, with savage wildlife, Gordunni ogres, and Woodpaw gnolls nearby. Lodging, trade supplies, and a wind rider roost support travelers crossing the region. Tauren hunters and braves watch for attacks from the wilderness. Holding Mojache extends the Horde's reach across Feralas, where Night Elves hold the coast and dark forces lurk within Dire Maul.

subzone:camp-wurg.text: Camp Wurg. Dustbelcher ogres hold Camp Wurg among the Badlands crags. Their camps reach across much of the harsh region. Dustbelcher ogres guard Camp Wurg among the Badlands crags. It is one of their four main camps, with Camp Cagg, Camp Boff, and Camp Kosh. The ogres scavenge across the desert wastes and defend their rugged territory fiercely. Brutes and enforcers gather around crude fires and rough hides. Boss Tho'grun, their chieftain, has no permanent seat at Wurg. He roams the Badlands trails and watches over all four camps.

subzone:cape-of-stranglethorn.text:
Cape of Stranglethorn. Booty Bay holds fast as rival crews contest the Cape of Stranglethorn. From Gurubashi Arena to the ocean cliffs, goblins, Bloodsail Buccaneers, ancient jungle trolls, and wildlife struggle for control. South of Gurubashi Arena, dense jungle reaches the coast. The Ruins of Jubuwal and the Ruins of Aboraz mark ground the Gurubashi Empire no longer holds. Now predators, murloc encampments, and rival pirate crews fill the beaches, coves, and clearings. They fight over trade routes and buried plunder. The Blackwater Raiders hold the cape’s greatest power. Baron Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn lead them from Booty Bay, a neutral harbor carved into the southern bay’s cliffs. Steamships link the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor through Ratchet.

Yet goblin control remains precarious. Along the southern shoals and outer islands, the Bloodsail Buccaneers raid supply lines and plot to overthrow Booty Bay and seize the South Seas.

subzone:capital-gardens.text:
Capital Gardens. In Dire Maul's western wing, corrupted growth and spirits haunt the Capital Gardens. Once a park for Kaldorei nobles, the grounds now shelter corrupted ancients, ghosts, and Shen'dralar remnants. Broken marble terraces and twisted gray boughs fill the Capital Gardens. Corrupted treants haunt the courtyards. Ten millennia ago, Eldre'Thalas was one of the Kaldorei empire's great cities. Its outdoor district offered enchanted plants and broad terraces where Highborne sorcerers met to debate and rest.

After the Great Sundering, the enclave fell on hard times. Without the Well of Eternity, the Shen'dralar turned to dark magic to preserve their immortality. The gardens withered, and lingering corruption keeps the woodland from healing.

subzone:cauldron.text: Cauldron. In the Searing Gorge, Dark Iron miners drive their work at Cauldron under the watch of overseers and fire elementals. Captured slaves labor in its depths, where heat and torment have driven many mad. At the center of the Searing Gorge, Cauldron cuts deep into scorched earth. The Dark Irons fortified the pit after Emperor Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros with catastrophic results. Heavy excavation machines scrape rock and ore from the smoldering stone along the canyon walls. Below, fire and magma elementals prowl beside Dark Iron taskmasters. Heat rises from the mountain's depths. Captured slaves endure brutal shifts beneath the lash of Dark Iron overseers. Relentless labor, sweltering heat, and torment have driven many mad. They can no longer tell friend from foe. Anyone who disturbs their work is struck, even those who might offer a chance at freedom.

subzone:caverns-of-time.text:
Caverns of Time. In the Caverns of Time, Nozdormu and the bronze dragonflight guard Azeroth's fragile timeways. Deep in Tanaris's eastern cliffs, they watch for mortal intrusion and changes to time's flow. Deep beneath Tanaris's eastern cliffs, the Caverns of Time gather the currents of history. At the dawn of the world, the titans charged Nozdormu the Timeless One and his bronze dragonflight with guarding these winding corridors.

Time moves strangely within them, and hidden rifts show glimpses of the past and future. Relics from distant eras lie scattered across the sands. Anachronos watches near the entrance while lesser bronze drakes patrol the descent and guard the one true timeline. The Caverns of Time also hold a vault where past and future meet. Over millennia, the bronze flight has gathered fragments of Azeroth's history: ancient dwarven structures, a watchtower from Lordaeron, chieftain quarters from the orcish clans, and armor from the first kings of Stromgarde. Some travelers have slipped past the sentinels to see these wonders. The inner gateways stay shut until the flight decides mortal intervention is needed.

subzone:cenarion-hold.text: Cenarion Hold. Cenarion Hold watches over the ancient dangers beneath Silithus. The Cenarion Circle keeps its druids in this desert stronghold, guarding what lies buried under the sands. In southern Silithus, Cenarion Hold directs the Cenarion Circle's work. You reach it by winding past Un'Goro Crater. Raised after the War of the Shifting Sands, the fortress watches over dormant threats sealed beneath the desert. Silithus is harsh country, home to silithid and arid storms. The hold gives shelter, trade, and supplies to night elf and tauren druids who keep watch over those buried dangers. Cenarion Hold stays neutral because guarding the world from ancient evils matters beyond mortal quarrels. Alliance and Horde travelers may enter, and quartermasters and wardens welcome them despite precarious supply lines. Flight routes link the hold with outposts in Feralas, Tanaris, and Un'Goro Crater. It is the desert's only staging ground for adventurers investigating the unrest there.

subzone:chamber-of-atonement.text: Chamber of Atonement. Captured undead and accused heretics face interrogation and torture in the Chamber of Atonement. At the entrance to the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing, the hall opens onto the cloister where the Scarlet Crusade casts their remains. The Chamber of Atonement opens onto the Forlorn Cloister, where no peace or prayer waits. The Scarlet Crusade has filled this grand entry hall with racks, shackles, and burning braziers. Zealous inquisitors use them to force confessions and torment captives. They believe unholy beings deserve pain as penance, while cries echo and cruel taskmasters keep watch. Interrogator Vishas oversees the chamber. He takes pride in breaking anyone caught crossing the monastery's boundaries. The Forsaken captive Vorrel Sengutz has endured weeks of torment at his hands. Here, the Scarlet Crusade's campaign for purity has turned to sadism.

subzone:chillwind-camp.text:
Chillwind Camp. At the southern pass, Chillwind Camp holds the Alliance line against the Scourge. Alliance soldiers and the Argent Dawn strike nearby strongholds and plague cauldrons from this outpost, before the blighted ruins of Lordaeron. Chillwind Camp guards the pass from Chillwind Point into the Western Plaguelands. It is the Alliance's first line of defense and its main base for pressing into the region. High mountain ridges keep the worst corruption at a distance, though the north's dead chill hangs over the tents and palisades.

Commander Ashlam Valorfist leads a small garrison of soldiers, scouts, and Argent Dawn specialists. They contain horrors along the King's Road and gather intelligence to reclaim Lordaeron's fallen fields. Without armies to assault Andorhal or Scholomance, Chillwind Camp depends on independent champions and mercenaries. Its forces strike the Cult of the Damned, disable plague cauldrons poisoning the soil, and keep supply routes open to eastern outposts such as Light's Hope Chapel. Scourge-held ruins lie just north, while the Forsaken fortify the western border. The defenders fight to keep the pass from being overwhelmed.

subzone:chillwind-point.text: Chillwind Point. At Chillwind Point, cold drafts sweep a rocky rise above the mountain pass. Ancient troll ruins stand where Hillsbrad Foothills, the Alterac Mountains, and the Western Plaguelands meet, and Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives among the stones. Chillwind Point looks down over a ravine at Hillsbrad's edge. The pass leads into the Western Plaguelands, with the Alterac Mountains rising nearby. Long before Lordaeron claimed these routes, ancient trolls raised stone structures on the heights. Their weather-beaten remains still face the elements. Cold winds now blow south through the ravine, carrying the north's chill into the foothills below. Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives among the old stones at Chillwind Point. The jungle troll hermit communes with the violent gales coursing through the gap. Though the heights are bleak and exposed, and Scourge-ravaged lands lie nearby, his camp is not entirely deserted. Travelers and shamans heading north often seek him out to learn the secrets of the mountain currents.

subzone:circle-of-aquementas.text: Circle of Aquementas. Travelers come to Tanaris’s eastern shore to summon Aquementas at the Circle of Aquementas. South of Lost Rigger Cove, the Circle of Aquementas stands where Tanaris’s eastern shore meets the desert. Weathered stones rise beside the sea in a ring. Travelers gather here to call Aquementas, an elemental spirit linked to an ancient artifact. Southsea brigands and sea creatures roam the nearby beaches, but the stones mark a place for summoning.

subzone:circle-of-east-binding.text: Circle of East Binding. In eastern Arathi, water elementals guard the Circle of East Binding, southwest of Hammerfall. At its heart, the Stone of East Binding draws fierce contest. East of Stromgarde, the Circle of East Binding lies among Arathi's rugged highlands. The Stone of East Binding rises at its center, charged with elemental magic. Cresting exiles roam the ground around it. These swirling water elementals fiercely defend the stone from any mortal who approaches. Ancient stones across Arathi bind volatile elemental forces. Around the eastern circle, restless water spirits show the strain on those wards. Drawn to the stone's magic or trapped by it, they lash out at travelers on the nearby road to Hammerfall.

subzone:circle-of-inner-binding.text:
Circle of Inner Binding. Beneath the Arathi Highlands, the Circle of Inner Binding holds Myzrael beneath ancient stones. The Stone of Inner Binding anchors the strongest ward, but cracks let the imprisoned princess reach out to wanderers. South of the main road, towering slabs ring the Stone of Inner Binding on a plateau. The stone thrums with the strongest ward beneath Arathi and its dense geo-magical power. Rumbling Exiles patrol the stones, drawn by the site's resonance or bound there as guardians.

Cracks in the inner seal let the imprisoned Myzrael reach out telepathically. She whispers pleas for freedom to unsuspecting wanderers who handle shards of her stone.

subzone:circle-of-west-binding.text: Circle of West Binding. Near Thoradin's Wall, Burning Exiles overrun the Circle of West Binding and guard its stone. The ancient ritual site is one of several scattered across the Arathi Highlands. Near Thoradin's Wall, the Stone of West Binding stands at the Circle of West Binding. The site belongs to a wider network of ancient ritual places scattered across the Arathi Highlands. Burning Exiles overrun the grounds and guard the stone. Their fiery presence makes an approach perilous for travelers crossing the western plains.

subzone:clockwerk-run.text:
Clockwerk Run. In Gnomeregan, toxic fumes and irradiated troggs choke Clockwerk Run between the Train Depot and the Hall of Gears. Clockwerk Run carries you from the outer Train Depot into Gnomeregan. Once, gnomish traffic and supplies passed through this corridor. Then High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered radioactive waste vented to stop the trogg invasion. The waste turned the passage into a deadly trap.

The blast and the fighting that followed brought parts of the hallway down. Toxic fumes and irradiated troggs now block the way to the upper Hall of Gears.

subzone:corin-s-crossing.text: Corin's Crossing. The Scourge has overrun Corin's Crossing, where ruined streets mark an old meeting place in south-central Eastern Plaguelands. Once travelers passed through on their way between Stratholme, Tyr's Hand, Darrowshire, and Andorhal. Now horrors haunt the town hall and forge, and unseen watchers drift among the ruins. Before the Third War, Corin's Crossing joined the roads of eastern Lordaeron. Merchants, couriers, and pilgrims stopped at this waystation between Stratholme and the southern strongholds. The settlement stood between Lake Mereldar and the place now blighted as the Infectis Scar. When the plague swept through the province, the undead vanguard reached the town. Corin's Crossing soon fell beneath its assault. The Scourge holds Corin's Crossing now, and wandering undead crowd its muddy streets. Rotting hulks and ghouls linger in the hollowed blacksmith shop and town hall. Scouts face another danger among the ruins. Unseen Servants drift beyond ordinary sight, pierce mundane stealth, and ambush anyone trying to slip past the main horde undetected.

subzone:corrahn-s-dagger.text: Corrahn's Dagger. Syndicate cutthroats hold Corrahn's Dagger, the second ridge among northern Hillsbrad's four rocky fingers. From its heights, they watch the valley and keep a hideout. In northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Corrahn's Dagger is the second of four rocky ridges called the fingers of Hillsbrad. Syndicate cutthroats overrun the ridge and use its high ground to watch the valley below.

subzone:crown-guard-tower.text: Crown Guard Tower. In the southern Eastern Plaguelands, blight surrounds Crown Guard Tower's ruins. The Scourge destroyed it during the invasion of Lordaeron in the Third War. Crown Guard Tower once watched over eastern Lordaeron as part of the Kingdom's defenses. When the Scourge overran the kingdom, they destroyed the tower and left it in ruins. Several fallen towers lie scattered across what are now the Eastern Plaguelands. Charred stones remain here in a land still held by the undead.

subzone:crusader-s-armory.text: Crusader's Armory. Munitions fill the Crusader's Armory in the Scarlet Monastery. Narrow halls hold gunpowder and cannonballs for the zealots guarding the way inward. A locked iron door bars the path to the Hall of Champions. Between the Footman's Armory and the Hall of Champions, narrow stone corridors hold crates of gunpowder and stacks of cannonballs. Armed crusaders stand ready to turn back intruders. The Scarlet Crusade has made a fortress of a former monastic compound, filling every available hall with the tools of war. A heavy iron door, locked with the Scarlet Key, bars the way into the inner chambers.

subzone:crypt-badlands.text: Crypt (Badlands). In the Badlands hills, an armored skeleton sits enthroned in a hidden tomb. Urns, chests, and an ancient sword lie beside the silent remains. Southeast of Hammertoe's Digsite, an unmarked path climbs the hillside to the Crypt. Below, an armored skeleton sits on a stone throne in dark chambers. Beside the remains lies the Sword of the Barbarian King, among bones, urns, and forgotten chests. Miners and travelers search nearby gullies for dwarven ruins and riches, while the seated ruler's origins remain lost to the Badlands.

subzone:crypt-stromgarde-keep.text:
Crypt (Stromgarde Keep). In Stromgarde Keep, loyalists guard the royal crypt beneath the Sanctum. It holds King Thoras Trollbane’s tomb and the treasures of his line. Beneath Stromgarde Keep’s Sanctum lies King Thoras Trollbane’s tomb. He led Stromgarde through the Second War. The city is in ruins, divided between Syndicate rogues and Boulderfist ogres, yet the surviving Stromgarde militia still holds this quarter.

Prince Galen Trollbane watches over the crypt with the royal caretakers. They keep his father’s body and legacy safe from scavengers and enemies outside. The crypt guards artifacts of the Trollbane line. Among them is Trol'kalar, an ancient runed greatsword forged centuries ago to slay trolls. Sworn caretakers, including Alaric, Nevlin, and Weston, protect the chamber and its treasures with powerful safeguards.

Galen and his loyalists keep watch. Rival factions and hostile trolls across Arathi covet the blade’s ancient power.

subzone:crystal-shore.text: Crystal Shore. Crystal Shore faces the South Seas along Stranglethorn's southeastern coast. Its beach lies south of the Ruins of Aboraz and across the water from Jaguero Isle. At Stranglethorn Vale's southeastern edge, jungle meets the South Seas along Crystal Shore. Steep ridges divide the beach from the inland wilds of Mistvale Valley, though a couple of rugged passes cross them. The crumbling troll structures of the Ruins of Aboraz stand to the north, while the Wild Shore follows the cape's southern curves. Far from Booty Bay's docks, this coast remains quiet and windswept.

subzone:crystal-vale.text: Crystal Vale. In northwestern Silithus, Crystal Vale gathers stone, wind, and ancient power. Jagged spires rise above rocky flats where earth and air elementals roam among rich ore veins. Potent summoning magic here is tied to the ancient elemental lords. Crystal Vale cuts a rocky basin into southern Silithus. Steep cliffs frame shimmering mineral formations, earthen elementals, and roaring whirlwinds of living air. Rich thorium draws a few prospectors, though the valley remains dangerous. Hostile elementals guard ground shaped by the primal conflicts of ancient Azeroth.

subzone:crystalvein-mine.text:
Crystalvein Mine. In central Stranglethorn Vale, prospectors risk the basilisks of Crystalvein Mine for its Singing Crystals. The cavern lies near the ancient ruins of Zul'Mamwe, and the creatures inside have overrun the site and turned miners to stone. Near Zul'Mamwe, Crystalvein Mine cuts into the jungle hills. Its Singing Crystals fetch a high price in southern trade ports, so the Venture Company came to work the valuable veins.

The mine's native basilisks have made that work perilous. They eat the strange crystals, which harden their scales and make them unnaturally lethal. Petrified trolls and humans outside the cave mouth mark the failure of the Venture Company's expeditions.

subzone:dabyrie-s-farmstead.text: Dabyrie's Farmstead. In northern Arathi, the Dabyries keep their farm against the dangers around them. Kenata Dabyrie holds fast with her sons, loyal to Stromgarde and the Alliance in a realm broken by the Third War. Kenata Dabyrie and her sons hold their farm against the dangers around them. Fardel and Marcel work the fields while a local family militia guards the grounds. Few human homesteads still endure in the broken kingdom of Stromgarde. Aggressive wildlife and bandits threaten the farm, and the Forsaken press from the north. The Dabyries keep their home in a land where few human settlements remain.

subzone:dalaran.text:
Dalaran. On Lordamere Lake, Dalaran's surviving magi are rebuilding their shattered city. Once the shining capital of the Kirin Tor, it fell to the Scourge and Archimonde during the Third War. Its protective violet shield has been removed. Dalaran began as a sanctuary for arcane study, founded by sorcerers of the Arathorian Empire after the ancient Troll Wars. For centuries, it was humanity's foremost center of magic. The Council of Six led the Kirin Tor, keeping vast archives and powerful artifacts in the Violet Citadel.

That age ended during the Third War. The traitor prince Arthas led the Scourge through the city gates to seize the Book of Medivh. Soon after, the demon lord Archimonde crushed Dalaran's soaring spires into rubble. After the Legion's defeat, the Kirin Tor's surviving wizards returned to their devastated homeland. They would not yield their ancestral ground to the Scourge or scavengers, and raised a shimmering violet barrier over the city's heart. The shield has since been removed, while rebuilding continues. The magi are restoring their fallen sanctuary, and Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver can be found in the Violet Citadel.

subzone:dalson-s-tears.text: Dalson's Tears. At Dalson's Tears, a Scourge cauldron poisons the fields of the Western Plaguelands. Once Dalson's Orchard, this farm became a Scourge staging ground during the Third War. Its former owners still haunt the fields and outbuildings. Dalson's Tears was once Dalson's Orchard, a productive farm in Lordaeron's breadbasket. Decay now chokes the fields, while a great iron cauldron at their center sends green plague vapors across the land. Cauldron Lord Malvinious oversees it. Blighted zombies, rotting cadavers, and skeletal horrors guard the device in the Lich King's service.

subzone:dandred-s-fold.text: Dandred's Fold. Syndicate outlaws hold Dandred's Fold on Lordamere Lake's northwestern shore. The farmstead and manor shelter Lord Aliden Perenolde and his co-conspirators. The Horde and Alliance watch the estate for different reasons. On the western edge of the Uplands, Dandred's Fold stands beside Lordamere Lake, apart from the surrounding country. The estate was once tranquil and may have belonged to an Alteraci noble named Dandred. After Alterac fell, the Syndicate turned it into a fortified refuge. Its assassins and enforcers patrol the grounds. They keep Southshore authorities and the Forsaken across the lake from the fallen nobility sheltered within.

subzone:dark-portal.text:
Dark Portal. At the Blasted Lands' southern rim, the dormant Dark Portal holds a rift between worlds. Its opening brought the Old Horde into Azeroth and began the First War. Where the Black Morass once spread across the south, the Dark Portal tore open. Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, joined his Tirisfal magics with Gul'dan's fel sorcery on Draenor. Their ritual drained countless lives and ripped reality apart. The Old Horde anchored the rift with massive stonework, then marched through to shatter the Kingdom of Stormwind in the First War.

Fel power from the portal poisoned the land. Lush marshes became the red, petrified wastes you see today. After the Alliance of Lordaeron won the Second War, Archmage Khadgar shattered the portal's stone frame with powerful magic. He hoped to sever Draenor from Azeroth forever, but the tear beneath it proved impossible to destroy. The Alliance built Nethergarde Keep nearby to watch the scar.

Demons and remnants of the Shadow Council still creep through the blasted caldera. The gateway has been reassembled, yet remains dormant. It is a silent wound between worlds that neither side dares abandon.

subzone:darkmist-cavern.text:
Darkmist Cavern. Darkmist spiders swarm the old mine in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh. Ruined shacks stand by its entrance, and locals still dispute whether cave or brood bore the name first. Rotting shacks stand outside Darkmist Cavern in northwestern Dustwallow Marsh. Thick webs choke the tunnels. People once came here for the mine, but no human presence remains. Now Darkmist spiders fill its passages. Their size and venom make them deadly to unwary wanderers.

Marsh dwellers still dispute how the cavern got its name. Some say it was named for the brood nesting inside. Others say the spiders took their name from the misty cave. Even this web choked cavern draws scavengers. The hermit ‘Swamp Eye’ Jarl sends travelers deep into its webs to gather the eyes of monstrous spiders. He claims they make fine broth. Most sensible travelers keep clear of the web strewn entrance.

subzone:darkwhisper-gorge.text:
Darkwhisper Gorge. Demons hold Darkwhisper Gorge in the southern heights of Winterspring. They fled there after Archimonde fell and now guard its minerals and planar relics. In Winterspring's southern heights, demons have made Darkwhisper Gorge their refuge. After Archimonde fell atop Mount Hyjal, the survivors scattered into the mountain ranges. A disciplined vanguard settled here and made the border a stronghold.

Hederine demons lead the foothold under Lady Hederine. Manastalkers, slayers, and initiates defend the tunnels and fiery camps. At the gorge's lowest point, a sealed archway hints at passages higher into the sacred mountain. Danger has not kept adventurers and opportunists from the gorge's wealth. Its ravines hold truesilver and dense thorium deposits. In the shadowed grottos, the imp vendor Vi'el sells fel-tainted reagents such as felcloth and gromsblood.

The elusive high elf Earthcaller Franzahl holds ancient metallurgical lore about smelting rare elementium.

subzone:darnassus.text:
Darnassus. In Teldrassil’s high boughs, Darnassus shelters the kaldorei as their capital and refuge. Its tranquil groves and waters are the night elves’ spiritual heart and the Alliance’s chief stronghold in northern Kalimdor. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Fandral Staghelm guide their people through the trials of newfound mortality. Darnassus took shape after the Third War, honoring the night elves’ survival after they lost the immortality granted by their sacred World Tree, Nordrassil. Unlike the stone cities of Ironforge and Stormwind, this is an open, tranquil settlement of wood-crafted lodges, glowing shrines, and arched bridges over clear lakes. Vigilant Sentinels, towering ancients of war, and druids who shape trees watch the paths and keep nature’s quiet within the city. Darnassus speaks of kaldorei unity, though its leaders bear different duties. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind handles civil and military affairs from the radiant Temple of the Moon, with the Sisters of Elune around her. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle’s affairs and championed the planting of Teldrassil to restore the elves’ lost immortality.

Malfurion Stormrage is missing, lost in a mysterious slumber within the Emerald Dream. Staghelm’s aggressive vision for the future often clashes with the more patient priesthood.

subzone:darrow-hill.text:
Darrow Hill. In northern Hillsbrad, Darrow Hill's rugged grassland rises beneath the Headland. Mountain lions and stags cross its open slopes, while feral yetis haunt the Foothill Caverns. Alterac Granite draws travelers into this dangerous frontier. Below the Headland, Darrow Hill's rocky slopes join southern Hillsbrad's rolling pasture to Alterac's colder, jagged heights. Mountain lions and stags move through the tall grass, while towering yetis emerge from the Foothill Caverns.

The cavern walls hold dense Alterac Granite, drawing quarry workers, miners, and adventurers into danger. Regional claims remain contentious, and travelers of either faction may be caught unaware on the trails.

subzone:darrowmere-lake.text:
Darrowmere Lake. At the heart of the Western Plaguelands, Darrowmere Lake surrounds Caer Darrow. The island fortress holds ruined halls above Scholomance, the Cult of the Damned's academy of necromancy. Darrowmere Lake is among the largest inland waters in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Thondroril and Darrowmere rivers feed its deep waters, beneath the blighted forests of Lordaeron. During the Second War, the Horde and Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet fought naval skirmishes here.

The Horde sacked Caer Darrow on the central island and carried away its ancient runestone. Once, the thriving House of Barov sent trade across the lake. Now a grim basin lies veiled in mist at the heart of the Plaguelands. Caer Darrow rises from the center of Darrowmere Lake. It was once the proud ancestral seat of the Barov family. Beneath its broken foundations lies Scholomance, the Scourge's chief academy of necromancy and dark arts. The waters around the island are stagnant, reflecting the Cult of the Damned's dark legacy. To reach the fortress at the lake's heart, you must cross those waters through the dangers of the blighted countryside.

subzone:darrowshire.text:
Darrowshire. Darrowshire lies in ruins in the southern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a peaceful hamlet of Lordaeron, it made a desperate stand against the Scourge during the Third War. Shattered timbers, restless spirits, and bitter memories remain. Darrowshire's villagers fought the Scourge during the Third War. Before plague consumed northern Lordaeron, the humble settlement stood beneath the southern cliffs. Marduk Blackpool, a death knight, and Horgus the Ravager, a ghoul lord, led the besieging force.

The villagers and local defenders held the line for a time, though the odds were impossible. Then their defense broke, and the Scourge slaughtered the town down to the last soul. Many fallen defenders were raised as ghouls to swell the Scourge's ranks. Darrowshire remains an empty memorial to those who died there. Darrowshire's ruins still bear the weight of the slaughter. The living abandoned the village long ago, but spectral remnants of its townspeople remain trapped there. Travelers report strange sights, including ghostly reenactments of the battle unfolding in silence. Sorrow still clings to the ground, a reminder of what the Scourge took from the kingdom.

subzone:deadman-s-crossing.text:
Deadman's Crossing. At Deadman's Crossing, travelers still follow the packed road beneath a tree hung with the dead. The junction in Deadwind Pass links Duskwood, the Swamp of Sorrows, and the track to Karazhan, carrying travelers across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Deadman's Crossing joins the roads through eastern Deadwind Pass. The western road runs toward Duskwood and the eastern road toward the Swamp of Sorrows. South, a track climbs toward Karazhan. At the fork stands a twisted hangman's tree, its branches bearing two rotting corpses.

Battered wooden signs warn travelers to turn back and abandon hope. Hostile beasts and dark sorceries haunt the canyon, yet the packed dirt road through the crossing remains clear. Travelers who keep to it avoid the blighted rocks.

subzone:deadmines.text:
Deadmines. Beneath ruined Moonbrook, the Deadmines lie quiet, though rumors speak of danger in their forgotten shafts. Once the greatest gold producer in human lands, the mines fell silent during the First War. Gold once poured from the Deadmines, the richest mines in human lands. Whitestone oak supplied their timber and supports. When the orcish Horde pushed north, the miners fled in haste.

During the First War, Sir Anduin Lothar entered the treacherous depths to recover the sacred Tome of Divinity. Subterranean ogres held him captive for twenty months before rescuers freed him. After the kingdom fell, the shafts went quiet, and people came to say they were cursed.

subzone:deadwood-village.text:
Deadwood Village. In southern Felwood, Deadwood Village's furbolgs defend their rough wooden homes from all who approach. Once peaceful and close to nature, they fell to the demonic corruption that blighted the forest. Near Felwood's southern border, the Deadwood tribe gathers in its village. When demonic energies swept through the ancient woodlands, the furbolgs could not resist the creeping rot. Fel malice warped their minds, and they abandoned their traditions and harmony with nature.

Now brutes, shamans, and den watchers defend their polluted grounds against intruders. Their violence brings despair to their uncorrupted cousins, the Timbermaw.

subzone:den-of-flame.text: Den of Flame. Black dragonkin hold the Den of Flame in western Dustwallow Marsh, west of the Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul ogres raised it as their mound, but Onyxia’s brood has driven them out. Black dragonspawn patrol the burning edge of the Den of Flame and guard its cavern entrance. The Stonemaul ogres built the rough stone stronghold as their main mound and sanctuary. Then the black dragonflight laid waste to the clan’s settlement. The brood scattered the ogres and seized the mound, where dragonspawn now keep watch beneath the shadow of Onyxia’s nearby lair.

subzone:dire-maul.text: Dire Maul. In Feralas, Dire Maul's broken halls and coliseums are divided among rival powers. Once called Eldre'Thalas, the ancient Highborne city guarded Queen Azshara's arcane secrets. Gordok ogres, invading satyrs, and withered elven caretakers now divide its crumbling plazas. Eldre'Thalas sheltered Queen Azshara's favored sorcerers, the Shen'dralar. When the Well of Eternity collapsed in the Great Sundering, Prince Tortheldrin raised a magical barrier that saved the city. Cut off from their source of magic, the surviving Highborne trapped the colossal demon Immol'thar beneath their sanctum. For millennia, they drew on its fel essence to preserve their immortality and arcane power.

subzone:direforge-hill.text: Direforge Hill. Hostile Dark Iron dwarves hold Direforge Hill in the northeastern Wetlands, southeast of Dun Modr and northeast of the Green Belt. Balgaras the Foul commands the Dark Iron dwarves on Direforge Hill. Their encampment lies southeast of Dun Modr, in the northeastern Wetlands. Travelers crossing the northeastern Wetlands must pass near the hostile Dark Iron encampment on Direforge Hill. Balgaras the Foul commands the dwarves there.

subzone:dragonmaw-gates.text: Dragonmaw Gates. At the Dragonmaw Gates, heavy fortifications bar the road climbing from the eastern Wetlands. They guard the ascent to Grim Batol, a mountain fortress among cursed dwarven ruins. The Dragonmaw Gates seal the winding road through rugged peaks in the eastern Wetlands. The Dragonmaw orcs held Grim Batol during the Second War, and the gates bear their name. The road remains fortified, but the climb is still dangerous. Powerful drakes haunt the pass, and grim reminders of the clan’s dark history linger in the mountains. The Dragonmaw orcs were broken and scattered after the Demon Soul was destroyed. Yet the mountain path remains dangerous. Powerful red dragons have been seen watching the winding slopes and perches around the gates. Monstrous drakes and Dragonmaw remnants still lurk in the nearby hills, while the gates bar travelers bold enough to venture into the heights.

subzone:dragonmurk.text: Dragonmurk. In southern Dustwallow Marsh, black dragonspawn and hatchlings swarm Dragonmurk. Ancient ogre ruins and scorched caverns flank this dangerous tract, held by Onyxia's brood. In southern Dustwallow Marsh, wet paths and thick mud teem with black wyrmkins, dragonspawn, and hungry whelps. The black dragonflight holds the land around Dragonmurk. Stonemaul, a ruined village, and the scorched Den of Flame both lie under its control.

subzone:dreadmaul-post.text: Dreadmaul Post. Ogres hold Dreadmaul Post near the Dark Portal. The Dreadmaul clan raised this fortified settlement in the Blasted Lands after crossing from Draenor. Travelers face the ogres and the harsh wastes around their camp. The Dreadmaul clan crossed into Azeroth with the Horde decades ago. Near the Dark Portal, they raised rough stone mounds and earthworks in the Blasted Lands’ red wastes. Dreadmaul Post is one of their chief outposts. From here, the ogres hold the badlands and clash with wandering beasts and travelers who approach their territory.

subzone:dreadmaul-rock.text:
Dreadmaul Rock. Firegut ogres make their home among the caves and earthen mounds of Dreadmaul Rock in the Burning Steppes. Above the scorched plains of the Burning Steppes, Firegut ogres hold the crags and caves of Dreadmaul Rock. The massive stone formation is cut through by a labyrinthine cave system. Though its name suggests a possible tie to the Dreadmaul ogres of the Blasted Lands, the Firegut clan controls the rock.

They use its high paths, crags, and interior earthen mounds as a defended camp. From there, they dominate the surrounding wasteland and menace anyone crossing the northern slopes toward Blackrock Spire.

subzone:dreadmurk-shore.text: Dreadmurk Shore. Fog and Mirefin murlocs endanger travelers on Dreadmurk Shore, between Theramore Isle and the Barrens. Sea beasts prowl the water, making this coast a dangerous passage through Dustwallow Marsh. At Dustwallow Marsh’s northeastern edge, muddy shoals, tide pools, and misty islands lie between Theramore Isle and Northwatch Hold. The Mirefin tribe holds this coast. These territorial murlocs attack travelers who come near their villages. Sea turtles and other aquatic predators patrol the shallows, while the swamplands bring danger from inland.

subzone:dream-bough.text: Dream Bough. On an island in northern Feralas, green dragons guard Dream Bough. The ancient Great Tree shelters a gateway into the Emerald Dream. Dream Bough rises above the forest on an island in Jademir Lake. It is the largest tree in northern Feralas. A natural portal opens in its trunk and leads straight into the untamed Emerald Dream. The Green Dragonflight guards Dream Bough and the gateway in its trunk. Dragonkin and drakes patrol the lake’s banks and the approaches to the great tree. Druids come to contemplate and sleep as they pass between realms. Few uninvited travelers are tolerated near this threshold, so approach with care.

subzone:drowned-reef.text: Drowned Reef. Ships bound for Faldir's Cove risk the Drowned Reef off Arathi's southern coast. Ancient ruins lie below, where Daggerspine naga seem able to command the bay's tides. Beyond the hidden entrance to Faldir's Cove, shattered ships rest beneath the waves. The Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine lie among them. Daggerspine naga dwell on the reef under Prince Nazjak's command. They seem able to command the bay's tides, and crews seeking shelter in the cove may be doomed by them. Deep beneath the reef lie the ruins of an ancient elven city. Dive among the drowned buildings, and calcified elven gems can still be found among the remains.

subzone:drowned-sacellum.text: Drowned Sacellum. At Blackfathom Deeps' entrance, the Drowned Sacellum lies beneath the coast. Murlocs and makrura now haunt its broken stones amid brackish pools and cavern roots. You pass Blackfathom Deeps' threshold into the Drowned Sacellum. Once a quiet place of worship to Elune, the chapel has long lain collapsed beneath Ashenvale's coast. Brackish pools cover its ancient marble flagstones. Starfish cling beneath great roots in the cavern ceiling, while dark wisps flicker through the gloom. Follow the broken stone path with care, and it leads deeper into the temple complex toward the Pool of Ask'ar. Night elf caretakers left the Drowned Sacellum long ago. Now shoreline scavengers hold the ruins. Aggressive murlocs and heavily armored makrura share the murky waters, attacking anyone who disturbs their nesting grounds. Darker cultic threats lie deeper in the temple. These predators guard the first stretch of the underground ruins.

subzone:drywhisker-gorge.text: Drywhisker Gorge. Northeast of Hammerfall, Drywhisker kobolds hold a gorge in the eastern mountains of the Arathi Highlands. They guard its inner cavern, rich mineral deposits and ancient elemental relics buried underground. Drywhisker kobolds hold the crags east of Hammerfall. Their clan has dug deep into the mountains and fiercely guards its winding passages. Below, they mine veins of Lesser Bloodstone Ore. Their stronghold lies close enough to trouble the orcs at Hammerfall.

subzone:dun-mandarr.text: Dun Mandarr. In southeastern Winterspring, enraged moonkin guard the abandoned dwarven camp of Dun Mandarr. Dun Mandarr lies in Winterspring’s frozen southeastern reaches. Jaron Stoneshaper made his camp there, and uncovered the Blue-Feathered Amulet. The discovery roused the native wildkin to fury. They swept down on the camp and drove the dwarves away. Now moonkin prowl the broken shelters and guard the cavern. No friendly souls remain among the snowbanks.

subzone:dunemaul-compound.text: Dunemaul Compound. At the western edge of Tanaris, Dunemaul ogres gather around their central settlement. The clan’s mound and cave network lie among rocky ridges. In western Tanaris, Dunemaul ogres guard their stronghold from travelers crossing the dunes. The harsh arid climate has taught the clan to survive through brute force and opportunism. Their settlement gathers around an ogre mound and a network of caves. Warriors and enforcers patrol beside twisted spellcasters who wield dark warlock and mage magic. The ogres violently reject uninvited guests.

subzone:dustbowl.text:
Dustbowl. In the Badlands, travelers cross the Dustbowl between Kargath and the Valley of Fangs. Its dry gullies and open ground are roamed by coyotes, buzzards, and rock elementals. Camp Wurg marks the Dustbowl in the northwestern Badlands. Dry gulches cut through cracked clay, and harsh winds sweep grit across the open flatland. Cacti and scattered, gnarled trees cling to the barren soil.

Coyotes prowl, buzzards circle overhead, and living rock elementals wander the rugged earth. Without a guide, crossing this wilderness is perilous. Camp Wurg offers a landmark amid the scrub, between Kargath and the Valley of Fangs.

subzone:dustfire-valley.text: Dustfire Valley. At Searing Gorge’s northern edge, Dustfire Valley ends at the locked gate of Stonewrought Pass and the road to Loch Modan. Ash lies across the rock in Dustfire Valley, where bare canyon walls rise around you. At its northern end, a locked dwarven gate seals Stonewrought Pass. The doors bar direct travel to the Valley of Kings and Loch Modan, leaving the valley a dead end amid Searing Gorge’s sulfurous wastes.

subzone:dustwallow-bay.text: Dustwallow Bay. Vessels thread the shallow waters of Dustwallow Bay on their way to Theramore Isle. The inlet lies between Dustwallow Marsh and the island, with coves and shoals far from eastern Kalimdor’s main sea routes. At Dustwallow Marsh, murky wetlands meet the Great Sea. Theramore Isle lies to the east, and ships cross the bay to reach Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s island haven. Vessels come and go from its docks, though the coast remains wild and dangerous. Rocky outcrops, murloc encampments, and hidden inlets such as Tidefury Cove line the shore. Beyond the marsh’s crocolisks and hostile beasts, the islands and inlets offer quiet waters and rich catches. Small islets near Tidefury Cove draw anglers seeking solitude. Nat Pagle, the famed fisherman, often casts from the rocks, away from Theramore’s crowds.

subzone:eastern-strand.text: Eastern Strand. Daggerspine naga hold the Eastern Strand along Hillsbrad's southeastern coast. Its beaches and shallows reach toward the Arathi Highlands border. Daggerspine naga dominate the Eastern Strand on Hillsbrad's southeastern edge. Across the bay lies the Western Strand. Southshore and Tarren Mill clash over the region's human farms, while the naga dominate these sandy flats and tidelines. They come from the Great Sea, crossing the sandbars and settling among rocky outcrops. From there, they watch the mainland.

subzone:eastmoon-ruins.text: Eastmoon Ruins. Dunemaul ogres occupy Eastmoon Ruins, west of the Gaping Chasm in eastern Tanaris. Their camp stands among the remains of an ancient troll site. West of the Gaping Chasm, old troll stones rise from Tanaris’s desert sands. Their pillars and plazas have crumbled with age. Now Dunemaul ogres shelter among the broken walls and watch the nearby trade routes.

subzone:eastwall-gate.text: Eastwall Gate. At Stratholme’s eastern wall, Eastwall Gate offers a way into the ruined city. It lies in northern Eastern Plaguelands, apart from the chaos at the main gates. Eastwall Gate cuts through Stratholme’s eastern fortifications. The main entrance opens onto King’s Square, but this barred passage leads to Elders’ Square near the steps of Alonsus Chapel. From there, you can enter the city’s depths without passing the front barricades or the undead lines. Heavy ironwork seals Eastwall Gate. The Key to the City, found inside Stratholme, opens it, and an infiltrator skilled enough can pick its masterwork locks. A mechanical lever on the inner wall raises the portcullis so allies can follow.

subzone:eastwall-tower.text:
Eastwall Tower. On the eastern road, Eastwall Tower watches over a wilderness still infested with Scourge. Built as a scout tower for Lordaeron, it fell when the Scourge swept across the kingdom during the Third War. Eastwall Tower's broken ramparts look down on roads through Scourge-infested countryside. Built to guard Lordaeron's border, it watched travelers bound for the far reaches of the realm. When the Scourge invaded during the Third War, the outpost fell with the settlements around it. Shattered stone arches and burnt timber remain.

The Lich King's armies still infest the region. From its high ground, the ruined tower overlooks the eastern roads.

subzone:eldreth-row.text: Eldreth Row. Gordunni ogres patrol Eldreth Row, the ruined western halls of Dire Maul. Overgrown stone once marked the outer threshold of ancient Eldre'Thalas. Eldreth Row opens onto the outer halls of ancient Eldre'Thalas. The avenue lies before the deeper quarters and the Broken Commons. Centuries of neglect have cracked the stone, and Feralas plants overrun its colonnades. The Highborne halls now serve the Gordunni ogres as a staging ground. Their patrols guard the paths east toward the Warpwood Quarter and west past the Dire Pool.

subzone:emerald-sanctuary.text: Emerald Sanctuary. At Felwood’s southern entrance, druids gather at Emerald Sanctuary to study the demonic taint and heal the woods. At Felwood’s southern edge, Emerald Sanctuary is the Cenarion Circle’s base in the blighted woods. Night elven and tauren druids work side by side here, setting aside the factional conflicts spreading across Kalimdor to restore the land. Researchers track corrupted flora and study Jaedenar, seeking a way to cleanse the poisoned soil.

subzone:ethel-rethor.text: Ethel Rethor. Along Desolace's northwestern coast, Ethel Rethor's drowned halls lie beneath the sea. A sealed tower rises above the waves, while naga hold the sunken settlement. Ethel Rethor's broken stones line the coast of western Kalimdor. Before the Great Sundering, a night elven settlement stood here, but much of it has since fallen beneath the sea. Shattered foundations lie under the waves, and one weathered tower rises from the surf. A small bridge reaches its sealed portal, still closed against the elements and intruders. Naga now hold the drowned chambers and nearby shallows, making these waters dangerous to approach. Travelers come to Ethel Rethor to study Kalimdor's forgotten history and watch its dangers today. Near the ruins, Azore Aldamort serves the Argent Dawn. He watches the naga and offers aid to those willing to dive into the sunken passages. The waters offshore are dangerous, and barren wastes stretch inland. So the ruins remain a lonely meeting place on the coast.

subzone:everlook.text:
Everlook. Everlook shelters travelers at the meeting of Winterspring’s routes. The Steamwheedle Cartel keeps this northern outpost open to merchants, prospectors, and researchers, offering a neutral refuge from the high-altitude cold. At Winterspring’s crossroads, Everlook is the Steamwheedle Cartel’s northernmost outpost. Like Gadgetzan and Booty Bay, it is a walled settlement beneath permafrost. Alliance and Horde travelers find warmth and shelter here because the town keeps strict neutrality. Its bank and shared auction house are the region’s only operational ones. Hired bruisers guard the settlement, where travelers seek refuge from ferocious frostsabers and yetis. Everlook’s icy wooden roofs and whimsical penguin wallpaper shelter workshops for engineering and advanced alchemical laboratories. Goblin tinkerers pursue their craft away from prying eyes.

The Argent Dawn recently sent Gregor Greystone to negotiate with town leadership. The order watches the region’s ancient ruins and gathering northern threats with care.

subzone:faldir-s-cove.text: Faldir's Cove. Blackwater Raiders now shelter at Faldir's Cove after disaster struck their fleet on the Arathi coast. The harbor also recalls the early settlers who sailed south from here to found Stormwind. South of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove lies behind the bluffs, reached through a hidden tunnel beneath the ground. The harbor bears the name of Faldir, an ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition sailed across the Great Sea to establish Stormwind. Now Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay shelter in its waters. Captains Steelgut and O'Breen led them north in search of ancient elven treasures, but their expedition became trapped in the bay. The Blackwater expedition met disaster on the Arathi coast. Unnatural tides, stirred by territorial naga on the offshore Drowned Reef, shattered two of their three ships. Only the Harbinger reached Faldir's Cove intact. With naga prowling the waters and their navigation charts lost beneath the waves, the surviving pirates and gnomish researchers are stranded. They rely on travelers to fight the aquatic horrors and recover salvage from the seabed.

subzone:fallow-sanctuary.text:
Fallow Sanctuary. In the Swamp of Sorrows, Fallow Sanctuary shelters a tribe cut off from the world they knew. The Lost Ones are mutated draenei, driven feral by grief and homesickness. Among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Lost Ones have made Fallow Sanctuary their refuge. Separation from their ancestral world and dark energies deformed them.

Sorrow and isolation wore away at the tribe’s sanity. Now they are hostile and feral, attacking outsiders who enter their village. Ongeku and Noboru the Cudgel once guided Fallow Sanctuary. Their absence and deaths left the village without its leaders.

subzone:feathermoon-stronghold.text:
Feathermoon Stronghold. Sentinels watch southern Kalimdor from feathermoon stronghold, on sardor isle off Feralas. General Shandris Feathermoon commands the night elves along the Forgotten Coast. Across the channel from Feralas, feathermoon stronghold guards the Sentinels’ southern base on sardor isle. Ancient elven groves surround the fortress, and a sacred moonwell lies within its grounds. Archers, huntresses, and support staff serve under General Shandris Feathermoon. From the island, the night elves watch Feralas and guard against demonic corruption, dangerous wildlife, and Horde expeditions. Feralas’s mainland holds savage beasts, Gordunni ogres, and the tainted shadows of Dire Maul. Sardor Isle gives the stronghold a defensive buffer. Alliance travelers cross from the Forgotten Coast by ferry to its fortified docks, where they can repair their gear and gather intelligence.

General Shandris Feathermoon leads the Sentinels and is the trusted right hand of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Under her command, the stronghold holds against the enemies of the kaldorei.

subzone:feathermoon-stronghold-classic.text: Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). On Sardor Isle, Feathermoon Stronghold guards Feralas's western shore. General Shandris Feathermoon established it as the Alliance's main staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Feathermoon Stronghold guards Sardor Isle, just off the Forgotten Coast.
