General Shandris Feathermoon built the fortress to carry Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Tyrande Whisperwind has trusted Shandris as her lieutenant for ten thousand years. The island shields the stronghold from beasts, ogres, and Horde forces crossing mainland Feralas. Boats and hippogryphs link Feathermoon Stronghold to the mainland and distant Alliance hubs. A passenger boat crosses the channel between Sardor Isle and the Forgotten Coast dock. For longer journeys, a hippogryph roost connects the stronghold with Thalanaar on the Thousand Needles border, Nijel's Point in the Desolace highlands, and Auberdine in the north.

subzone:felpaw-village.text: Felpaw Village. At Felpaw Village, corrupted furbolgs guard Felwood’s northern path to Timbermaw Hold. Demonic blight has turned the settlement against all outsiders. Corrupted Deadwood furbolgs hold Felwood’s northern edge at Felpaw Village. Once gentle wardens of the forest, they fell to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War and became feral. Crude huts and ritual totems fill their blighted enclave. Near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold, hostile warriors attack anyone who comes close. At Felwood’s northern mouth, Timbermaw guards watch over the few uncorrupted furbolgs left in the region. They mourn their fallen cousins, yet keep their guard. The Deadwood threaten the passage to Timbermaw Hold and could carry corruption through its gates into Moonglade and Winterspring. So the guards call on travelers to thin their ranks and seize their ritual fetishes.

subzone:felstone-field.text: Felstone Field. Scourge corruption has claimed Felstone Field in the northwestern Western Plaguelands. Once farmland for Lordaeron, it now lies in ruins beneath a plague cauldron that sends toxic fumes into the air. Felstone Field once fed Lordaeron from a peaceful family farm. When plague swept through the north, the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge quickly seized the homestead. Dead weeds and rot cover the fields now. At the farm’s heart, an enormous plague cauldron churns foul vapors into the sky. Cauldron Lord Bilemaw guards it with skeletal flayers, sorcerers, and ravenous ghouls.

subzone:feral-scar-vale.text: Feral Scar Vale. In western Feralas, Feral Scar yetis hold a rocky gorge deep in the High Wilderness. Their caves lie beyond the forest trails, where travelers face danger. Primal Feral Scar yetis guard the caves of Feral Scar Vale in the High Wilderness. Unlike the yetis of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these brutes have adapted to Feralas's humid wilds. They defend their cave network fiercely and keep bone trophies. Intruders are driven from their hunting grounds. Gnomish distress signals have sometimes led into the deeper caves of Feral Scar Vale. Lost devices have become trapped there among the yetis, including robotic survey chickens. They wait to be activated and recovered.

subzone:fire-plume-ridge.text: Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge burns at Un'Goro Crater's heart. Its magma warms the basin and feeds the geysers and steam pools. Fire elementals roam its slopes. Lava runs down Fire Plume Ridge into Un'Goro Crater's jungle basin. Beneath the rock, magma channels spread under the soil and feed the geysers and hot springs. The heat is fierce, so travelers climbing the ridge need water and shade. Fire elementals roam the glowing lava flows, drawn by the deep heat below the ridge. Blazerunner dwells in a cavern near the summit and rules Un'Goro's elementals. Those who climb toward the peak face scorching heat and spirits defending their fiery home.

subzone:firewatch-ridge.text: Firewatch Ridge. Dark Iron dwarves hold Firewatch Ridge above the Cauldron in northern Searing Gorge. Their sentries, golems, and fire spiders guard the bluff, while the Twilight's Hammer holds caves to the northwest. From Firewatch Ridge, you look down on the Cauldron's industrial devastation. Dark Iron guards, engineers, and molten golems patrol the crags, defending their foothold beside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. The height lets the Dark Irons watch the ash plains and spot incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood early. The Twilight's Hammer holds a cave network in the ridge's northwestern reaches. Its cultists work in the Dark Iron camp's shadow, performing dark rituals below the rock, where powerful elite zealots keep watch. The caves lie near both the Dark Iron works and Blackrock Mountain. Elemental and apocalyptic cults meet in Searing Gorge's fiery heart.

subzone:flame-crest.text: Flame Crest. Flame Crest watches the volcanic wastes from a rocky ledge in the Burning Steppes. The neutral camp shelters scouts, beast collectors, and strategists, while wind riders carry travelers across the Redridge range and beyond. Flame Crest clings to a stone ledge above the ash and lava plains. You cross a narrow wooden bridge to reach the camp. Its height helps keep prowling beasts and roaming orc warbands at bay. Wind riders carry travelers across the Redridge range to Kargath, Stonard, Thorium Point, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades. Scouts at Flame Crest watch the Blackrock clan entrenched in Blackrock Spire. They gather intelligence and plan how to break the renegade Dark Horde. The camp also trades with eccentric loners, including Kibler, a pet master who lives in a nearby cave.

subzone:foothold-citadel.text: Foothold Citadel. At Foothold Citadel, Theramore's guards prepare to defend the island. The fortress holds the Alliance command and barracks on Theramore Isle, overlooking the settlement. Foothold Citadel holds the Alliance defense within Theramore Isle's stone walls. Captain Garran Vimes and Commander Samaul lead the Theramore Guard from its halls. Field medics, logistics officers and quartermasters work beside them. Guards patrol and drill, preparing Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces for threats from the surrounding swamplands. Foothold Citadel recalls the early days of Theramore. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore seized the city to wage his personal crusade against the Horde, and the fortress became the place of his final stand. Thrall's allied force broke through the citadel under Rexxar, a half-ogre warrior, and struck down the Admiral. The fortress has been repaired, though the bloody conflict is remembered.

subzone:forgotten-coast.text: Forgotten Coast. Sea giants and water elementals roam Feralas’s western shore, where the Forgotten Coast meets the Veiled Sea. The rainforest ends at the Forgotten Coast, and the Veiled Sea opens beyond it. With no canopy overhead, the strand lies exposed to wind and weather. Sea giants tower over the shore while water elementals prowl the surf. Travelers crossing the forest must pass these ancient guardians to reach the water. A ferry carries them from the mainland to sardor isle, home of the night elven feathermoon stronghold.

subzone:forgotten-pool.text:
Forgotten Pool. Beyond the Moonshrine Ruins, Forgotten Pool lies beneath Blackfathom Deeps. Monstrous deep-sea predators haunt its dark waters. Dive through the sunken waterways beyond the Moonshrine Ruins to reach Forgotten Pool. Dark water fills this isolated cavern, cut off from dry ground.

Nearby, Twilight's Hammer cultists chant and naga patrol the flooded halls. The pool lies apart from them. Old Serra'kis, an ancient aquatic terror, lairs hidden in its depths.

subzone:forlorn-cloister.text:
Forlorn Cloister. Among the tombs of Forlorn Cloister, the fallen dead rise, and Scarlet Crusaders burn their bodies to stop them. You enter a graveyard where Scarlet Crusaders hurry between tombs with torches. They burn their fallen brothers, but the plague has already tainted the earth beneath them.

Once, priests and paladins of Lordaeron laid their honoured dead here in peace. Now spectres drift between the crypts, and corpses claw their way from the graves. The Crusaders keep watch, yet dark magic deep in the grounds still calls the dead to rise. Bloodmage Thalnos commands the dead within the cloister. A skeletal sorcerer, he is another of the Monastery's tragedies, lost to undeath and hungry for vengeance. With dark magic, he binds the souls of the deceased and slaughters anyone who enters his blighted graveyard.

subzone:forlorn-ridge.text:
Forlorn Ridge. Alliance and Horde positions line the slopes of Forlorn Ridge in southwestern Azshara. The ridge rises above the coast. Forlorn Ridge rises above western Azshara, shaped like an ancient volcano long quiet. From its heights, you can see the coast and the ruined elven estates below.

The ridge commands this stretch of land, so Alliance and Horde forces have built encampments and outposts along its rugged slopes. They watch each other across the bluffs.

subzone:frayfeather-highlands.text: Frayfeather Highlands. In Feralas, Frayfeather hippogryphs defend their ancestral roosts. Scavengers and naturalists brave the flocks in search of intact eggs. Wild hippogryphs raise their broods on steep slopes and crags above Feralas's forest floor. The flocks defend their scattered nests among the rock shelves with fierce aggression. Their mastery of the rugged cliffs draws outsiders to the nesting grounds. Goblin entrepreneurs in distant Gadgetzan seek unhatched eggs for study and profit.

subzone:frostfire-hot-springs.text: Frostfire Hot Springs. Steam rises from Frostfire Hot Springs beneath the snow of western Winterspring. Curious scholars and hardy fishers come despite the cold, while hostile furbolgs keep near the pools. Near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold, warm water runs beneath the snow at Frostfire Hot Springs. No one knows what keeps it hot. Winterfall furbolgs roam the banks, and their aggression makes the pools dangerous to approach. Fishers who brave the furbolgs and the winter chill find rare open water where fish thrive. The springs draw curious observers who wonder how their waters stay hot in this frozen land. Donova Snowden, an inquisitive dwarf, keeps a lonely vigil nearby as she studies their origin and composition. She suspects the heat may not be natural. Dark magic from the demonic stronghold of Darkwhisper Gorge could be seeping north and stirring the waters underground.

subzone:frostsaber-rock.text: Frostsaber Rock. Frostsabers find shelter and training at Frostsaber Rock in northern Winterspring. Its stone rise overlooks the region’s snowy reaches. Frostsaber Rock rises over Winterspring’s frozen northern wilds. Frostsabers prowl its slopes and valleys. At the summit, Rivern Frostwind, a solitary night elf, raises and tends the cats. Alliance champions who brave the harsh conditions and prove their devotion may earn the rare privilege of learning to raise, tame, and ride one of these snowy mounts.

subzone:frostwhisper-gorge.text: Frostwhisper Gorge. In southern Winterspring, Frostwhisper Gorge runs just north of Darkwhisper Gorge. Ancient night elven ruins lie across its icy floor and cliffs, now held by Frostmaul giants. A lone dwarf camp overlooks the ocean from the eastern rim. Frostwhisper Gorge cuts through Winterspring's southern mountains, just north of Darkwhisper Gorge. Snow covers the ravine floor and cliff ridges, where stonework from ancient night elven settlements remains. Frostmaul giants and their preservers claim the gorge now. They fiercely defend its frozen crags, making travel into the ravine perilous. A narrow, quiet track leads to a small outpost atop the gorge's eastern cliffs. Travelers flying by wyvern or gryphon between Azshara, Orgrimmar, and Winterspring may spot it from above. An Ironforge banner marks the solitary dwarven camp at the cliff's edge. Crates of provisions, barrels of ale, a comfortable chair, and a rifle leaning against its rest sit there. The camp overlooks the drop to the Great Sea below.

subzone:fungal-rock.text: Fungal Rock. At Un'Goro Crater's northeastern cliff, gorillas make their den in Fungal Rock. Ghost Mushrooms grow in its damp passages, among the crater's most dangerous ape dens. A waterfall and pool mark Fungal Rock's entrance on Un'Goro Crater's northeastern edge. Massive gorillas make their den in the damp underground corridors. Un'Goro Stompers and Thunderers move among Ghost Mushrooms there. Deep inside, the silverback U'cha and the albino gorilla Uhk'loc hold their territory. Near the cave mouth, a curious traveler may find A-Me 01, a damaged mechanical ape abandoned by gnome researchers.

subzone:fungal-vale.text: Fungal Vale. In Fungal Vale, Scourge horrors roam beneath a murky haze, and Cult of the Damned acolytes serve among the fungi. The vale lies in south-central Eastern Plaguelands, north of Crown Guard Tower and Marris Stead. North of Marris Stead, Fungal Vale lies among Lordaeron’s most corrupted places. Sickly purple earth swells with alien fungi beneath a haze of necrotic spores. The Plague of Undeath has warped the soil, raising unholy growths that feed carrion beasts and shambling undead. Members of the Cult of the Damned tend the blighted blooms and perform foul rites amid the decay.

subzone:gadgetzan.text:
Gadgetzan. Trade brings both factions to Gadgetzan, where the Steamwheedle Cartel keeps the peace. Anyone may enter, provided they bring coin or work to offer. Amid Tanaris's scorching sands, Gadgetzan is the Steamwheedle Cartel's base for trade in southern Kalimdor. Goblin ingenuity gives its buildings a haphazard shape. Within them are an auction house, a bank, an inn, and workshops for engineers, blacksmiths, and alchemists.

Flight masters carry travelers of both factions toward Tanaris, Feralas, and the basin of Un'Goro. Commerce rules here. Keep your weapons sheathed and your purse open, and the goblins will let you pass in peace. Goblin bruisers keep order in Gadgetzan. They pummel anyone who threatens trade or starts a faction brawl. Beyond the gates, the Gadgetzan Water Company struggles against Wastewander bandits at Waterspring Field. Water is precious in Tanaris, so the cartel hires mercenaries to defeat the bandit leaders and recover water pouches. The town's reservoirs depend on that supply.

subzone:gahrron-s-withering.text: Gahrron's Withering. At Gahrron's Withering, the Scourge foul an old Lordaeron farm beside the road to the Eastern Plaguelands. A massive cauldron sends plague vapors into the air. Before the Third War, this farm fed Lordaeron with grain. Then the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge swept across the land, and the fields fell silent. Now the farmstead is broken and derelict. Haunting visions, wailing wraiths, and restless spirits roam its ruined outbuildings under Scourge overseers sworn to the Lich King.

subzone:gallery-of-treasures.text:
Gallery of Treasures. In the Scarlet Monastery, the Gallery of Treasures joins the Huntsman's Cloister to the Athenaeum. The Scarlet Crusade guards a corridor of Lordaeron's paintings, relics, and illuminated texts as it wages war against the undead. Deep in the Library wing, the Gallery of Treasures runs from the Huntsman's Cloister kennels to the Athenaeum archives. Paintings and historical artifacts line the corridor. Small chambers hold books salvaged from across fallen Lordaeron.

The Scarlet Crusade calls these relics humanity's untainted legacy and has sworn to protect that heritage. Its zealots guard the passage against outsiders who enter their sanctuary.

subzone:gaping-chasm.text: Gaping Chasm. In southeastern Tanaris, the Gaping Chasm opens into a Hazzali silithid hive. Its tunnels spread beneath the desert and reveal how far the brood has reached beyond the western sands. The Gaping Chasm cuts through Tanaris, where tunnels wind among mounds of resin. Beneath the desert, the Hazzali silithid burrow in an aggressive brood. Stingers, swarmers, and hulking sandreavers hunt anyone who descends, traveler or treasure-hunter. The tunnels may trap them in sticky cocoons. As the hive grew, Gadgetzan grew concerned. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser sent junior surveyor Scrimshank into the pit to map and measure the geological shifts caused by the insect tunnels. The expedition ended in disaster. Scrimshank died among the chittering broods, leaving scattered gear and measuring instruments as a warning against underestimating the silithid.

subzone:garrison-armory.text: Garrison Armory. Alliance miners work the Garrison Armory southwest of Nethergarde Keep. Their ore supplies the fortress and brings wealth to Stormwind. Nethergarde Keep must hold its watch over the Dark Portal, and long supply trains from Stormwind cannot meet every need. In the Garrison Armory’s underground mine shafts, miners work under foremen with engineers at their side. Ore mined there goes to Nethergarde’s smiths and fortifications, or travels to Stormwind in trade for food, tools, and other provisions the keep needs. The Garrison Armory lies beyond Nethergarde Keep’s main walls, exposed to the red desert’s dangers. Dreadmaul ogres and wild beasts prowl the surrounding crags. Armed guards protect the workers in the tunnels, for any disruption to the mine threatens the keep’s watch over the blasted frontier.

subzone:gelkis-village.text:
Gelkis Village. In southwestern Desolace, the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan holds its village and guards the southern route. Their ravine overlooks the north-south road, making passage perilous for travelers without the clan’s favor. Gelkis Village fills a deep gorge between steep bluffs and rope bridges. The Gelkis have made their ancestral grounds a lasting fortress, with outposts reaching toward the Feralas border. Khan Shaka leads the warriors from Bolgan's Hole, a cavern in the southern cliff face.

Travelers heading south through Desolace must fight through the gorge or tread carefully. The Gelkis consider uninvited wanderers fair game in their endless war with rival centaur clans.

subzone:ghost-walker-post.text:
Ghost Walker Post. In central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post holds its ground beside the Kodo Graveyard. Tauren and orcs defend the Horde outpost from centaur clans and the Burning Blade, while its shamans tend dying kodos and their spirits. Ghost Walker Post gives the Horde a foothold on central Desolace’s dusty flats. Centaur marauders and Burning Blade cultists roam nearby, keeping the post in danger. Its facilities offer only the bare essentials. There is no inn or flight master. Tauren guards and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep watch over the badlands. Gurda Wildmane, a tauren shaman, leads Ghost Walker Post beside the Kodo Graveyard. Shamans tend the dying kodos who come there to perish. They ease the beasts into the next life and commune with their lingering spirits.

The post’s defenders stay ready against threats. Here, the tauren honor their ancient bond with the mighty kodo.

subzone:gnomeregan.text:
Gnomeregan. Troggs and leper gnomes roam Gnomeregan’s poisoned halls among the broken defenses. The city was once the gnomes’ underground capital, until a desperate defense ended in catastrophe. Gnomeregan’s halls once rang with the work of gnomish engineers. Ironforge dwarves helped build the city centuries ago, carving it into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh. Steam-driven gears, copper pipes, and vast assembly halls made it the heart of gnomish industry and invention. During the Second War, its designs, flying machines, and complex weapons supplied the Alliance. Even Orgrim Doomhammer’s Horde could not break the city during its siege. During the Third War, troggs surged up from deep underground and broke into Gnomeregan’s lowest chambers. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque chose to face the invasion alone, unwilling to draw Alliance armies away from the slaughter in Lordaeron.

On the advice of chief engineer Mekgineer Thermaplugg, he ordered radioactive gas released through the lower chambers to wipe out the troggs. Instead, the gas empowered many troggs and killed nearly eighty percent of the gnomish people. Survivors exposed to it became twisted leper gnomes, and Thermaplugg took control of the poisoned ruins.

subzone:go-shek-farm.text: Go'Shek Farm. Go'Shek Farm gathers food and livestock for Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Forsaken apothecaries also work there in secret. South of Hammerfall, Go'Shek Farm lies just north of hostile Witherbark troll territory. The Horde holds the farm, and Hammerfall Grunts patrol its fields and stables. Its food and livestock help the orcish settlement keep its foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

subzone:golakka-hot-springs.text: Golakka Hot Springs. In western Un'Goro Crater, Golakka Hot Springs send geysers skyward north of Terror Run. Fire Plume Ridge's heat draws researchers and alchemists to the steaming pools. Golakka Hot Springs bubble north of Terror Run in western Un'Goro Crater. Heat from Fire Plume Ridge drives scalding water up through the ground. It leaves mineral terraces, and geysers break across the basin. Steaming Furies prowl the pools where groundwater meets volcanic heat. Explorers, herbalists, and researchers still come to study the crater's unusual geology. Alchemists prize Golakka's spring water as a strong catalyst. They use it even in delicate concoctions such as love potions. Spark Nilminer, a curious visitor, perches atop the central geyser vent. Researcher Krakle comes to study how the springs reach into the crater's volcanic heart.

subzone:gordok-commons.text: Gordok Commons. In the Gordok Commons, King Gordok rules the Gordunni’s northern stronghold in Dire Maul. The Gordok Commons fill an old aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas. The ogres have remade its night elven pillars and arched passages for their own needs. Armories, crude barricades, and training grounds crowd the halls. Here the Gordok train, the fiercest and most disciplined fighters in the Gordunni clan. At the far end, King Gordok holds court at Gordok's Seat and rules through force and fear. Among the Gordunni, might decides who rules. By clan tradition, whoever slays the sitting monarch takes the title of King Gordok and wins the obedience of the surviving captains and guards. A challenger may slip past the king's lieutenants through stealth or guile. If the challenger kills only the king, the guards accept the victor's authority and bring lavish tributes instead of avenging their former ruler.

subzone:gordunni-outpost.text:
Gordunni Outpost. North of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni ogres hold a fortified camp in the cliffs. Their presence leaves the surrounding wilderness dry and withered. Above Lariss Pavilion, Gordunni ogres patrol trails cut into Feralas's northern mountains. Their magic and destructive ways drain life from the wild. Plants die, and the hillsides lie bare.

Dirt paths lead to a shallow cave entrance and a larger mound burrowed into the rear cliffs. Hillguards, channelers, and tamers guard the camp. Near the deeper den, they keep Bigfist, a captured sasquatch, in crude confinement.

subzone:green-belt.text: Green Belt. In eastern Wetlands, Green Belt lies below the ridges of Grim Batol. Bog beasts, crocolisks, and toxic oozes roam the marsh, while Rethiel the Greenwarden keeps watch alone. In eastern Wetlands, Green Belt’s mossy waters make travel hazardous. Massive crocolisks, shifting oozes, and shambling bog beasts roam the fen. Deep within, Rethiel the Greenwarden mans a solitary watch post. The night elf studies the fen’s ecology and keeps its hostile creatures in check. Wreckage from a Dragonmaw clan caravan lies scattered in the muck. It was left after the catastrophic battle at nearby Grim Batol. Crimson whelplings linger around the broken carts and crushed cages, reminders of the clan’s past enslavement of Alexstrasza and her red dragon brood.

subzone:grimesilt-dig-site.text: Grimesilt Dig Site. Dark Iron sentries patrol the Grimesilt Dig Site in the Searing Gorge. Ironforge's search for relics began here, and its surviving crew struggles to endure in hiding. Dark Iron sentries patrol the Grimesilt Dig Site in the Searing Gorge. Ironforge scholars first sent an expedition beneath the crags to seek relics. The native Dark Iron dwarves drove the excavators out and seized their equipment. Wounded and scattered, the original crew remains trapped in and around the pit.

subzone:grimtotem-compound.text:
Grimtotem Compound. In central Feralas, the Grimtotem keep two encampments east of Dire Maul. Their compound is a base for mysterious, destructive operations in the region. East of Dire Maul, two Grimtotem encampments give the clan a foothold in Feralas. Unlike the tauren who follow Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, they act alone and meet outsiders with hostility.

In the southern half, captive native sprite darters are held in a large wooden cage for reasons of their own. Rogue gnolls stalk the northern perimeter.

subzone:grom-gol-base-camp.text: Grom'gol Base Camp. Grom'gol Base Camp holds the Horde's western coast position in Stranglethorn Vale. Commander Aggro'gosh leads the fortified outpost in northern Stranglethorn, with zeppelins linking the camp to Orgrimmar and the Undercity. Jungle trolls and hostile Alliance forces threaten the camp. In northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, Commander Aggro'gosh holds Grom'gol Base Camp. Palisades and armed grunts guard against Bloodscalp headhunters, lurking naga, and prowling beasts. The camp keeps supply routes north to Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows open. Its sentries watch Alliance traffic coming down from Duskwood or up from Booty Bay. Wooden zeppelin towers make Grom'gol a key supply hub in the Eastern Kingdoms. Goblin skycraft fly regular routes from the camp to Orgrimmar and the Undercity. This airbridge brings Horde reinforcements and supplies straight into Stranglethorn, away from Alliance-held highways and the deep sea.

subzone:growless-cave.text:
Growless Cave. Mountain yetis roam Growless Cave in the Alterac Mountains, while its Flame of Uzel keeps Helcular's dark purpose close. Mountain yetis roam Growless Cave in the crags above Alterac's foothills. Travelers avoid its entrance on the treacherous slopes, especially when Skhowl, a notorious yeti, prowls outside. Yet the beasts are not the cave's only danger.

Within stands the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left by the human mage Helcular. Before his death, Helcular meant to use the pyre in a dark ritual to become a lich. Its foul warmth once drew Frostmaw, a massive predator, from the frozen wastes.

subzone:gurubashi-arena.text:
Gurubashi Arena. In southern Stranglethorn Vale, pirates and wandering brawlers gather at Gurubashi Arena. Fighters clash over locked chests of treasure in its ancient stone ring. Before humans or orcs came to Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi troll empire raised the Gurubashi Arena, also called the Great Arena. It honored their martial strength. In ancient days, champions fought to the death on its sands, until troll blood slicked the earth. The Gurubashi Empire has fractured into warring tribes, yet bloodshed still comes to the arena floor. Now lawless buccaneers and ruffians gather for another spectacle. Short John Mithril, a pirate, oversees the grounds.

Every few hours, a chest of plundered booty is hauled to the ring's center. Anyone who steps onto the floor becomes fair game. Faction allegiances fall away, and every combatant must fight all comers to reach the prize.

subzone:haldarr-encampment.text: Haldarr Encampment. In western Azshara, Haldarr satyrs hold a corrupted outpost northeast of Shadowsong Shrine and southwest of Valormok. Their camp blights ancient elven ruins, and the injured Night Elf Sentinel Keldara Sunblade lies among them. Broken stones mark the Haldarr satyrs’ camp in western Azshara. These twisted creatures descend from the Highborne and were cursed by demonic corruption during the Sundering. They hunt and harass anyone crossing the autumn forests. Their crowded settlement threatens the Horde forces at nearby Valormok and the dwindling Night Elf sentinels watching the region.

subzone:hall-of-arms-tyr-s-hand.text: Hall of Arms (Tyr's Hand). Scarlet fighters hold the Hall of Arms in Tyr's Hand, deep in the southeastern Plaguelands. This wing of Tyr's Hand Abbey houses the crusade's martial vanguard, across the abbey from its library. Scarlet fighters keep watch in the Hall of Arms, south of Tyr's Hand Abbey's main hall. Their armory and quarters fill this wing, while archives and holy texts are kept opposite. The defenders wear heavy armor and swear to destroy the undead and anyone they judge impure. As horrors surround them in the Plaguelands, they guard the abbey and keep their weapons and shields ready.

subzone:hall-of-champions.text:
Hall of Champions. Within the Scarlet Monastery's armory wing, the Hall of Champions tests the Crusade's elite. Herod, the Scarlet Champion, leads its fiercest fighters from this inner sanctum. Beyond the Footman's Armory, you come to the Hall of Champions at the heart of the monastery's armory wing. Herod, the Scarlet Champion, commands the Crusade's fiercest fighters here.

Scarlet trainees sharpen their resolve and skill for the Crusade's aim: to purge Lordaeron of all undead and outsiders.

subzone:hall-of-masks.text: Hall of Masks. In the Hall of Masks, carved skulls loom over a bone-choked trench beneath the Swamp of Sorrows. The chamber marks a threshold to deeper passages in the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Past the staircase from the Broken Hall, you reach a central junction in the Sunken Temple. Stylized skull masks line its stone walls. A deep trench choked with discarded bones cuts across the floor, though its purpose remains unknown. From here, passages lead to the Butchery, the Chamber of Blood, and the Den of the Caller.

subzone:hammerfall.text:
Hammerfall. Horde forces hold Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, where old losses and a hard-won freedom shape the outpost. Orcs and Forsaken defend it against Boulderfist ogres, Witherbark trolls, and the League of Arathor. Beneath Hammerfall lie the ruins of an Alliance internment camp. After the Second War, the human Alliance built vast camps across Lordaeron for defeated orcs, and this was among the largest. Years later, Thrall and Orgrim Doomhammer struck at the camp to free its lethargic captives.

As they retreated, an Alliance knight charged and drove a lance through Doomhammer's backplate. The Warchief was mortally wounded. After the Third War, the new Horde reclaimed the ruins and named its outpost Hammerfall in his memory. Hammerfall gives the Horde a foothold in Arathi. Its garrison faces aggressive Boulderfist ogres from Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall, as well as the native Witherbark trolls. Forsaken Defilers use the outpost to claim resources in the contested Arathi Basin. There they oppose the Alliance's League of Arathor.

subzone:harborage.text: Harborage. At the northern edge of the Swamp of Sorrows, Harborage shelters exiled Draenor natives who have kept their minds. They seek peace by the water in a harsh wilderness. At the foot of the northern mountains, you find Harborage, a small camp apart from the feral tribes in the nearby waters. Leather shelters and hanging crystals mark this refuge for exiled survivors from Draenor who have kept their minds. Elders like Magtoor guide the community. Together, they watch the wilderness, its native predators, and the feral tribes of their fallen brothers beyond the camp.

subzone:hearthglen.text:
Hearthglen. In the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands, Hearthglen holds firm. Its walls survived Lordaeron's fall, and the Scarlet Crusade now uses the settlement and its farmlands as a northern stronghold and training ground. Hearthglen still looks like a living town of Lordaeron, while nearby Andorhal lies in skeletal ruin. Its lumber mill, scout towers, stables, and working mine are still here. Lord Tirion Fordring once governed from Mardenholde Keep. During the Second War, Hearthglen prospered and stood staunchly defended.

When the Plague of Undeath swept Lordaeron during the Third War, Prince Arthas Menethil intercepted tainted grain here. He purged the infected townsfolk and joined Uther the Lightbringer to repel a massive Scourge siege. Hearthglen's formidable walls survived intact. After the kingdom's collapse, the Silver Hand fell into disarray. Tirion's son, Taelan Fordring, renounced the order and joined the Scarlet Crusade. Grief and zealotry soon consumed the fortress. Scarlet crusaders now patrol Hearthglen's approaches and man its ramparts. They execute any outsider, living or undead, who trespasses on their land.

Highlord Taelan Fordring rules from Mardenholde Keep. From there, he serves the Crusade's uncompromising war against the Plaguelands.

subzone:hetaera-s-clutch.text: Hetaera's Clutch. Hetaera's brood now nests among the drowned ruins beneath Azshara's Bay of Storms. Once, night elves came to this temple to worship Elune. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor apart, night elves came to this temple to worship Elune. The sanctuary sank beneath the Bay of Storms, where its pillars and halls have rested under the sea for ten thousand years. Now the tides cover every sign of worship, and the Kaldorei ruins lie below the waves. Hetaera makes her nest in the drowned sanctuary. The massive hydra has many heads and stalks the nearby coastal waters and rocky isles. Her offspring, the Spawn of Hetaera, prowl the ruined arches and corridors. They attack any surface-dweller bold enough to dive into the bay.

subzone:hidden-grove.text:
Hidden Grove. Wild moonkin now guard the Hidden Grove in northeastern Winterspring. Cliffs shelter the Hidden Grove from Winterspring’s bitter winds. Snow-dusted trees fill the sunken crater, nearly cut off from the world beyond. Its hidden rim is hard to reach. You must risk a steep drop or find a narrow cavern passage in the southeastern ridge.

White hares once lived undisturbed in the valley. Now aggressive wild moonkin have taken the glade, and unwary travelers may be ambushed there.

subzone:high-wilderness.text: High Wilderness. In western Feralas, the High Wilderness runs from the Verdantis River to the Forgotten Coast. Its towering trees shelter wildlife, wandering treants, and dangerous beasts. The High Wilderness spreads across western Feralas beneath trees so vast and foliage so thick that little sky shows through. Wolves, bears, hippogryphs, and yetis roam below. Ancient treants wander among the roots, while aggressive ogre clans hold shaded clearings. Brush hides predators and hazards from an earlier age, so travelers must stay alert.

subzone:hive-ashi.text: Hive'Ashi. Across northern Silithus, Hive'Ashi sends its silithid swarms through sand and tunnel. It is one of three great hives in the region, with workers, defenders, and stingers moving over towering mounds. In northern Silithus, Hive'Ashi's chitinous spires mark the ground claimed by a silithid swarm rising again. Workers forage while venomous defenders move south and east toward the Swarming Pillar. Beneath the mounds, dangerous tunnels shelter the colony. To learn what stirs in the desert, travelers must enter them. Cenarion scouts keep watch on Hive'Ashi. They send combatants to thin the swarm and bring back reports from deep in the colony. Glyphs and coordinated behavior found in Ashi suggest the insects share a single will, though they seem mindless. Their numbers are swelling, and those guarding the southern borders make destroying the brood a priority before it spreads beyond northern Silithus.

subzone:hive-regal.text: Hive'Regal. In southern Silithus, Hive'Regal's broods threaten the desert around one of its three great silithid colonies. Hive'Regal spreads across southern Silithus, where silithid gather in great numbers. Resin spires rise above deep tunnels. Within them, dangerous broods range from venomous spitfires and burrowers to predatory slavemakers. The hive guards its borders and harvests organic material from travelers who stray too close. Beneath Silithus's red sands, Hive'Regal's passages reach deep into the earth. Strange glyphs mark the entrance and far places within the tunnels. They suggest an organized intelligence directs the swarm, beyond mere feral instinct. Scholars and scouts study Hive'Regal and its sister hives for signs of a greater power stirring beneath the wastes.

subzone:hive-zora.text: Hive'Zora. Across western Silithus, Hive'Zora's silithid swarm spreads through the sands. It is one of three great hives in the desert, and its aggressive castes press outward. Stone spires rise from Hive'Zora's sands in western Silithus. Porous mounds mark entrances to deep tunnels carved by silithid burrowers. Waywatchers and reavers patrol the perimeter. Below, tunnelers and hive sisters brood. The Cenarion Circle and other scouts watch as the silithid menace presses into this ancient frontier.

subzone:horizon-scout.text:
Horizon Scout. Off Azshara’s southern coast, Horizon Scout lies sunk in the Ruined Reaches. Captain Vanessa Beltis is stranded ashore, and part of her crew is trapped below the waves. Horizon Scout lies wrecked among the Ruined Reaches’ shoals off Azshara’s jagged coast. Captain Vanessa Beltis reached a nearby peninsula, but part of her crew went down with the hull. They still live because Roland Geardabbler, a gnome, sustains a spell of water breathing inside the wreck.

Hostile aquatic predators and predatory naga patrol the waters. The sailors are trapped in the forward compartments and cannot reach the surface alone. A shard of raw Azsharite lies in Horizon Scout’s forward stairwell. The mineral is mysterious and found only on these shores. Spitelash naga prowl the Ruined Reaches and likely struck the ship to seize artifacts or resources from its expedition.

The vessel sank, leaving its survivors unable to escape with any secrets or treasures the coast holds.

subzone:ice-thistle-hills.text: Ice Thistle Hills. Ice Thistle yetis menace travelers southeast of Everlook. Snow covers the high hills, where a rugged cavern cuts through the slopes. The yetis claim the area and threaten anyone who leaves the main road. At the heart of Ice Thistle Hills, a great cave cuts deep into the rock. Ice Thistle yetis hunt and make their nests there, roaming the rocky slopes and winding tunnels. Their territory lies near Everlook, putting goblin trade and visiting prospectors at risk. So travelers and traders hire hunters to cull the beasts for their thick pelts and pristine horns.

subzone:infectis-scar.text:
Infectis Scar. Near Corin's Crossing, the Infectis Scar remains open in the blighted earth of the Eastern Plaguelands. Necromantic power split the ground when a cursed runeblade broke against a dwarven shield, and blight still festers below. Near Corin's Crossing, a jagged chasm cuts through the Plaguelands. The Pestilent Scar began as natural terrain and was poisoned by plague, but this wound opened during the Third War. Death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a dwarf captain, and his cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield.

Marduk discarded the broken weapon but kept its hilt. The severed blade sank into the soil, and its foul enchantment tore open the earth. Blight still festers at the bottom of the scar.

subzone:ironforge.text:
Ironforge. Beneath Dun Morogh, Ironforge’s Great Forge still burns at the heart of dwarven rule and Alliance trade. Deep within Ironforge Mountain, the city anchors Khaz Modan and guards the Alliance. Ironforge fills the deep halls of Ironforge Mountain, with stone rings circling the Great Forge. Dwarves founded the city millennia ago, after awakening and migrating from Uldaman. It has endured ages of history, including the War of the Three Hammers, which left the Bronzebeard clan in sole control.

Natural magma pours through the mountain and powers the city. Massive stone gates guard its halls. Dwarven craftsmen and warriors share them with many exiled gnomes, who arrived after Gnomeregan fell recently. Ironforge is one of the Alliance’s busiest centers of commerce and industry. From the High Seat, King Magni Bronzebeard rules Khaz Modan. Dwarven prospectors, miners, and engineers work beside gnome refugees in Tinker Town.

Beneath the mountains, the Deeprun Tram runs to Stormwind City. It carries trade and troops at high speed, keeping the capitals linked in mutual defense.

subzone:ironstone-camp.text:
Ironstone Camp. At Ironstone Camp, Horde fighters now face the silithid swarm at Rustmaul Digsite. They came to drive out Alliance dwarven excavators, but the attack has changed their purpose. Ironstone Camp stands where Thousand Needles meets the western edge of the Shimmering Flats. Moktar Krin led the Horde fighters sent to drive Alliance dwarven excavators from nearby Rustmaul Digsite.

Then silithid burst from a cavern and overran the dig. They attacked both sides, so the surviving defenders now fight the swarm before it spreads across the region.

subzone:irontree-woods.text:
Irontree Woods. Across northern Felwood, Irontree Woods lies blighted by the scars of the Third War. Its ancient protectors stand petrified among twisted treants and elementals. Irontree Woods lies quiet beneath a demonic stain. During the Third War, the Burning Legion's taint choked life from the soil of this kaldorei glade. The guardian Ancients Hastat, Stoma, and Vartrus fell to dark magic and hardened into stone. Their lifeless forms remain among the corrupted brush.

Maddened treants, vile bog beasts, and tainted water elementals roam the twisted forest floor. They strike at travelers who come near.

subzone:isle-of-dread.text: Isle of Dread. South of Sardor Isle, sheer cliffs guard the Isle of Dread off Feralas’s southwestern coast. Chimaeroks roam its highlands, while naga hide in sea caves. A narrow path on the southeastern shore leads you into the island’s high valley. Two-headed chimaeroks roam this enclosed highland, strengthened by arcane energies. Lord Lakmaeran leads the beasts. Anyone crossing from Sardor Isle faces danger here. Hatecrest naga occupy caves along the island’s northern shore. Lord Shalzaru leads them as they plot against the night elven sentinels at nearby Feathermoon Stronghold. Submerged passages wind through the deep chambers to secluded grottoes. Their fortified lair stays beyond mainland scrutiny.

subzone:itharius-s-cave.text: Itharius's Cave. Green whelps roam the marsh around Itharius's Cave, where Itharius keeps watch. The cave lies among the far southwestern cliffs of the Swamp of Sorrows. Green whelps wander the mire outside Itharius's Cave in the southwestern Swamp of Sorrows. Itharius lives in the damp cavern, far from civilization. He appears to be a high elf, a people rarely found alone in these southern swamps. He keeps watch over the young dragonkin as they grow, sharing their remote home.

subzone:jadefire-run.text: Jadefire Run. Jadefire Run shelters Felwood’s strongest and most cunning satyrs in the north. Their fortified camp spreads demonic corruption through the tainted woods. In northern Felwood, Jadefire satyrs hold a stronghold among the blighted woods. Demonic structures shelter formidable spellcasters and tricksters, far stronger than those in the valley’s lesser outposts. The satyrs use dark sorcery and foul trickery against anyone who enters their territory. They seek to spread corruption farther across Kalimdor.

subzone:jaedenar.text: Jaedenar. Cultists and demons now hold Jaedenar, the Shadow Council’s chief base in northern Kalimdor. Blighted woodland covers ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens, with the Shadow Hold below. Night elf sacred grounds and barrow dens once filled these hollows. Druids slept in the dens while connected to the Emerald Dream. After the Third War, the Shadow Council claimed the valley and named it for the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Renegade orc and Forsaken warlocks gathered there with satyrs, succubi, and felguards. They hold the surface ruins and deeper barrow dens, turning sacred woodland into a center for demonic rites. Cultists gather at profane sites above ground, including the Shrine of the Deceiver. Braziers burn with fel flame, and rituals further corrupt the timberland. Below lies the entrance to the Shadow Hold, where the council's true masters direct their work across Felwood. The Emerald Sanctuary watches Jaedenar with concern. It regularly calls on daring wanderers to disrupt summoning circles and douse the dark flames sealing the tunnels.

subzone:jagged-reef.text:
Jagged Reef. Along Azshara’s northern coast, ships find no safe passage through Jagged Reef. Sandy beaches meet stone spurs and churning surf, where hydras, makrura, and murlocs prowl. Jagged Reef cuts along Azshara’s northern edge. Broken cliffs and jutting stones divide sandy shores into quiet inlets. Beneath the water, crags and shifting shallows make the passage deadly to ships.

On shore, hydras and makrura prowl the surf. Murlocs search the tides for scraps and unwary prey.

subzone:jaguero-isle.text:
Jaguero Isle. On Jaguero Isle, King Mukla rules the wild beasts. Fierce panthers and gorillas haunt its jungle off Stranglethorn Vale’s eastern coast. Jaguero Isle lies off Stranglethorn Vale’s southeastern coast, far from the mainland pirate camps and troll ruins. Untamed panthers and aggressive gorillas roam the island. King Mukla, a gigantic ape, rules the rocky interior and guards it fiercely.

Few sailors willingly approach the reefs. Bottles found along the mainland beaches sometimes carry desperate pleas for rescue from people stranded ashore.

subzone:janeiro-s-point.text: Janeiro's Point. Ships pass Janeiro's Point on their way into Booty Bay. Mok'rash the Cleaver claims the island's shores and waters. Ships bound for Booty Bay pass Janeiro's Point at the harbor's edge in southern Stranglethorn Vale. A colossal stone goblin spreads its arms atop the rocky crag, welcoming vessels to the bay. Sailors can see the statue for miles, yet Mok'rash the Cleaver claims the island. The sea giant makes landing on its shores perilous.

subzone:karazhan.text:
Karazhan. In Deadwind Pass, Karazhan's sealed tower stirs with dangerous magic. Once Medivh's home, it rises above a meeting of ley lines that twists time, space, and reality. Restless spirits haunt its halls, and dangers remain within. Karazhan rises from ground shaped like a human skull, above a vast meeting of mystical ley lines. Built long before the First War, it was Medivh's refuge and storehouse for his magical secrets. The Last Guardian of Tirisfal lived in its winding halls with his castellan, Moroes. He welcomed noble guests and gathered arcane books and relics said to surpass even the libraries of the Kirin Tor.

Yet these walls witnessed Azeroth's greatest betrayal. Possessed by the demon Sargeras, Medivh secretly arranged the opening of the Dark Portal. Anduin Lothar and Medivh's apprentice, Khadgar, killed the Guardian, and Karazhan's gates were sealed. The tower fell into decay, but its powerful ley lines still twist reality. Ghostly echoes, illusions, and distortions of time ripple across Deadwind Pass.

Rumors say an evil presence stirs again inside the quiet fortress. Strange beings are drawn to its silhouette. Among them are the shadowy Dark Riders, who search the surrounding lands for forgotten relics.

subzone:kargath.text: Kargath. In the western Badlands, Kargath guards the Horde's foothold. The Kargath Expeditionary Force built the outpost on Warchief Thrall's orders, linking Horde holdings and preparing operations near Uldaman and Blackrock Mountain. Kargath honors the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist. The outpost is the Horde's only settlement in Khaz Modan, surrounded by arid wastes, dangerous wildlife, and hostile dwarven factions. Its garrison gives travelers a refuge midway across the continent. From here, a flight master connects northern holdings such as the Undercity and Hammerfall with southern outposts such as Stonard and Grom'gol Base Camp. Warchief Thrall sent the Kargath Expeditionary Force to pursue two aims. Troops enter Uldaman's ancient titan halls to learn why Ironforge's Prospectors value the dig site so highly. Scouts also seek a route through the Searing Gorge into Blackrock Mountain. There they hope to strike Rend Blackhand's false 'Dark Horde' while facing the entrenched Dark Iron dwarves.

subzone:kodo-graveyard.text: Kodo Graveyard. In central Desolace, kodos make their way to Kodo Graveyard to die among their ancestors. Their bones cover a broad stretch of grey earth. Ancient bones lie across Kodo Graveyard, some from beasts far larger than any living kodo. When a kodo nears its end, it comes here to spend its last breaths among centuries of remains. Scavengers prowl the edges. Disturb the calcified ribs or skulls, and furious kodo spirits may rise from the dust. Restless spirits wander among Kodo Graveyard’s bones. Those who look into the spirit realm can see towering kodo apparitions moving silently through the dust storms. Nearby, the Horde keeps watch from Ghost Walker Post. They guard the sacred grounds and watch over the herds and spirits that linger among the bones.

subzone:kormek-s-hut.text:
Kormek's Hut. Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle make their home at Kormek's Hut in north-central Desolace. The ramshackle dwelling shelters Willow, a peaceful cultist, and Bibbly, a goblin intent on harvesting kodo bones. In north-central Desolace, you may find Willow and Bibbly F'utzbuckle at Kormek's Hut. The name belongs to someone whose identity and whereabouts remain unknown. Willow sits inside, a member of the usually hostile and nihilistic Twilight's Hammer, yet she welcomes outsiders calmly.

Outside, a pen strewn with sun-bleached kodo bones is Bibbly's dance floor and work site. The excitable goblin sees profit in gathering the bones.

subzone:kurzen-s-compound.text: Kurzen's Compound. Stormwind's expedition has turned against the kingdom at Kurzen's Compound in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Colonel Kurzen's madness has made it a camp of rogue soldiers and wild beasts. Colonel Kurzen's expedition came to Stranglethorn on Stormwind's orders. Then the colonel's madness changed its course, and the garrison broke from the kingdom to follow him. Now the compound is a mercenary stronghold. Its lumber mill and stables hold captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers trained for war. In the caves called the Stockpile, Kurzen's men keep their plundered supplies. Some of Kurzen's original soldiers refused to follow him into savagery. When madness took hold of the colonel, they mutinied and fled west. There they founded the Rebel Camp. A bitter, bloody feud followed beneath the jungle canopy. Kurzen and his loyal men hunt the deserters, and treat every outsider who enters their domain as an enemy.

subzone:lake-elune-ara.text: Lake Elune'ara. At Moonglade's heart, Lake Elune'ara rests beneath moonlit groves. The sacred waters honor Elune, and the Cenarion Circle's shrine grounds border its shores. Moonlit groves frame Lake Elune'ara, whose waters are said to bear the White Lady's blessing. Nighthaven lies to the north, and the Cenarion Circle's shrine grounds border the lake. Initiates have long searched its depths for lost relics. Through contact with nature's currents, they seek harmony with the land. Ancient peril sleeps beneath Lake Elune'ara's quiet surface. Legends tell of Omen, a two-headed wolf demigod and revered ancient corrupted by the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Defeated long ago, Omen was cast into the lake bed. There he sleeps beneath the dark water, a reminder of nature's wounds.

subzone:lake-kel-theril.text: Lake Kel'Theril. Beneath Lake Kel'Theril's ice, ancient ruins hold the spirits of the kaldorei who once lived there. Snow and frozen water cover the remains of their outpost from before the Great Sundering. Lake Kel'Theril lies frozen beneath Winterspring's bitter cold. Shattered pillars and arches rise through the ice and along the snowy banks. They are all that remains of Kel'Theril, an outpost of the ancient Highborne before the Great Sundering broke Kalimdor apart. Even in death, the fallen aristocracy found no rest. Their ghosts and specters still wander the lake, bound to the ruins of their former home.

subzone:lake-mennar.text: Lake Mennar. At Lake Mennar, blue dragonspawn guard the freshwater amid Azshara’s shattered ruins. The shores stay strangely serene, and blue dragons gather here in numbers rarely seen beyond Northrend. Lake Mennar draws the blue dragonflight into Azshara’s ancient, broken landscape. Few places on Kalimdor hold so many blue dragons; Mazthoril in Winterspring is another. Blue dragonspawn patrol the ridges and approaches, guarding the basin’s waters. Beyond their ring of sentries, the lake remains strangely serene, shielded from the arcane turmoil and roaming beast packs found across the peninsula.

subzone:lake-mereldar.text:
Lake Mereldar. Lake Mereldar's waters south of Corin's Crossing have turned foul and corrupted. Once part of Lordaeron's rural heartland, the lake now breeds twisted elementals beneath the Scourge's lingering taint. South of Corin's Crossing, Lake Mereldar rests among the old farms of northern Lordaeron. Ruins of a homestead, an abandoned shack, and a worn ferry mark its shores. Farmers and travelers once crossed its gentle waters by ferry.

Then the Scourge brought its plague of undeath, and the lake and its surroundings fell into ruin. The soil withered, and the water turned foul and poisonous. The blight in Lake Mereldar has tainted the water and the spirits bound to it. Blighted Surges are corrupted water elementals, driven mad by necromantic residue. They lurk in the shallows and surface without warning.

Plague Ravagers prowl the muddy, weed-choked banks. They hunt living creatures that stray near the dead shoreline.

subzone:lake-nazferiti.text: Lake Nazferiti. In northern Stranglethorn, river waters gather at Lake Nazferiti. Crocolisks and snapping frenzies hunt beneath its surface, while the Venture Company works along the shores. The Nazferiti River runs across the southern Eastern Kingdoms and widens into Lake Nazferiti in Stranglethorn. It begins in the northern heights, where it plunges from the Redridge Mountains in waterfalls. Its headwaters may reach as far inland as Deadwind Pass. By the time the river spreads into the lake, its waters are murky. Snapping river frenzies and crocolisks hunt there, making a swim deadly. The Venture Company has brought heavy operations to Lake Nazferiti's banks. Goblins cut jungle timber and take other resources with saws, drills, and crews that clear the land. Their base pollutes the water. The work brings them into constant clashes with local wildlife and hunters traveling through the vale.

subzone:lakkari-tar-pits.text: Lakkari Tar Pits. In northern Un’Goro Crater, the Lakkari Tar Pits hold beasts fast and give rise to hostile tar elementals. South of Marshal’s Refuge, the Lakkari Tar Pits spread across northern Un’Goro Crater. Their black tar grips anyone who steps in and drags beasts and travelers into the mire. Bones of countless prehistoric creatures jut through the surface. Scavengers circle the pools for trapped prey, while tar beasts, lurkers, and creepers rise from the muck to attack those who enter.

subzone:land-s-end-beach.text:
Land's End Beach. At Kalimdor’s southern edge, Land's End Beach lies quiet beneath the sun. Tanaris’s southern mountains and the vast South Seas cut this coast off from the desert. Beyond Tanaris’s southern mountains, Land's End Beach meets the far southern edge of Kalimdor’s mainland. The sealed titan gateway to Uldum stands beyond the ranges. No desert route reaches this coast, so travelers must swim through the dangerous open waters of the South Seas.

Surf breaks on shifting sand along the barren shore. The cartels and desert explorers who live farther north around Gadgetzan rarely come here. Unnamed islets lie beyond the beach’s breakers, with broad stretches of deep water between them and the mainland. Reaching these rocks can exhaust even seasoned swimmers. Few mortals have reason to seek out the lonely waters at Kalimdor’s end, so the beach and nearby shoals remain undisturbed beneath the southern sun.

subzone:lariss-pavilion.text: Lariss Pavilion. At Lariss Pavilion, dryads attack those who draw near. The ancient retreat north of Camp Mojache now shelters an exiled Highborne mage. You stand on the bluffs north of Camp Mojache, where graceful stonework and towering arches overlook Feralas's dense canopy. The kaldorei empire built Lariss Pavilion to serve Eldre'Thalas, the great city now called Dire Maul. Yet the glades around it offer no safe refuge. Dryads once wandered here gently, but madness and corruption have taken hold. Now they attack anyone who draws near. Azj'Tordin, an elusive elf, has made his home at Lariss Pavilion. He broke from Prince Tortheldrin's decadent rule in Dire Maul and escaped through a secret passage linking the pavilion to the ancient city's underbelly. But his quiet exile was disturbed by Pusillin, an erratic imp who stole his treasured book of incantations. Now the Highborne seeks outside aid to recover it.

subzone:launch-bay.text:
Launch Bay. Hostile leper gnomes and corrupted machines hold Launch Bay beyond the Hall of Gears. Once Gnomeregan’s airfield for flying machines and bombers, this hangar lies deep beneath the city. Two tiers once held Gnomeregan’s aerial fleet. Ramps from the upper walkway lead to a central platform, where flying machines and heavy bombers remain parked. They were left behind before the city was evacuated.

Crazed leper gnomes now roam the flight decks. They maintain and guard the idle war machines where skilled pilots once served. Launch Bay joins several parts of the complex. Ramps from its southeastern corridor descend into the Engineering Labs.

On the lower deck, invading Dark Iron dwarves choke the southern passage. That tunnel offers a perilous route toward Tinkers' Court, deep in the city.

subzone:lethlor-ravine.text: Lethlor Ravine. Black dragons roost and rear their young in Lethlor Ravine, deep in the eastern Badlands. Scorched plateaus rise around Lethlor Ravine in the eastern Badlands. Craggy walls shelter the black dragonflight’s nests. Fierce whelps crowd beneath the watch of larger drakes that breathe fire. Few travelers dare approach the ravine floor. Overhead, shadows mark winged predators circling among the rocky spires. Crystalline obelisks lie scattered among the crags beside the dragon brood. They are involved in a local chain of tasks, but their origin is not established.

subzone:library-wing-tyr-s-hand.text:
Library Wing (Tyr's Hand). In the Library Wing of Tyr's Hand, Scarlet Crusaders guard their books and relics. The secluded hall lies within the order's fortified redoubt in the Eastern Plaguelands. Crusaders gather there to study scripture and keep watch over the sanctum. Off the abbey's central nave and opposite the martial quarters, the Library Wing holds the Scarlet Crusade's religious writings. Priests and crusaders study theology, militant doctrine, and works shaped by years of war against the Scourge.

These books do not preserve open scholarship. They feed the Crusade's suspicion and its belief that every outsider bears corruption. The Scarlet priesthood guards the library's scrolls and scriptures. To reach its back rooms, you must fight through elite Scarlet defenders. They protect the library as both a bastion of faith and a fortress.

subzone:light-s-hope-chapel.text:
Light's Hope Chapel. At Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Dawn holds its chief redoubt against the Scourge. In the eastern Plaguelands, the Church of the Holy Light's secluded Eastweald chapel has become the order's headquarters. Light's Hope Chapel began as a secluded chapel of the Church of the Holy Light in the Eastweald. It survived Lordaeron's fall and now shelters those in a blighted land. Among the survivors, zealous extremists broke away to form the Scarlet Crusade. More temperate knights and priests joined to establish the Argent Dawn, which chose the hallowed chapel as its forward base.

The order opens its doors to every race and faction. Alliance and Horde fighters stand together there, seeking to purge the Scourge and reclaim the northern lands.

subzone:loading-room.text:
Loading Room. In Gnomeregan's depths, the Loading Room lies amid danger. It once staged cargo for the city's transit networks. Now radioactive fallout and rogue machinery threaten all who enter. Cargo once passed through the Loading Room on its way across Gnomeregan's underground transit network. Goods gathered in its staging bay before the trains carried them through the tinker capital.

Now ruin has overtaken the chamber. Radioactive fallout, invading troggs, and failing machinery make it perilous. Techbot, a rogue mechanized construct, guards the vicinity. Gnome survivors and Alliance reclaimers who try to secure the perimeter must face that danger.

subzone:lordamere-internment-camp.text: Lordamere Internment Camp. Surviving Dalaran magi and guards hold Lordamere Internment Camp above Dalaran. The old prison also shelters Forsaken defectors. Lordamere Internment Camp now serves Dalaran’s remnants as a research outpost. After the Second War, the Alliance built camps across the northern kingdoms to hold the defeated orcish Horde. Lordamere was the only camp in the Alterac Mountains, and Dalaran oversaw it. The orcs have long since been freed or fled. Warden Belamoore leads the camp, where Dalaran’s survivors study dangerous magical relics.

subzone:lost-fleet.text: Lost Fleet. Off the Wetlands’ northern coast, the Lost Fleet lies broken in Baradin Bay. Red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan destroyed the Kul Tiras Third Fleet in the Second War. Now cursed undead sailors haunt its wrecks. The Wave Mistress and the Intrepid lie wrecked on the shallows and reefs of northern Bluegill Marsh. On the Third Fleet’s last voyage in the Second War, red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan attacked. Dragonflame engulfed the ships, and almost the entire contingent drowned or burned. First Mate Fitzsimmons was the lone living survivor.

subzone:lost-point.text: Lost Point. At Lost Point in western Dustwallow, deserters have driven out Lady Jaina Proudmoore's guard. Theramore built the tower as an advance scout post, but it has fallen into disrepair. Lost Point once watched the Barrens for traffic and threats on Theramore's behalf. Its military purpose passed, and marsh damp rotted the timber. Regular troops abandoned the defenses. Now human deserters from Theramore hold the tower and the nearby ground. They found shelter in this isolated wilderness, far from the discipline of the city's commanders.

subzone:lost-rigger-cove.text: Lost Rigger Cove. At Lost Rigger Cove, pirate ships take shape along Tanaris's eastern cliffs. Desert mountains shield the hidden port on three sides, where the Southsea Pirates keep docks and fortified camps beside their shipyard. Rock walls guard almost every side of Lost Rigger Cove. Here on Kalimdor's southeastern edge, the Southsea Freebooters haul salvage and build fresh hulls under Gadgetzan's nose. Cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands work from this stronghold. From here, Southsea power reaches across the Great Sea, and its pirates raid trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements. Gadgetzan and nearby Steamwheedle Port oppose the Southsea Pirates at their doorstep. The goblins resent the raiders, so they pay mercenaries to slaughter them, thin their ranks, and disrupt their operations.

subzone:lower-wilds.text: Lower Wilds. In eastern Feralas, the road runs west from Thalanaar toward the settlements beyond. Humid forest gives way to the dry canyons of Thousand Needles. At Thalanaar, night elves guard the mountain pass where the road enters Feralas from Thousand Needles. You travel west beneath dense canopies, with ancient treants and native wildlife in the woods around you. Leave the road, and the forest grows perilous. Travelers, scouts, and couriers use the Lower Wilds road between southern wilderness and eastern territories. Night elves hold Thalanaar at the gateway, while the Horde keeps Camp Mojache further inland. The road carries supplies across southern Kalimdor, though woodland dangers and faction tensions make the journey fraught.

subzone:magram-village.text: Magram Village. In southeastern Desolace, the Magram hold their village amid foul yellow pools. They use it as a base in their war against the Gelkis, their hated rivals. Stagnant yellow pools ring the islands and shores where the Magram make their home in southeastern Desolace. Crude wooden bridges cross the mire, joining their hide tents. The clan keeps watch against its neighbors and is known for brutality and deep hatred of the southern Gelkis. Outsiders find no welcome unless they prove their worth by slaughtering Gelkis enemies.

subzone:maker-s-terrace.text: Maker's Terrace. At the Badlands' northern edge, Dark Iron dwarves hold the Maker's Terrace beside the pass from Loch Modan. Their open-air dig guards the way into Uldaman. From the pass out of Loch Modan, you cross trenches and scaffolds spread across the northern Badlands. The dig fronts Uldaman's entrance, an ancient vault built by the Makers. Travelers cross this exposed ground before reaching the halls below. Rival factions contest the approach as they seek a way into the ruins. Dark Iron dwarves patrol the ditches and perimeter, keeping outsiders from the dig. They seek the Makers' relics and power to dominate what lies beneath the earth. Their crews search the hillside for armaments, records, and other relics left by the ancient Makers. The sentries guard the route into Uldaman, and travelers who try to pass meet a hostile welcome.

subzone:mannoroc-coven.text: Mannoroc Coven. Burning Blade cultists keep portals open at Mannoroc Coven in southern Desolace. They draw felhounds, succubi, and infernals into an ancient ruin, making it the Burning Legion’s largest stronghold in central Kalimdor.

subzone:mardenholde-keep.text:
Mardenholde Keep. In western Lordaeron, the Scarlet Crusade holds Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep. Highlord Taelan Fordring rules from the fortress once held by his father, Tirion. Mardenholde Keep once governed the principality of Hearthglen and the vales around it. Lord Tirion Fordring ruled from its council chambers with trusted advisors, keeping peace across the region. For generations, Lordaeron's people praised the fortress because it never fell during the Second War.

Then Tirion defended the orc Eitrigg and was exiled. Governance passed to his ambitious apprentice, Barthilas, and later to Tirion's son, Taelan. Taelan inherited his father's domain on the eve of Lordaeron's destruction.

subzone:marris-stead.text: Marris Stead. In the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, Nathanos Blightcaller holds Marris Stead. Once a peaceful Lordaeron homestead, the ridge now shelters his lonely, heavily defended redoubt.

subzone:marshal-s-refuge.text: Marshal's Refuge. In Marshal's Refuge, expedition survivors shelter above Un'Goro Crater's dangerous basin. Williden Marshal and his party established the camp after beasts overran their lower camps. Williden and Hol'anyee Marshal led their expedition into Un'Goro Crater. Its ancient beasts proved fiercer than they expected. After the creatures overran their first camps again and again, the survivors fled to the northern cliffs. Now Marshal's Refuge clings to a cavernous ledge above the jungle floor, where weary explorers can rest, find basic supplies, and speak with flight masters. Researchers and wanderers gather at Marshal's Refuge to study Un'Goro Crater's ancient life and strange crystals. The surviving Marshal crew shares the crowded ledge with naturalists from many lands, including dwarven scholars and gnomish tinkerers. From the camp, scouts set out for Fire Plume Ridge and the Golakka Hot Springs. They hope to record the wilderness before it overwhelms them.

subzone:marshlands.text: Marshlands. The Tanaris trail brings travelers into Un'Goro through the Marshlands. Raptors hunt among the wetlands, where Blue Power Crystals lie scattered and two wilderness experts keep apart. From Tanaris, the trail descends into the Marshlands. It is the only safe way down Un'Goro's sheer crater rim. Dense canopies, standing water, and mud conceal packs of fierce raptors. Some are venomous hunters that stalk the reeds. Blue Power Crystals, found nowhere else in Un'Goro, lie across damp clearings. Several wilderness experts keep solitary outposts in the dangerous marsh. Torwa Pathfinder, a tauren hunter, watches the primeval fauna from a prominent earthen mound. Across the wetlands, Mor'vek studies and trains native ravasaurs. Mor'vek is a troll.

subzone:master-s-cellar.text: Master's Cellar. Restless dead haunt Master's Cellar beneath the ruined hamlet south of Karazhan. Wine and provisions once filled its vaults for Medivh's estate; now the dead crowd its cellars and caverns. South of Karazhan, ruined homes mark the hamlet where Medivh's servants, groundskeepers, and attendants once lived. Two entrances in the ruins lead beneath them into Master's Cellar. One opens into vaulted wine cellars. The other descends through broken stone into natural caverns. Whatever dark fate overtook Karazhan and its master reached the hamlet too. Caretakers, wailing spectres, and damned souls remain trapped below, bound to endless service. At the deepest reach of Master's Cellar, the Lower Cellar opens into the rock beneath Deadwind Pass. The floor and foundations crumbled into natural caverns, leaving a jagged maze where ghostly wails travel through the stone. Few living souls enter these depths. Magical corruption from the nearby tower holds the apparitions here, making the caverns perilous, much like the ruins above.

subzone:maul-subzone.text: Maul (subzone). In Maul, fighters face beasts and rivals in the sunken pit beyond Dire Maul. The Broken Commons ring once belonged to Eldre'Thalas, but no faction now keeps order on its floor. Deep in the Broken Commons, Maul’s stone pit once hosted the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas for theater or ceremony. After the Sundering, Gordok ogres took the ruins, and the pit became a raw colosseum. Like the Gurubashi Arena in distant Stranglethorn Vale, its sands erase allegiance. Fighters from opposing factions meet freely, and survival belongs to the strong. Take care on the way down. Daring fighters sometimes leap from the Broken Commons’ high ledges, but the fall hits hard. A western archway leads down more safely through tunnels where Gordok hyenas sleep. It is the only way out on foot. Dangerous beasts and notorious gladiators enter at irregular times, so each descent brings an uncertain fight.

subzone:mazthoril.text:
Mazthoril. In central Winterspring, Mazthoril shelters the blue dragonflight in a vast cavern. Its ice tunnels are guarded by dragonkin, spell-wielding wyrms, and arcane sentries, and lead to the aerie of Haleh, the reclusive blue matriarch. Just south of Everlook, Mazthoril is cut into the frozen mountains. A large brood lives within and answers to Malygos, the Spell-Weaver. Dragonkin patrol the cavern and the nearby crags, among them Spellmaw, Azurous, and General Colbatann.

Elite guardians keep watch over the inner caverns. The dragonspawn are attuned to raw arcane energy, so any journey inside is perilous without serious preparation.

subzone:menethil-bay.text: Menethil Bay. Alliance ships cross Menethil Bay along the Wetlands' western coast. Its sheltered waters open into Baradin Bay, between Menethil Harbor to the north and Dun Morogh's steep cliffs to the south. Crocolisks prowl the shallows, and sunken vessels lie below. Menethil Bay opens from the Wetlands into the Great Sea, within Baradin Bay. Menethil Harbor lies to the north, Black Channel Marsh to the east, and Dun Morogh's coastal bluffs to the south. Crocolisks of many sizes prowl the shallows and marshy shores. Without a guide, travelers risk the waters. Alliance ships cross the bay, and near its mouth lies the ruined Flying Osprey, a warning of wreckage below.

subzone:menethil-keep.text: Menethil Keep. At Menethil Keep, Captain Stoutfist leads the militia guarding Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Four watchtowers rise above the Alliance port. Menethil Keep watches over Menethil Harbor, its wooden docks, and the marshes beyond. Four stone watchtowers look across the town and bay for raiders from the sea, renegades, and swamp beasts entering the area. Inside the fortress, Captain Stoutfist directs the town militia and sets its patrols. They defend the port and Alliance interests across the region.

subzone:mirage-flats.text: Mirage Flats. East of Dustbelch Grotto, heat shimmers over Mirage Flats in the Badlands. Hungry predators roam the dry plateau beneath the desert sun. East of Dustbelch Grotto, cracked red dirt runs beneath wavering heat. Few civilized souls linger on Mirage Flats. Giant buzzards circle overhead, watching for scraps left by ferocious ridge stalkers and crag coyotes that hunt in packs through the brush.

subzone:misty-reed-post.text: Misty Reed Post. Between Stagalbog and the Misty Reed Strand, Misty Reed Post keeps watch over the wetlands and the dangerous coast. The Horde holds this camp under Stonard's authority. A handful of Stonard hunters, the shaman Katar, and Tok'Kar keep watch between Stagalbog and the eastern shore. The camp stands under Stonard's banner, exposed to marsh wildlife and lingering damp. Tok'Kar hopes Horde command in Stonard will send an orcish burrow or watchtower. For now, the scouts hold the marsh with tents, campfire smoke, and sharpened steel.

subzone:misty-reed-strand.text: Misty Reed Strand. At Misty Reed Strand, the Great Sea meets the eastern edge of the Swamp of Sorrows. Crabs, crocolisks, and murlocs contest its foggy shore, where driftwood and wreckage wash ashore. Fog rolls in from the Great Sea along Misty Reed Strand, the eastern edge of the Swamp of Sorrows. It hides the water and dulls the cries of wildlife. Driftwood, sea debris, and rotting plants from the inland bog litter the beach. No permanent settlement holds this remote shore. Aggressive crabs forage among the debris, crocolisks stalk the water’s edge, and territorial murlocs defend their grounds. Neither the Alliance nor the Horde claims the beach, though scouts from both send adventurers there. Alliance parties gather driftwood and salvage while thinning the crab population. Farther inland, Horde outposts watch the murloc camps. They send fighters to curb the tribes before raiders push toward Stonard or threaten travel through the marsh.

subzone:misty-shore.text: Misty Shore. Along Lordamere Lake's eastern bank, Misty Shore lies between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Fog softens the view across the water, where the Dawning Isles and Fenris Keep rise in the distance. Misty Shore follows Lordamere Lake's eastern bank between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Damp air drifts off the water, often hiding snapping turtles along the shore. Zealous fanatics sometimes wander down from nearby strongholds. Across Lordamere Lake, the Dawning Isles and Fenris Keep rise through the fog. Dalaran lies nearby, with Scarlet-controlled pockets close at hand. Travelers keep a low profile along the bank to avoid unwanted attention.

subzone:misty-valley.text: Misty Valley. Fog gathers in Misty Valley, north of the pass into Deadwind. Swamp beasts and marsh horrors roam its secluded basin in the northwestern Swamp of Sorrows. Cliffs rise between the Swamp of Sorrows and Deadwind Pass, and fog shrouds the hollow below. Colossal marsh elementals crowd this isolated valley. Swampwalkers and ancient swampwalker elders roam among creeping tangled horrors. At the gorge’s far end, a cavern shelters one of the bog’s strongest natural threats: the Mire Lord.

subzone:mizjah-ruins.text: Mizjah Ruins. In northern Stranglethorn Vale, Mosh'Ogg ogres have taken shelter in the Mizjah Ruins, southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp. They ambush supply caravans bound for the Swamp of Sorrows. The Gurubashi Empire raised the Mizjah Ruins long before modern empires rose. Now Mosh'Ogg ogres dwell among the cracked stones, including brute warriors and crude witch doctors. They raid supply convoys bound for the Horde settlement of Stonard. Their attacks trouble Grom'gol's commanders.

subzone:moon-horror-den.text: Moon Horror Den. In Winterspring’s mountains northeast of Everlook, raging owlbeasts defend their den. Travelers who draw near the icy cave mouth meet wildkin guarding their home. Moon Horror Den opens in the mountain northeast of Everlook. Raging owlbeasts live within, fierce and at home in Winterspring’s harsh snows. Winterfall Village lies south, but a sheer mountain face bars the way. The den remains an isolated refuge, far from the paths travelers take.

subzone:moonshrine-sanctum.text: Moonshrine Sanctum. Twilight's Hammer gathers beneath Queen Azshara's statue in Moonshrine Sanctum. Twilight Lord Kelris watches over the ancient shrine and the sealed way to Aku'mai's lair. Beyond the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, Twilight's Hammer gathers in the Moonshrine Sanctum, the cult's heart inside Blackfathom Deeps. Night elves built the hall millennia ago to honor the moon and their rulers. Now the cult has defiled it, though Queen Azshara's towering statue remains carefully tended. Beneath the high stone ceiling, Twilight Lord Kelris watches as cultists chant dark rituals day and night.

subzone:morgan-s-plot.text:
Morgan's Plot. Restless dead roam Morgan's Plot behind Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Its ruined chapel and graves hold those who once belonged to Medivh's household. Behind Karazhan, Morgan's Plot lies against rocky slopes. A ruined chapel stands above crypts beneath the earth. Before Deadwind Pass fell into decay, the estate buried those who lived in the tower and on the nearby grounds.

After Medivh, the Last Guardian, fell, dark energies seeped into the earth. Restless dead drove away all normal life. Now the unliving wander among the headstones, where servants and figures from Karazhan's history lie buried.

subzone:morgan-s-vigil.text:
Morgan's Vigil. Alliance defenders keep watch over the passes to Blackrock Mountain from ruined Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Charred homes and a shattered mage tower stand around their camp, the Alliance's only foothold in a land held by Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs. You find Morgan's Vigil on high stone above the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. Once a modest settlement, it fell when the horrors of the region overran it. Charred timbers and a cracked mage tower mark what remains. The defenders shelter in rough canvas tents among the soot.

A gryphon roost links the camp by air to Stormwind City across the mountains. Scouts, marshals, and travelers find shelter here from the warbands below. Morgan's Vigil watches against the threat of Blackrock Mountain. The Dark Iron clan delves into dark sorceries, while Blackrock orcs claim the surrounding wastes. So the defenders maintain the camp's defenses and coordinate scouting runs across the ash. They also secure the vital pass leading south into Redridge.

subzone:morlos-aran.text: Morlos'Aran. In southern Felwood, Morlos'Aran lies in ruins beneath demonic blight. The ancient night elf settlement flourished before the Great Sundering. Before the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand center of ancient kaldorei life. Like Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas held elven life and arcana. The Well of Eternity collapsed, and the city broke apart.
