Its shattered colonnades remain from the height of kaldorei civilization. During the Third War, the Burning Legion trampled the corridor where Morlos'Aran stood. Demonic corruption and toxic mire choked its surviving foundations. The ruins suffered a grimmer fate than those in Darkshore and Ashenvale, where decay and wilderness took hold. Today, wandering beasts, corrupted elementals, and remnants of shadow forces haunt the ruins and linger in Felwood.

subzone:mosh-ogg-ogre-mound.text: Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. In northern Stranglethorn Vale, Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound lies south of Zul'Gurub's ruins. The Mosh'Ogg tribe holds its fortified caverns under Mai'Zoth, their ruthless ogre mage chieftain. Mosh'Ogg ogres fill the jungle caverns south of Zul'Gurub. Maulers, shamans, and warmongers guard the twisting passages. The tribe seized the ridges as a refuge from hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts. Mai'Zoth commands the Mosh'Ogg clan from deep within the mound. The formidable chieftain has two heads and practices ogre magic. He holds the Mind's Eye, a potent and dangerous arcane relic. Its power strengthens his hold over his followers through mind and sorcery. His magic and brute force make the mound's deepest reaches perilous for travelers in northern Stranglethorn.

subzone:mosshide-fen.text: Mosshide Fen. In eastern Wetlands, the Mosshide gnolls keep travelers from their hunting grounds. Their camps lie far from the main trade roads, where danger waits in the marsh. Rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps mark the Mosshide gnolls’ territory in eastern Wetlands. Gnawbone and the other pack leaders command the tribe. Their hunters ambush travelers, scouts, and prospectors who enter the tangled marsh, then devour them.

subzone:nat-s-landing.text: Nat's Landing. At Nat's Landing, fishermen come to Dustwallow Bay seeking Nat Pagle's highest instruction. The famous angler keeps a quiet camp there. Southwest of Theramore Isle, you find Nat's Landing beside the murky waters of Dustwallow Bay. A canvas tent, drying racks for the day's catch, spare tackle in the trees, and a rickety pier mark the weathered camp. Mists and swamp dangers surround this quiet shore. Nat Pagle comes here for solitude and a drink, away from the clamor of civilization. Anglers who have learned all they can from trainers in Ironforge, Orgrimmar, and elsewhere are sent to Nat Pagle. Politics and factional quarrels mean nothing to him. To earn his highest instruction, you must brave marshland predators and show patience and skill across the world's most perilous waters.

subzone:nek-mani-wellspring.text: Nek'mani Wellspring. Naga guard Nek'mani Wellspring high above the Southern Savage Coast. Its fountain holds remarkably pure holy water, the only pristine fresh water south of Duskwood. Nek'mani Wellspring rises among the coastal heights of western Stranglethorn Vale. Scholars and pilgrims call its waters holy. Each culture claims the divine spring was blessed for its own people, and faiths still dispute whose claim is true. Now a vicious band of naga holds the basin and guards its water against all who approach.

subzone:nesingwary-s-expedition.text: Nesingwary's Expedition. Hunters gather at Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, north of Lake Nazferiti. Hemet Nesingwary has made this camp a base for hunters who test themselves against the jungle's fiercest predators. Beside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, Nesingwary's Expedition is a hunters' camp founded by Hemet Nesingwary. Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot are among its seasoned hunters. Hired marksmen guard the camp, while neutral vendors supply it. Skilled riflemen and bowmen of any allegiance are welcome to hunt the jungle's deadliest predators. At Nesingwary's Expedition, hunters trade competition and tall tales. They learn to track panthers, raptors, and tigers before turning to the jungle's greatest beasts. There is work for scholars, too. Pages from Nesingwary's long manuscript have scattered across the wilds, and the scholars at camp seek every missing chapter.

subzone:nethander-stead.text: Nethander Stead. Along the road east of Southshore, Nethander Stead lies abandoned beneath the Mudsnout gnolls. Giant white Mudsnout Blossoms now cover its fields and draw Forsaken alchemists. Ruined fences and outbuildings at Nethander Stead stand within sight of Southshore’s eastern borders. Once part of Hillsbrad’s working fields, the farm was abandoned as security weakened and wild packs moved in. The Mudsnout gnolls make their only home in these foothills. They drive off travelers who come too close to their territory.

subzone:nethergarde-keep.text:
Nethergarde Keep. Nethergarde Keep watches the Dark Portal from the bluffs above the road into the Blasted Lands. The Alliance raised it after the Second War to guard the dormant gateway and the red wastes beyond. Mages and soldiers, supplied by Stormwind, keep watch against demons and lingering corruption. After the Dark Portal fell at the end of the Second War, Archmage Khadgar and the Alliance of Lordaeron knew the rift could not go unguarded. So the Alliance raised bastions, barracks, and mage spires along the canyon pass into the Blasted Lands. Kirin Tor sorcerers took their posts in the keep. They watched the shattered gateway and wove wards to keep demonic blight from creeping north into the human kingdoms. When the Dark Portal reopened, the Alliance Expedition crossed into Draenor. Khadgar and his companions sealed the gateway behind them, leaving Nethergarde to guard its silent remnant. For two decades, scholars from Dalaran and the Wizard's Sanctum have studied the portal's lingering energies, mutated local fauna, and demonic incursions.

After Dalaran was ravaged during the Third War, Stormwind City became the keep's sole source of vital supply caravans. Its soldiers and mages now stand alone against the horrors haunting the wasteland.

subzone:nighthaven.text: Nighthaven. Nighthaven welcomes druids of both factions to Moonglade’s northern shore. Night elves and tauren study together in peace at the Cenarion Circle’s heart. Along Lake Elune'ara’s calm northern shore, Nighthaven gathers night elf halls and moonwells among its groves. The Cenarion Circle keeps this secluded village as a place for druids to learn and tend to nature. Trainers, herbalists, and suppliers serve those who come to study. Here, druids find neutral ground whatever their ties to the Alliance or the Horde. Peace in Nighthaven has faced a trial. Centuries after the War of the Ancients, champions gathered there to face the enraged demigod Omen. They drove him beneath Lake Elune'ara. During the Lunar Festival, the village opens its borders to pilgrims from across Azeroth, who honor the ancestors beneath Elune's watchful gaze.

subzone:nijel-s-point.text:
Nijel's Point. Alliance soldiers and Cenarion druids hold Nijel's Point above Desolace's harsh wastes. The outpost shelters travelers, researchers, and soldiers crossing the blighted valleys below. Nijel's Point clings to cliffs along the Stonetalon Mountains, high above Desolace's gray dust and marauding centaur packs. Captain Pentigast commands a Stormwind Army detachment there. His soldiers watch the clan wars that threaten Alliance interests across southern Kalimdor. High cliffs and narrow trails make the outpost easy to defend.

Couriers, scouts, and griffin riders use Nijel's Point as a staging ground on routes between Stonetalon Peak, Theramore, and Feathermoon Stronghold. Stormwind soldiers share Nijel's Point with emissaries whose work takes them into danger. Keeper Marandis and his dryads use the camp as a base to confront Princess Theradras deep within Maraudon and recover the fallen demigod Zaetar. Brother Anton, an emissary of the Scarlet Crusade, seeks to scour the undead ravaging the valley floor. Even among the soldiers and druids on the ridge, Nijel's identity remains an ancient mystery.

subzone:northdale.text: Northdale. Northdale lies in ruins north of Light's Hope Chapel, near the border of Quel'Thalas. Banshees, hidden watchers, and corrupted elementals haunt its streets. Here, Taelan Fordring left the Order of the Silver Hand for the Scarlet Crusade. Northdale lies among the hills north of Light's Hope Chapel, beside the northern highway to Quel'Thalas. The Third War shattered this once peaceful town. Its people were slain or driven away, and its hearths went cold. Now wailing banshees drift among the broken walls. Invisible Eyeless Watchers watch the cursed roads from the dark. The nearby lake has fallen to the plague, too, and corrupted water elementals churn its waters.

subzone:northfold-manor.text:
Northfold Manor. The Syndicate holds Northfold Manor in northwestern Arathi. Once a prosperous human homestead, the estate fell into ruin after Stromgarde collapsed and now shelters criminals and dark practices. Near the passage through Thoradin's Wall, Northfold Manor spreads across the rolling highlands. The estate once supported the kingdom of Stromgarde. After the realm fractured, displaced Alteraci nobles and Syndicate outlaws claimed the manor house, barn, and fields as their base.

Mercenaries, highwaymen, and pathstalkers gather there, leaving the crops untended. From the farmstead, they ambush travelers on nearby roads and coordinate the Syndicate's presence across Arathi.

subzone:northpass-tower.text: Northpass Tower. Northpass Tower watches over the northern road to Quel'Thalas as a ruin. Shattered during the Third War, the old Lordaeron scout tower still looks toward the elven lands. Northpass Tower once guarded Lordaeron's road north into Quel'Thalas. During the Scourge invasion, the tower was reduced to a broken shell. From its high ground, it still overlooks the frontier between Stratholme's blighted outskirts and the distant elven lands. No garrison mans Northpass Tower today. Its broken walls stand beside the road, now haunted by the Scourge. The ruin marks the watch Lordaeron once kept over the route to Quel'Thalas.

subzone:northridge-lumber-camp.text: Northridge Lumber Camp. Scarlet Crusade guards hold Northridge Lumber Camp, an active, fortified mill in the hills near Hearthglen. Its timber feeds nearby strongholds, and the Alliance and Horde seek ways to cripple the Crusade’s supply. Scarlet Crusade workers fell and process timber at Northridge Lumber Camp, despite the plague in the surrounding forests. The mill lies down the road from Hearthglen, in the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands. Its wood builds fortifications, repairs watchtowers, and sustains the Crusade’s war effort in Lordaeron. Guards and laborers garrison the camp in force, defending it from the Scourge and trespassers. Hearthglen depends on Northridge Lumber Camp for timber to maintain its defenses. That need makes the mill a target for outside forces. Alliance commanders and Horde scouts know a direct assault on fortified Crusade positions would cost dearly. So their agents seek quieter ways to sabotage the operation, such as releasing wood-boring termites into the lumber stores and spoiling the Crusade’s supplies from within.

subzone:noxious-glade.text:
Noxious Glade. North of Light's Hope Chapel, the Noxious Glade lies under a heavy veil of plague. The Scourge hold the hollow close to the Argent Dawn's watch. At Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Dawn keeps watch while a Scourge camp lies in the hills just north. Plague grips this hollow more fiercely than much of the surrounding land. Sickly green mist fills the air, and the soil has turned a bruised purple.

The undead have raised ziggurats here, along with a slaughterhouse where they assemble abominations. A plague cauldron continually sends pestilence into the air. The glade lies close enough to Light's Hope Chapel to threaten travelers, couriers, and holy warriors who work from there. Scourge forces build monstrosities and brew toxins in the hollow, hidden from view by the natural ridge.

Climb the path unwary, and the Scourge may be waiting just ahead.

subzone:noxious-lair.text: Noxious Lair. In Tanaris, Centipaar silithid have made the Noxious Lair their home. They drained the water from a sunken basin near Un'Goro Crater and raised an acidic hive above rich mineral veins. Beside the western ridges above Un'Goro Crater, the Noxious Lair fills a sandy hollow. A lake or shallow river once lay here, but the Centipaar silithid consumed the remaining underground moisture and claimed the basin. Now pincers and twitching limbs rise from the dunes above tunnels in the sand. Corrosive secretions coat the passages, and clusters of eggs fill the chambers. Entrances descend into humid breeding chambers slick with acid. Centipaar workers, tunnelers, wasps, and colossal sandreavers patrol the perimeter and guard their brood from outside threats. Their digging has exposed deep mineral deposits too. Ore lies bare among the hives, drawing hunters and prospectors to the basin.

subzone:old-port-authority.text: Old Port Authority. In Booty Bay, the Old Port Authority draws travelers to its market stalls. Beneath its roof, they find exotic pets, firearms, hearty rations, and finely crafted weapons. Beneath Booty Bay’s boardwalks, the Old Port Authority draws brisk trade in the pirate haven. Its stalls offer supplies, firearms, bows, food, and weapons to scoundrels and privateers. Nautical imports include colorful birds and oddities from the docks, all offered to anyone with coin.

subzone:oneiros.text: Oneiros. In northern Feralas, green dragonkin guard Oneiros and its ancient night elven ruins. The stones lie south of Jademir Lake, near portals that lead toward Ysera's realm. In northern Feralas, broken arches and columns mark an ancient Kaldorei settlement. Abandoned millennia ago, its stones are now threaded with roots and overgrowth. Green Dragonflight guardians patrol the shaded paths and ruined plazas, keeping mortals from ancient secrets.

subzone:onyxia-s-lair.text: Onyxia's Lair. Deep in the Wyrmbog, magma burns beneath the marsh in Onyxia's Lair. Onyxia keeps her stronghold and nesting place here, watching over clutches of black dragon eggs. The entrance cuts through the Wyrmbog's mud and petrified wood like a dragon's open maw. Beyond it, volcanic heat drives out the marsh's cool rot. Magma seeps through cracks in the obsidian, and tremors often shake the ceilings. In a vast chamber, hundreds of black dragon eggs lie among ash and embers. Flightkin and dragonspawn guards watch the clutch beside Onyxia.

subzone:orgrimmar.text:
Orgrimmar. In northern Durotar, Orgrimmar shelters the New Horde as its warrior capital. Warchief Thrall founded the city in memory of Orgrim Doomhammer. Its red canyons shelter the orcs’ renewal and their struggle to survive on Kalimdor. After the victory at Mount Hyjal, Warchief Thrall led his surviving people south to make a homeland in Durotar. They built Orgrimmar among steep mountain crags, with spiked timber walls, stone watchtowers, and caverns cut deep into the mountains.

Darkspear trolls, tauren stonemasons, and goblin engineers helped raise the fortress. Its defenses turned the wilderness into a stronghold built to withstand a siege. Freed from the demonic bloodlust that once bound them, the orcs built Orgrimmar as a beacon of honor, community, and survival. Orcs and Darkspear trolls live in the city. Emissaries from the tauren of Mulgore and the newly allied Forsaken are welcomed there.

Shamans teach the next generation ancestral balance. In gladiatorial rings, veterans clash to hone the army that guards Kalimdor’s fragile peace.

subzone:ortell-s-hideout.text: Ortell's Hideout. Hermit Ortell keeps to a cave against the mountains in southeastern Silithus. Few choose to live alone in this barren wasteland. In southeastern Silithus, a cave among the cliffs shelters Hermit Ortell. Sandstorms sweep the wastes, and silithid swarms prowl beyond his door. He lives alone, far from civilization and the fortified garrisons of the Cenarion Hold. Travelers brave the dangerous route to this remote corner to seek his peculiar knowledge of the desert and its hazards.

subzone:owl-wing-thicket.text:
Owl Wing Thicket. In southern Winterspring, berserk, moontouched, and crazed owlbeasts prowl the snowy crags of Owl Wing Thicket. Its caves and stone roosts hold ancient night elf altars tied to their origins and to Elune. South of Everlook, Owl Wing Thicket is among Winterspring’s densest owlbeast nesting grounds. Long ago, night elf caretakers revered the creatures as sacred guardians blessed by Elune.

Ancient shrines and moonstone altars remain beneath the cavern overhangs. The lingering spirits of the Guardians of Elune watch over them. Many owlbeasts have fallen to madness and attack travelers who trespass in their holy hollows.

subzone:pestilent-scar.text: Pestilent Scar. In the Eastern Plaguelands, ravenous oozes churn across the floor of Pestilent Scar. The hollow seems older than the Scourge blight that fills it. Pestilent Scar cuts through the eastern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, a gloomy rift in corrupted land. Nearby, sudden eruptions of the Plague of Undeath tore open Infectis Scar. Pestilent Scar seems to have formed naturally, perhaps as a deep river canyon or a lake that dried when the Scourge swept across Lordaeron. Barren at first, the trench gradually filled with noxious runoff and foul slime. Without pure water and under constant unholy decay, the hollow now breeds mutated, acidic slimes and carrion vermin. Crossing its crumbling rim is dangerous. Acrid fumes choke the air above the drop, and unstable soil can send the unwary into the churning muck.

subzone:plaguemist-ravine.text: Plaguemist Ravine. In western Plaguelands, sickly fog drifts south through Plaguemist Ravine. The narrow passage links the Hinterlands to Darrowmere Lake and offers a quiet, desolate route across the range. Northwest of Quel'Danil Lodge, Plaguemist Ravine cuts between the Hinterlands and the Western Plaguelands. Lush, untamed highland forest lies to the south. Northward, the pass opens onto Caer Darrow and the blighted shores of Darrowmere Lake. The two realms could hardly be more different. Foul vapors creep south from the Plaguelands, meeting the crisp mountain air of the neighboring wilderness. Though the ravine cuts into Scourge-ravaged territory, it remains remarkably deserted. No wild beasts or wandering undead linger in the gorge. Its winding path makes a convenient, if ominous, back road for daring couriers and adventurers. They can use it to bypass the heavily fortified highways and border checkpoints leading into Lordaeron.

subzone:plaguewood.text: Plaguewood. Scarlet Crusaders patrol Plaguewood, where the Scourge gathers south of Stratholme. Greenwood has become a blighted forest choked with fungus. Before the Third War, Greenwood was a forest much like Elwynn's lush woods. A modest village stood by its entrance, and farmers and soldiers traveled the roads. Then tainted grain came from Andorhal, and the woodland fell. Rich earth turned to spongy, corrupted soil. Huge mushrooms now dwarf the dead trees and spread noxious brown vapors over the forest floor. The Scourge has taken Plaguewood and made it a staging ground for the undead around Stratholme. Ziggurats and slaughterhouses dot the ruined land, producing abominations and cultists. Scarlet Crusaders patrol the road to Stratholme's gates, bent on purging the Scourge. They also slaughter any living travelers they meet.

subzone:plaguewood-tower.text:
Plaguewood Tower. Plaguewood Tower watches over the northern trails near Terrordale, its stones broken. Lordaeron kept a watchpost here until the Scourge invasion brought it to ruin. Plaguewood Tower's fractured stones overlook the northern trails between the Plaguewood and blighted Terrordale. The Kingdom of Lordaeron kept this post to guard the region.

When the Scourge swept across the land, the tower was battered into ruins among corrupted fungal canopies. Its broken walls still face the trails, the last remnant of Lordaeron's watch here.

subzone:pool-of-tears.text: Pool of Tears. In the eastern Swamp of Sorrows, the Pool of Tears surrounds a sunken temple. Frenzies patrol its murky waters, and troll ruins line its drowned banks. Atal'ai trolls raised a great ziggurat to Hakkar the Soulflayer, their bloodthirsty god. Ysera, the Dragon Aspect, was horrified by the blasphemies within. She broke the ground beneath the temple and sank it into the marsh. Water covered the ruins, but the ziggurat still lies beneath silt and lake water. Green drakes keep watch nearby, guarding against the corruption sealed below. Crossing the murky lake toward the sunken halls is perilous. Flesh-eating frenzies haunt the water, while Atal'ai artifacts and drowned stonework lie across the muddy floor. To reach the temple's upper passages, you must brave the hostile shallows. There, cultists and lingering dragon guardians struggle for control of the dark sanctuary.

subzone:purgation-isle.text: Purgation Isle. Condemned spirits haunt Purgation Isle, off Hillsbrad’s southern coast. Tombstones and a ruined watchtower mark its winding paths, where fallen humans and dwarves wander without peace. Purgation Isle rises from the sea south of Hillsbrad, its winding paths passing tombstones and an abandoned watchtower. No living nation claims the isle. Condemned souls roam among the graves. They were paladins, priests, mages, and judges, and death has brought them no peace. Dark spellcasters have taken an interest in the condemned souls of Purgation Isle. The ogre necromancer Kormok and others are said to delight in calling upon the anguished dead. They summon the spirits to do their bidding.

subzone:quagmire.text: Quagmire. In central Dustwallow Marsh, the Quagmire is a perilous stretch of fen. Brackenwall Village lies north and the Dragonmurk south. Waterlogged flats, hostile beasts, and ravenous oozes make crossing it dangerous. The Quagmire runs from Lost Point in the west to Dustwallow Bay in the east, through the marsh’s wild heart. Solid ground can give way to murky water and clinging mud without warning. Crocolisks wait beneath the scum, aggressive spiders nest in dead brush, and strange oozes seep through the muck. The Quagmire lies where sentient powers contest the swamp, an unpredictable crossing in their struggles. Tabetha's Farm stands in the bog as a lonely refuge. There, practitioners seek wisdom from a hermit amid the swamp’s dangers.

subzone:quel-lithien-lodge.text: Quel'Lithien Lodge. Farstrider rangers keep watch at Quel'Lithien Lodge, amid the blighted woods of the Eastern Plaguelands. The high elven hunting lodge stands among the northern hills near the entrance to Quel'Thalas. The Scourge surround it, and Forsaken agents hunt its rangers as they guard old elven archives. Before the Third War, Farstriders kept camp at Quel'Lithien on the road to Quel'Thalas. The lodge held records of the ranger order. Then the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and into the elven kingdom, and the lodge's fortunes worsened. Now its rangers watch over the corrupted forest. They are one of only two major concentrations of high elves left in Lordaeron.

subzone:rage-scar-hold.text: Rage Scar Hold. At Rage Scar Hold, savage yetis guard their cavern in Feralas, not far from Feathermoon Stronghold. Deeper inside, books, symbols, and night elven stonework point to an older purpose. Savage yetis attack anyone who comes near Rage Scar Hold. Alliance sentinels and travelers face danger on the forest trails because of them. Yetis roam Kalimdor’s wild reaches, but these beasts are especially aggressive. They fiercely defend their lair. Deeper in the cave, carved stonework and night elven architecture mark an older presence. Forgotten tomes and mystic symbols lie among dirt and bone. Did the yetis kill scholars here, or does lingering magic draw the beasts?

subzone:ragefire-chasm.text: Ragefire Chasm. In Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm threatens the Horde from below. Magma lights its tunnels, where savage troggs gather. The Cleft of Shadow opens onto the caverns. Ragefire troggs threaten Orgrimmar from below. While Thrall works to secure Durotar above, the troggs infest the chasm’s unstable vents and magma rivers. They rose from unknown depths and violently rejected Magatha Grimtotem’s attempts at diplomacy. Left unchecked, their numbers could undermine the city and overrun it.

subzone:raptor-ridge.text: Raptor Ridge. Razormaw raptors hunt the crags of Raptor Ridge in the eastern Wetlands, northwest of the Dragonmaw Gates. Their matriarch guards her brood deep in the caverns. Razormaw raptors hunt in packs along Raptor Ridge's rocky trails, high above the eastern Wetlands. Travelers near the foothills of Khaz Modan risk crossing their path. Deep in the ridge's central cavern, the Razormaw Matriarch guards her brood and nests from intruders. The Dragonmaw Gates lie close by.

subzone:ravaged-twilight-camp.text: Ravaged Twilight Camp. In the Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, Ravaged Twilight Camp lies broken and quiet. Highlord Demitrian remains there alone, devoted to the Windseeker. Twilight's Hammer keeps outposts across Silithus, yet its broken camp in the Crystal Vale is quiet and nearly deserted. Highlord Demitrian remains among the stones. He serves Thunderaan and broods over elemental bindings and the Windseeker's lost power, apart from the wider Twilight hierarchy.

subzone:ravencrest-monument.text:
Ravencrest Monument. On southern Azshara’s windswept cliffs, Ravencrest Monument lies broken above the Great Sea. Hostile Spitelash naga stalk the remains of the ancient night elven colossus. Southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, Ravencrest Monument rises above the ocean. The ancient colossus once showed the skill of Kaldorei stoneworkers. Now only its enormous legs remain, fixed to a stone base. Its torso and head lie in fragments, buried in the cliff dirt or lost beneath the waves.

To reach this remote coast, you must cross Azshara’s mainland bridges. Steep, rocky drops block any approach from the sea. Some scholars believe Ravencrest Monument honors Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest, the famed noble who rallied and led the night elven host after Zin-Azshari fell in the War of the Ancients. Its closeness to ancient Eldarath and the surviving stonework leave its origins uncertain.

Spitelash naga now claim the cliff. They defend the fallen monument with fierce aggression, where pilgrims or night elven caretakers once might have stood.

subzone:rebel-camp.text:
Rebel Camp. At Rebel Camp, Alliance soldiers hold a fortified refuge in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Lieutenant Doren leads those who broke from Colonel Kurzen and now fight to survive and end his tyranny. Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into Stranglethorn Vale on Stormwind's behalf. But the jungle turned against it. Dark magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth drove Kurzen and his closest loyalists mad. They went rogue and terrorized the wilds.

Lieutenant Doren led the handful who kept their minds. They refused to join the atrocities and broke from Kurzen's Compound before building a hidden camp in the north. From there, they wage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades. Near the Duskwood border, the Rebel Camp perches precariously under constant threat. Stormwind sends no regular relief, so Doren relies on covert supplies and defensive arms to hold the perimeter against Kurzen's raiding parties. Goblin explosives brokered through Booty Bay help fortify the camp.

For Alliance travelers heading south into the savage jungle, the camp is a vital first foothold of sanity.

subzone:refuge-pointe.text:
Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe holds its ground in the Arathi Highlands as Stromgarde's remnant prepares to reclaim its fallen keep. The camp guards the trade road at the highlands' heart while Alliance forces face rivals across the region. Stromgarde's surviving soldiers hold Refuge Pointe. After the Third War and the fall of Stromgarde Keep, most of the kingdom's people fled south for safer lands. Those who stayed formed a vanguard under Captain Nials. Battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers stand with League of Arathor forces and Alliance specialists. Together, they are the last organized Stromgarde force in its ancestral homeland. Refuge Pointe has no reserves to spare. The Forsaken and Horde hold Hammerfall, while Witherbark trolls, Syndicate rogues, and Boulderfist ogres press the garrison from other sides. When dwarven commanders at battered Thandol Span asked for help against the Dark Iron clan, Captain Nials had to refuse.

Every soldier and supply at Refuge Pointe must defend the highlands and prepare to retake Stromgarde Keep.

subzone:roguefeather-den.text: Roguefeather Den. In the southern cliffs of Thousand Needles, Roguefeather harpies guard their roost. Deep in the cavern, they keep scavenged provisions and stolen supplies. Among the sandstone bluffs of southern Thousand Needles, Roguefeather harpies guard their roost. Their screeching carries through the cavern as they defend the food and stolen supplies gathered in its dark recesses.

subzone:ruined-reaches.text:
Ruined Reaches. Along Azshara’s southern coast, the Ruined Reaches lie beneath the mainland cliffs. Wrecked ships and dangerous shallows mark the beaches, while predators haunt the surf and a small gnomish outpost watches from above. The Ruined Reaches stretch along southern Azshara, just north of Durotar. Rocky inlets and cliff faces break up the sand, where wreckage washes ashore. Like the Jagged Reef farther north, hidden shallows make sea travel perilous. Many ships have broken against this coast.

Hostile creatures roam both beach and water. Territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura make crossing the shore as dangerous as crossing the surf. A steep trail climbs from the beaches to a gnomish workshop high on the western cliff. Blimo and Jubie Gadgetspring keep the outpost, selling engineering components and general trade goods to travelers. An elevator leads up to private quarters with three beds. Who, if anyone, sleeps in the third bunk remains unknown.

subzone:ruins-of-aboraz.text: Ruins of Aboraz. Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls now hold the old Gurubashi terraces on Stranglethorn Vale's southeastern cliffs. At Aboraz, weathered stone crowns the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine. Zanzil the Outcast, an exiled witch doctor, has turned the courtyards into a place for alchemy. Banished by local tribes and mainlanders alike, he fled here to brew potions that alter the mind and toxic elixirs. His servants are shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and coastal naga under his control.

subzone:ruins-of-alterac.text:
Ruins of Alterac. Snow lies over the Ruins of Alterac, where Crushridge ogres now hold the old mountain capital. After King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Alliance in the Second War, Alterac was cast out and placed under martial law. Alterac once ruled as an independent human realm, carved from the old Arathor empire and set high on mountain trade routes. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde feared the invading Old Horde would destroy his kingdom, so he secretly made a pact with the orcs. After the fighting at Caer Darrow, the betrayal came to light. The Alliance of Lordaeron struck swiftly.

King Terenas Menethil II placed the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The people fled or turned to outlawry, and the grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair. Surviving Alteraci nobles and rogue soldiers formed the Syndicate. They waged guerrilla campaigns from towns like Strahnbrad, but lost their ancestral capital. Today, Crushridge ogres under Mug'thol dwell among broken ramparts, palace halls, and wrecked ballistae. Neither the Syndicate nor Southshore's human defenders have reclaimed the fallen city.

Its crumbling towers and abandoned vaults remain dangerous ground for treasure hunters and scavengers.

subzone:ruins-of-andorhal.text: Ruins of Andorhal. In the Western Plaguelands, Andorhal’s ruined streets belong to the Scourge. Once northern Lordaeron’s grain hub, the town now teems with undead abominations, ghouls, and wraiths under Araj the Summoner. Andorhal packed the Cult of the Damned’s tainted grain and sent it across the human kingdom. That grain began Lordaeron’s plague of undeath. Now the ruined city is a Scourge stronghold in the Western Plaguelands. Araj the Summoner holds its center, surrounded by ghouls, skeletal horrors, and towering flesh golems. Scarlet Crusade scouting parties sometimes probe the outskirts, but the Scourge rules the shattered streets.

subzone:ruins-of-constellas.text:
Ruins of Constellas. At Mount Hyjal’s roots, Jadefire satyrs hold the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood. Their fel magic has corrupted the settlement’s moonwell. Broken arches and crumbling plazas mark the night elf settlement that once stood at Constellas. The Burning Legion marched through Felwood during the Third War and shattered the haven. Demonic corruption followed. Now Jadefire satyrs hold the ruins.

Xavathras leads the satyrs as they tend the defiled moonwell. They turn its pure waters into fel power for their master, Lord Xavaric. Those who work to cleanse Felwood face a foul corruption at Constellas. Xavathras and his Jadefire satyrs guard their tents among the ruins. At the heart of the settlement lies the tainted moonwell. The satyrs fight to keep their work safe from anyone who would end it.

subzone:ruins-of-eldarath.text:
Ruins of Eldarath. Naga overrun the Ruins of Eldarath along Azshara’s rocky bluffs. Once a Highborne city of arcane study, its surviving plazas and temples still draw scholars and adventurers seeking ancient tablets and relics. Before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath flourished as a night elven city. Highborne mages gathered there and carved their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets.

They left the tablets in public squares for their peers to study. The Sundering sank much of the city into the Bay of Storms. Modern night elves have shunned the surviving ruins along the eastern cliffs for millennia, while salt spray and ivy slowly claim them. Vicious naga have risen from the sea and seized Eldarath’s shattered streets. Warlords command them from nearby sanctuaries, including the Temple of Zin-Malor. Yet danger has not kept outsiders away.

The Explorers' League sends Alliance adventurers into the broken courtyards to take rubbings of the ancient tablets. Whispers of lost treasures and lingering magic have also drawn the blue dragon Azuregos to the surrounding wilderness. Beneath the cracked flagstones, secrets of immense power may still lie buried.

subzone:ruins-of-isildien.text:
Ruins of Isildien. In southwestern Feralas, Gordunni ogres hold the overgrown Ruins of Isildien. The ancient night elven city fell during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Isildien once rose as a grand night elven settlement, before the world shattered. Marble arches and terraces showed the reach of kaldorei civilization and their devotion. Then the Well of Eternity imploded and tore the continents apart, leaving the city in ruins. Jungle growth covered its stones over the millennia.

A colossal dome crowns the upper terrace. It recalls Darnassus's Temple of the Moon and suggests Isildien held an important sanctuary dedicated to Elune. The Gordunni ogres have made Isildien's terraces and outcroppings one of their chief settlements in Feralas. They brace the crumbling walkways with bonfires, barricades, and war banners, defiling the ancient plazas. The ogres fiercely defend their stolen home from outsiders who venture too near the southern hills.

subzone:ruins-of-jubuwal.text:
Ruins of Jubuwal. East of the Gurubashi Arena, Zanzil the Outcast and his followers hold the Ruins of Jubuwal. The old Gurubashi settlement lies in ruins. Jubuwal once belonged to the great Gurubashi civilization. Stone carvings and ivy-covered walls remain beside Stranglethorn Vale’s main road. Now Zanzil the Outcast holds the ruins. The eccentric witch doctor is known for potent concoctions and foul voodoo.

His followers include enthralled ghouls, subjugated naga and renegade trolls. Desperate fugitives shelter beneath the stone arches too. Jon-Jon the Crow and Maury 'Club Foot' Wilkins hide here from 'Sea Wolf' MacKinley, the ruthless debt collector in Booty Bay.

subzone:ruins-of-kel-theril.text: Ruins of Kel'Theril. Snow and ice hold the broken stones of Ruins of Kel'Theril beside Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring. The ancient night elven city fell in the Great Sundering, and the spirits of its lost Highborne still haunt the ruins. Kel'Theril once stood among the great settlements of the ancient night elven empire. When the Well of Eternity collapsed in the Great Sundering, the city was blasted apart and buried beneath ice and snow. Its Highborne residents perished in the disaster, their souls bound to the stones. Now their spirits linger among the frostbitten arches, reliving their final moments. Along Lake Kel'Theril, restless Highborne spirits haunt the ruined colonnades. Many are hostile, driven mad by millennia of isolation and the violent magic that tore their civilization apart. A few, including the Remorseful Highborne, seek travelers willing to hear their laments and help them make peace with their forgotten past.

subzone:ruins-of-lordaeron.text:
Ruins of Lordaeron. At the Ruins of Lordaeron, the hollowed surface of Capital City guards the way into the Undercity. Once the heart of humanity’s northern empire, the city fell when Prince Arthas murdered his father and unleashed the Scourge. Capital City once united the northern realms under King Terenas Menethil II. Its splendor ended when Prince Arthas returned from Northrend with Frostmourne, the cursed runeblade. Celebration gave way to slaughter. Arthas slew his father on the throne, and the Scourge ruled the city as it rotted.

After civil war tore the Scourge apart, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner claimed the devastated palace. She secured the surface and expanded the crypts and dungeons below into the Undercity. The palace still bears the psychic wound of its violent fall. In the entryway and courtyards, travelers hear celebration bells, the murmurs of adoring crowds, and the chilling exchange between Arthas and his father before the regicide.

Blood still stains the grand throne room floor. Those with magical detection can glimpse spectral citizens reliving the afternoon their prince doomed them all.

subzone:ruins-of-ravenwind.text:
Ruins of Ravenwind. In northern Feralas, harpies nest among the Ruins of Ravenwind as dragonkin watch the broken stone. The marble once belonged to an ancient Highborne city. Before the Great Sundering, the Highborne ruled from Ravenwind at the height of their power. Like Dire Maul to the east, the kaldorei city was abandoned long ago.

Now foliage winds through broken arches and forgotten arcane altars. Northspring harpies roost there and prey on anything that wanders beneath the stone. Northspring harpies are not the only danger near Ravenwind. Fierce green dragonkin called the Jaedemir circle the central groves and waterways, guarding ancient arboreal sites.

Night elf explorers and solitary gnolls sometimes wander nearby. Lingering magic and wild predators can trap them among the ruins.

subzone:ruins-of-thaurissan.text:
Ruins of Thaurissan. Ash lies over the Ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes. The city once stood in the northern Redridge Mountains as the Dark Iron clan’s surface capital. During the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan called Ragnaros the Firelord, and the eruption reduced the city to cinders. After High King Modimus Anvilmar died, the Dark Iron clan was exiled from Ironforge. Roughly two centuries ago, they traveled south and founded Thaurissan City. During the War of the Three Hammers, the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans joined forces and brought the Dark Iron to the edge of defeat.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan sought a weapon to turn the tide. He and seven trusted sorcerers worked ancient magic deep beneath the earth. Their ritual did not summon an obedient servant. It tore open a path to the Elemental Plane and brought forth Ragnaros the Firelord. The eruption shattered the surrounding mountains, scorched the land into the Burning Steppes, raised Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the city.

subzone:ruins-of-uldum.text: Ruins of Uldum. In southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum guard a sealed Titan facility beneath the cliffs of the Valley of the Watchers. Stone doors keep grave robbers and curious explorers from its secrets. Deep in southern Tanaris, a grand stone threshold leads into the bedrock toward a sealed underground complex. Colossal gates block the way, and no mechanism or key known to modern scholars has opened them.

subzone:ruins-of-zul-mamwe.text: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe. Skullsplitter warriors hold the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe in central Stranglethorn Vale, south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. Cliffs ring the ancient stone platforms on nearly every side, and Ana'thek the Cruel rules the stronghold. In central Stranglethorn Vale, the Skullsplitters hold the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe as one of their chief seats of power. Mountains form a natural amphitheater around the site, open only to the north. From weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors. They defend their ground fiercely against intruders and rival jungle troll tribes. Zul'Mamwe's stones come from the ancient Gurubashi Empire, which once ruled the southern reaches of the continent without rival. The empire broke apart long ago into hostile factions. Among the overgrown masonry and broken monoliths, the Skullsplitters guard these ancestral stones and keep their age-old tribal rituals.

subzone:rustmaul-dig-site.text: Rustmaul Dig Site. Silithid swarm over Rustmaul Dig Site, a ruined camp in the southern Shimmering Flats. The Ironforge Explorers' League dug here for ancient ruins until Moktar Krin's Horde war party slaughtered the miners and a swarm rose from below. No mortals remain. Ironforge's Explorers' League sent prospectors to Rustmaul Dig Site, seeking forgotten artifacts beneath the salt flats. Their work ended when Moktar Krin led a fierce Horde war party against the camp and killed the dwarven excavators. Yet the attackers found no lasting victory. Their clash apparently disturbed a dormant cave network below, and silithid poured out. The battered survivors could not hold against the swarm and fled. Silithid now overrun Rustmaul, leaving the surface races with no hold there. Alien carapaces and skittering mandibles cover the mining gear and scaffolds. Frightened by the unceasing tide of insects from below, the survivors of Moktar Krin's war party fled north to Ironstone Camp.

subzone:saltspray-glen.text:
Saltspray Glen. Along Baradin Bay, salt winds sweep across Saltspray Glen, where wild raptors roam the lowland. The glen lies between murloc waters and ancient dwarven ruins. At the Wetlands' far northwest, salty spray blows inland from Baradin Bay across Saltspray Glen. Bluegill Marsh and its murloc-haunted waters lie to the south. To the east, the quiet bluffs of Ironbeard's Tomb rise above the lowland.

Cunning wild raptors nest in the marshy grass and hunt across the brackish flats. Their kin range nearby at Raptor Ridge and Black Channel Marsh, leaving little comfort for travelers passing through.

subzone:salty-sailor-tavern.text: Salty Sailor Tavern. In Booty Bay, travelers from both factions find shelter at the Salty Sailor Tavern. Goblin Innkeeper Skindle runs the port's inn and watering hole, where scoundrels and mercenaries seek respite from the jungle. Among Booty Bay's wooden tiers, the Salty Sailor Tavern offers warm beds and strong drinks. The Blackwater Raiders watch over the place. Innkeeper Skindle tends the bar as buccaneers, traders, and adventurers mingle on neutral ground. Outside hangs a massive Zul'Gurub Protector Stone, a curious trophy in this den of commerce.

subzone:sanctum-stromgarde-keep.text: Sanctum (Stromgarde Keep). Behind the chapel in Stromgarde Keep, the Sanctum remains a sacred refuge. It guards the way to the Trollbane family crypt amid Arathi's ruin. Syndicate infiltrators and Boulderfist ogres have taken much of Stromgarde Keep. Yet defenders still hold the Sanctum and the chapel beside it. Behind the Church of Light, the Sanctum borders the keep's graveyard and marks the way into the royal crypt, where Stromgarde's kings rest. Prince Galen Trollbane's loyalists defend this ground to protect their kingdom's ancestral heritage and faith from the invaders. Stone flags cover the passage into the royal tomb beneath the Sanctum. The ground is consecrated for quiet reflection and worship of the Holy Light. After King Thoras Trollbane's murder and Stromgarde's collapse, the Sanctum became a defensive retreat. Royal guards hold its halls against anyone seeking the inner tomb. At this sacred threshold, an ancient human lineage clings to survival.

subzone:sandsorrow-watch.text: Sandsorrow Watch. At Sandsorrow Watch, Sandfury trolls hold the desert ruins and dunes just west of Gadgetzan. Leave Gadgetzan through its western gate and you enter Sandfury territory almost at once. Trolls and shambling dead command the open desert, while an old watch tower rises at the eastern edge. Sandfury trolls hold even the eastern tower, within sight of Gadgetzan's walls. From its heights, they watch the goblin town. Travelers leaving through the western gate step onto a tense frontier, where settlers and sand trolls face one another.

subzone:sar-theris-strand.text: Sar'theris Strand. Along western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand's green shores meet the Veiled Sea. Its sunny grass stands apart from the grey wastes, though naga, sea giants, and makrura make the coast perilous. Green clifftops and beaches mark Sar'theris Strand along western Desolace. They offer a bright respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Serpentine naga patrol the surf beside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Wrecks mark the shoals: the ruined Karnitol vessel lies to the north, and small shattered skiffs rest beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor. The sea is as treacherous as the shore. Naga and sea giants are not the strand's only dangers. Jagged shallows hide salvage from lost expeditions and merchant ventures, while rare marine life dwells in the deep surf. Among it is the Sar'theris Striker, a fish sought by master fishermen across Kalimdor.

subzone:sardor-isle.text:
Sardor Isle. At feathermoon stronghold, night elves hold Sardor Isle against beasts and naga along its wild shores. The island guards Feralas's western coast, north of the Isle of Dread. Across the water from mainland Feralas, Sardor Isle is held by feathermoon stronghold, an elven garrison commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon. The fortress is heavily fortified, and a regular ferry links it to the mainland.

Beyond its walls, the island remains wild. Wolf packs roam the timbered slopes, while naga lurk along the rocky western and northern beaches, testing the night elven sentinels.

subzone:sargeron.text:
Sargeron. Hatefury satyrs hold Sargeron in northern Desolace, amid the ruins of an ancient night elf city. The city fell in the Great Sundering, and the satyrs defiled its temples of Elune before naming the ruins for their master, Sargeras. Sargeron once flourished around sacred grounds devoted to Elune. Before the War of the Ancients broke the continent, worshippers came to Elune's Temple, Sanctuary, and Cathedral. The city's true name is lost.

When the world shattered, Sargeron fell into rubble, leaving relics among the stones, including the Cup of Elune, Elune's Brazier, and Elune's Handmaiden. For millennia, corrupted Hatefury satyrs have overrun the ruins. They made Kaldorei holy places a stronghold in honor of the titan Sargeras.

subzone:savage-coast.text: Savage Coast. Along Stranglethorn Vale’s western shore, danger follows the Savage Coast from Westfall toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Crocolisks, basilisks, and hostile troll tribes make the beaches perilous. The Savage Coast follows the western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Its beaches run south from the cliffs by Westfall toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Crocolisks and stonestalkers roam among tide pools and drift logs, while territorial jungle troll camps threaten anyone walking the shore. Beyond the sand, the water deepens toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef.

subzone:scarab-dais.text: Scarab Dais. Northwest of the Scarab Wall, the Scarab Dais holds the Scarab Gong in southern Silithus. The gong is tied to the wards that seal the qiraji within Ahn'Qiraj. Before the Scarab Wall, the Scarab Dais overlooks the sands where Ahn'Qiraj was sealed a millennium ago. The Scarab Gong rests on its stone platform, forged during the War of the Shifting Sands. Ancient night elven history and the bronze dragonflight say only the reconstructed Scepter of the Shifting Sands can break the magical barrier when it strikes the gong. Until then, horrors remain sealed beyond the wall.

subzone:scarab-wall.text:
Scarab Wall. At Silithus's southern edge, the Scarab Wall bars the way to Ahn'Qiraj. Stone and bronze dragonflight sorcery keep the ancient swarms sealed beyond it, as they have since the War of the Shifting Sands. The Scarab Wall runs across the desert from east to west. It was raised a thousand years ago, after the War of the Shifting Sands. The qiraji nearly destroyed the night elf armies and their dragon allies before they drove the swarms back into their ancient kingdom.

To hold the qiraji there, the allies raised a great rampart of desert stone. The bronze dragonflight crowned it with a magical barrier. The wall cut the insectoid armies off from Kalimdor, yet their dread presence still hangs behind its stones.

subzone:scarlet-base-camp.text: Scarlet Base Camp. Scarlet forces hold a barricaded camp on Lake Mereldar’s eastern shore, just west of Tyr’s Hand. It marks an outer line of the Scarlet Crusade. On Lake Mereldar’s eastern shore, just west of Tyr’s Hand, the Scarlet Crusade holds a barricaded camp. It guards an outer line in the blighted countryside. Tyr’s Hand is one of the Scarlet Crusade’s strongholds in Lordaeron. Scarlet Base Camp guards its western approaches as the Crusade seeks to reclaim land from the undead. Outsiders are met with suspicion.

subzone:scarlet-basilica.text: Scarlet Basilica. At Tyr's Hand, Scarlet Basilica commands the Scarlet Crusade's eastern forces. Crusader Lord Valdelmar oversees the cathedral, a stronghold against the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands. At Tyr's Hand, Scarlet Basilica rises above the Eastern Plaguelands as the Scarlet Crusade's cathedral and command center. The Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades remains the order's spiritual heart, while the basilica anchors its surviving stronghold in Lordaeron. Elite crusaders guard its walls. Inside, Crusader Lord Valdelmar directs the local defense and drives away outsiders who approach.

subzone:scarlet-monastery.text: Scarlet Monastery. Scarlet Monastery now shelters the fanatical Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Once a center of learning and worship for the Church of the Holy Light, it is now a fortified stronghold. Anyone who approaches without red clothing is treated as a carrier of the plague and executed on sight. Before the Third War, Scarlet Monastery was a proud center of Lordaeron's priesthood. Its halls held theological studies and sacred archives, and paladins trained there. When the Scourge brought down the kingdom, defenders who survived held the monastery against the undead. They became the zealous Scarlet Crusade and fortified the cloister. Its libraries, gardens, and cathedral now lie within an armed stronghold. Scarlet Monastery has four wings: a defiled graveyard, an expansive library, an armory, and a grand cathedral. Scarlet Commander Mograine and High Inquisitor Whitemane command its large garrison. To the Crusaders, every outsider is a plague-bearer, living or undead, Alliance or Horde. The Forsaken seek to destroy the garrison threatening their doorstep. Alliance leaders increasingly see the Crusade's violent extremism as a dangerous corruption of the Light.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-armory.text: Scarlet Monastery Armory. Behind iron gates, recruits train and weapons are forged for the Scarlet Crusade in Scarlet Monastery Armory. Herod, the Scarlet Champion, commands the wing. The Scarlet Monastery once sheltered Lordaeron's peaceful priesthood. After the Third War, the Crusade remade the Armory into a forge, a weapons depot, and a proving ground. Scarlet footmen, conjurers, and crusaders train in its open yards and deep halls. They mean to purge the Scourge and all they judge tainted. The wing is sealed from the Grand Vestibule. Only those bearing the Scarlet Key from the neighboring Library may enter. Towering statues of the Scarlet Crusade's heroes fill the Hall of Champions. Herod, the Scarlet Champion, oversees the hall. The brutal warrior is famed among the crusaders for his ferocity and whirling attacks, and trains new zealots himself. When battle presses him hard, his recruits rush into the chamber to fight and die for their champion.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-cathedral.text: Scarlet Monastery Cathedral. Within Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, the Crusade keeps its inner sanctum and command seat. After the Third War, hatred took hold of the Cathedral. The Scourge destroyed Lordaeron, and its surviving zealots turned the complex from a peaceful place of prayer and learning into a stronghold. Beyond the Chapel Gardens stands the grand Crusader's Chapel. There, priests and warriors gather in devotion to their cause. They see every outsider, whatever their race or faction, as a bearer of the undead plague, to be purged by blade and holy fire.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-graveyard.text: Scarlet Monastery Graveyard. Undead haunt Scarlet Monastery Graveyard in northeastern Tirisfal Glades. Lordaeron's clergy and nobility once rested here in peace, but neglect and Bloodmage Thalnos's corrupted magic now trouble the burial wing. Before the Third War, Lordaeron's priests rested in peace in this cloistered cemetery. When the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the undead, its fanatical watch left the crypts uncleansed. Now the Graveyard lies neglected and haunted. Lingering spirits, restless corpses, and shambling horrors wander the Chamber of Atonement and the mist-covered Forlorn Cloister. Beneath the Crusade's uncaring gaze, the dead suffer endless torment instead of hallowed rest. At the rear of the grounds, Honor's Tomb holds Bloodmage Thalnos, who mocks the Crusade's dogma. No record tells who he was in life. The plague of undeath claimed him, and he rose as a skeletal horror wielding shadow bolts and fire. The crusaders above preach the total extermination of the undead plague. Yet a rotting, fallen sorcerer remains in their consecrated soil.

subzone:scarlet-monastery-library.text:
Scarlet Monastery Library. In Tirisfal Glades, scholars and mages seek Lordaeron's old religious and arcane records in the Scarlet Monastery Library. Crusade zealots and battle hounds patrol its halls. Before the Third War, Lordaeron's priesthood came to the monastery to study. Its eastern cloisters held religious writings, histories, and arcane treatises. Then the Scarlet Crusade fortified the monastery against the Scourge. They kept the archives and armed the quiet halls.

Now beastmasters send tracking hounds through the courtyards, while battle-mages patrol the shelves. They guard the Compendium of the Fallen and ancient Titan research from outsiders. Houndmaster Loksey guards the Huntsman's Cloister with trained hounds. They sniff out anyone seeking passage to the inner chambers. Beyond the Gallery of Treasures, Arcanist Doan watches over the Athenaeum.

A formidable mage, Doan wields devastating fire and protective sorcery. Doan studies alone and fiercely defends the Crusade's hoarded knowledge from anyone who enters the heart of the complex.

subzone:scholomance.text:
Scholomance. Beneath Caer Darrow, Scholomance trains mortals and undead in necromancy and the dark arts. Darkmaster Gandling leads the studies, while Ras Frostwhisper watches over the halls. Before the Third War, House Barov ruled from Caer Darrow and held vast lands across Lordaeron. Those lands included Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore. Fearing the loss of their wealth and mortal lives, the Barovs accepted Kel'Thuzad's promise of eternal life.

They deeded their fortress and ancestral catacombs to the Cult of the Damned. The cult repaid them by butchering the nobles and turning the crypts into a hidden place to train necromancers.

subzone:scholomance-classic.text:
Scholomance (Classic). In the Western Plaguelands, Scholomance trains mortal spellcasters in the Scourge's arts. The academy lies beneath Caer Darrow, hidden in the crypts of the island fortress. Before the Third War laid Lordaeron waste, the rogue archmage Kel'Thuzad sought recruits for his Cult of the Damned. The wealthy Barov family ruled Caer Darrow and became willing benefactors. They traded their lands and crypts for promised immortality. The cult instead slaughtered them and raised them as monstrous undead.

Beneath the ruined fortress, the cult remade the ancient Arathorian catacombs into a school for the dark arts. Mortal acolytes study plaguecraft, soul binding, and flesh shaping beyond watchful eyes. There, they hone the foul magic that shattered Lordaeron. Kel'Thuzad now directs Scourge operations from above, but Scholomance remains active. The eternal lich Ras Frostwhisper watches over the complex in the Scourge's name. The mortal necromancer Darkmaster Gandling leads the school and tutors ambitious sorcerers through horrific experiments.

Students who show weakness are cast into the catacombs. In the lower vaults, the voracious wight Ravenian lurks, ready to feed on them.

subzone:sea-of-cinders.text: Sea of Cinders. Ash and embers sweep the Sea of Cinders, north of Blackrock Mountain. Ash and burning grit sweep the plain between the Searing Gorge cliffs and Blackrock Mountain. Centuries ago, the Firelord Ragnaros was summoned into the mortal world. The upheaval fractured the Redridge Mountains and left the surrounding land an arid slag heap. The Sea of Cinders is one of the cataclysm’s most barren remnants, where the earth never cools. Travelers and scavengers taking the north approach to Blackrock Mountain often cross these scorching flats. Winds drive blinding ash clouds across the way, hiding sudden fissures, elemental horrors, and predators adapted to the heat. Dark Iron dwarves claim this hostile land. Anyone crossing the cinders must stay watchful and move swiftly.

subzone:sentry-point.text: Sentry Point. At Sentry Point, Theramore's forces watch the causeway to their island citadel. From the mainland edge of Dustwallow Marsh, the human watchtower overlooks traffic in both directions. Sentry Point guards the western end of the bridge between Theramore Isle and Dustwallow Marsh. From its stone scout tower, Theramore's forces watch the swamp road. They guard the mainland approach to the island city and watch for marsh beasts and Horde raiders.

subzone:serpent-s-coil.text: Serpent's Coil. Dark cultists shelter in Serpent's Coil, among caves and burnt encampments in the eastern Blasted Lands. Scorched orcish ruins from older wars line the ridges. In the eastern Blasted Lands, Serpent's Coil winds through cliffs and old ruins. Its paths pass ruined orcish huts from the First and Second Wars. Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts haunt the tunnels. Demonic energies lingering in the red wastes draw them there, beyond the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

subzone:shadow-hold.text: Shadow Hold. In the depths of Jaedenar, the Shadow Council holds Shadow Hold as its chief stronghold on Kalimdor. The cult rules from a defiled night elf barrow den beneath Felwood's blighted canyon. Beneath Jaedenar's corrupted red earth, Shadow Hold's corridors wind through an ancient night elf barrow den. Druids once slept here while tending the Emerald Dream. Now warlocks and demonic servants stalk its twisted passages by fel fire. Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan command a formidable force in the deepest tiers. From here, demonic power holds its chief seat in the region.

subzone:shadowbreak-ravine.text: Shadowbreak Ravine. Burning Blade cultists and demons gather in Shadowbreak Ravine, southeast of Magram Village. Among barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, the ravine stays hidden from wandering centaur tribes. Strange oversized mushrooms rise beside grim ritual camps, where cultists work with summoned demons. Dark practitioners call on fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains. Here, the Burning Blade gathers reinforcements and holds a demonic foothold in Desolace.

subzone:shadowfang-keep.text:
Shadowfang Keep. Above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep broods over southern Silverpine Forest. Once Silverlaine Keep, it fell to worgen summoned during the Third War. Now Archmage Arugal holds its halls, haunted by slain nobles and overrun by wolf-beasts. Before the Third War, Baron Silverlaine ruled Pyrewood Village from his ancestral seat, Silverlaine Keep. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Archmage Arugal used Dalaran mage Ur's dimensional research to summon worgen from beyond this world. The beasts tore through the Scourge, then escaped his control.

They rampaged across southern Silverpine and besieged the keep. The worgen killed Baron Silverlaine, his family, and the defenders under Commander Springvale. Guilt and grief broke Arugal's sanity. He claimed the fortress, renamed it Shadowfang Keep, and called the monstrous predators his children. Shadowfang Keep is the heart of a growing wolf curse in Silverpine Forest. Arugal dwells in the highest observatory, surrounded by ravenous worgen of the Moonrage and Shadowfang packs. Sinister beasts prowl the keep too, including his massive pet wolf, Fenrus.

Below Arugal's sanctum, the restless ghosts of the keep's former lords and household remain trapped in torment. Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale are among them, cursed to defend the halls they failed to protect in life. From the walls, Arugal's influence reaches Pyrewood Village and the surrounding woodlands. His madness threatens neighboring Forsaken who seek to purge the forest.

subzone:shadowprey-village.text:
Shadowprey Village. Along Sar'theris Strand, Darkspear fishermen and tauren keep Shadowprey Village alive as a Horde port on Desolace's rocky southern coast. Their work sustains trade across the barren region. On Desolace's southern shore, Shadowprey Village clings to cliffs where centaur clans and the wastes leave few safe harbors. Troll fishermen make up most of the settlement. Their catches feed the village and inland posts such as Ghost Walker Post.

Wooden piers reach into the rough sea. From them, anglers fish deep water and dive for shellfish among the wrecks scattered along Sar'theris Strand. A port on Desolace's frontier faces danger from land and sea. Marauding centaur and the demon-summoning Burning Blade threaten from inland. Rough shoals and hungry sea life challenge those who fish the coast.

Tauren allies help defend the village and keep trade routes open across Kalimdor. They include Taiga Wisemane and the keepers of the inn and wind rider roost.

subzone:shadowsong-shrine.text:
Shadowsong Shrine. In western Azshara, Shadowsong Shrine lies in haunted ruin near the Ashenvale border. Ancient Highborne spirits haunt the hillside sanctuary. Its name recalls Maiev Shadowsong, though its tie to her bloodline remains a mystery. Shadowsong Shrine crowns a hill above Azshara’s shattered lands, its stones lost beneath overgrowth. Highborne ghosts wander the ruins and try to kill mortals who enter their domain.

The shrine bears the name of Maiev Shadowsong, the warden of Illidan Stormrage. Time has erased whether it honors her family or predates the Sundering.

subzone:shady-rest-inn.text: Shady Rest Inn. At the Shady Rest Inn, smoke and blackened beams mark the place where travelers once stopped between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Fire left the inn in ruins and its keeper shattered. Theramore's investigators search the wreckage for clues. Travelers once found shelter at the Shady Rest Inn between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens. Then a sudden fire burned it to the ground. Innkeeper James Hyal survived, but his wife and child died in the blaze. Grief and trauma have left him with nothing. Now Theramore's authorities search the ruins for whoever lit the fire.

subzone:shalzaru-s-lair.text: Shalzaru's Lair. Hatecrest naga gather at Shalzaru's Lair on the Isle of Dread's northern tip. Their master directs them from flooded caverns south of Feathermoon Stronghold. At the Isle of Dread's northern end, the bluffs open into Shalzaru's Lair. A broad cavern and a smaller chamber join through submerged waterways. Hatecrest serpent guards patrol the dry paths, while sorceresses weave magic across the water. Deep within, Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest brood across the island. The lair lies close to Sardor Isle, across the channel from the night elf Sentinels at Feathermoon Stronghold.

subzone:shaper-s-terrace.text:
Shaper's Terrace. High above Marshal's Refuge, Shaper's Terrace bears the mark of the ancient titans. Its overlook honors Khaz'goroth the Shaper and recalls the experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. From the northern bluffs, Shaper's Terrace looks across Un'Goro Crater. Monumental stone works left by the titans crown the high plateau. The site is believed to honor Khaz'goroth the Shaper, one of the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth.

From these heights, ancient entities once watched and directed the flora and fauna below. Stone arches and massive metallic plinths still rise above the wilderness thriving beneath them.

subzone:shatter-scar-vale.text:
Shatter Scar Vale. Fel fire still burns in Shatter Scar Vale, north of Bloodvenom Falls in central Felwood. The vale bears the marks of the infernals that struck northern Kalimdor during the Third War, and demons remain among the craters. During the Third War, the Burning Legion sent living siege engines against northern Kalimdor. Shatter Scar Vale bore the force of that assault. Demonic infernals fell from the sky, breaking through the ancient canopy and striking deep into the earth. Their blows shattered the ground and left blackened hollows that still smolder with unholy fire.

The Legion was broken at Mount Hyjal, but the infernals and lesser demons did not disperse. They remain entrenched in the scarred earth.

subzone:shattered-strand.text: Shattered Strand. Waves batter Shattered Strand along Azshara’s northern coast, where ancient ruins overlook the shore. Sea beasts and aquatic tribes prowl the shallows. The Shattered Strand runs along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms. Rocky beaches and tidal shallows teem with danger. Sea giants, hydras, and snapping makrura roam beside coastal murloc camps. Ruined elven buildings overlook the waves, including the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the lone Tower of Eldara. Travelers who descend Azshara’s cliffs reach an isolated coast held by deadly amphibious creatures.

subzone:shifting-mire.text: Shifting Mire. In the Swamp of Sorrows, the Shifting Mire spreads west of the Pool of Tears. Beneath its murky water, strange silt drifts and gathers under an unseen force. The Shifting Mire covers the swamp’s central reaches, where firm ground is scarce. Along the bog floor, fine silt shifts and gathers under a strange energy in the peat. Predators prowl the drifting mud: swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks. Bands of broken draenei called the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

subzone:slag-pit.text: Slag Pit. In the Cauldron, the Slag Pit drives the Dark Iron dwarves’ mining. Slavers force workers through the tunnels while incendosaurs prowl below. The Slag Pit cuts into the Cauldron, where Dark Iron dwarves force enslaved workers to mine ore and minerals. Overseers and taskmasters keep them digging day and night. Beneath Blackrock Mountain, the tunnels feed supply lines to Blackrock Depths. The Dark Irons guard those lines against anyone who interferes. Below, the tunnels open into scorching caverns where incendosaurs roam. These fierce reptiles threaten workers and intruders alike. Still, the Dark Iron masters drive their laborers deeper into the rock, heedless of the lives lost.

subzone:slaughter-hollow.text: Slaughter Hollow. Crushridge ogres keep to Slaughter Hollow in the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains. Travelers come rarely, usually to hunt ogres or cross the frozen passes. High in the peaks between Hillsbrad and Alterac, Slaughter Hollow shelters the Crushridge ogres. Makeshift fires, scattered bones, and crude shelters mark their mound. Other ogre dens in the highlands often see fights over territory or stolen supplies. Slaughter Hollow stays quiet, beyond the reach of major military campaigns. Crushridge ogres sometimes hold prisoners taken along the mountain trails in their secluded mound. Travelers speak of Rizz Loosebolt, an unlucky gnome locked in a crude cage who tries to bargain with anyone passing by. Captives seldom fare well against the clan's appetite.

subzone:slither-rock.text:
Slither Rock. Cyrus Therepentous keeps to Slither Rock in the far northeastern cliffs of the Burning Steppes. Beyond the perilous Terror Wing Path, the cave is his solitary refuge, and his sharp tongue masks an agenda of his own. Beyond the Terror Wing Path, Slither Rock lies among the scorched crags of the Burning Steppes. Far from Blackrock Spire's roaring forges and marching orc warbands, this remote hollow shelters Cyrus Therepentous, a solitary black dragonspawn.

Dragonspawn usually serve the Black Dragonflight with fierce loyalty, but Cyrus keeps apart from his kin. He speaks with mortal travelers instead of killing them on sight. Yet every exchange brings an insult.

subzone:slithering-scar.text:
Slithering Scar. In southern Un'Goro, the Gorishi swarm presses into the crater. Their hive tunnels through the cliffs and threatens life in the basin. In southern Un'Goro, the Gorishi hive cuts into the cliffs. This organized strain of silithid has burrows and egg chambers through the rock. Workers and tunnelers tend eggs and grubs, while towering wasp broods fill the warrens below.

The colony also raises fledgling silithid colossi, behemoths meant to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystals pulse inside the hive with an unnatural resonance, focusing the colony's dark, coordinated will. Scholars and explorers crossing Un'Goro's perimeter find no ancient crystalline pylon on its southern boundary. Pylons stand sentinel along the basin's northern, eastern, and western edges. Through this unprotected gap, the Gorishi have burrowed inward from the neighboring deserts.

Did the silithid undermine a forgotten southern ward, or enter where the crater's primordial wards were weakest? Those watching the swarm's rapid expansion have no answer.

subzone:sorrow-hill.text:
Sorrow Hill. At Sorrow Hill, the dead rise beneath headstones south of Andorhal. Plague cauldrons have corrupted the old burial ground, and its dead roam again. Before the Third War, Sorrow Hill received the dead of Andorhal and the nearby townships. When the Scourge brought the Plague of Undeath, the gravediggers could not keep pace. Shallow, poorly marked pits spread around the cemetery’s neat crypts.

Terrified survivors abandoned the old rites and burned their loved ones on a great pyre to the south. They feared the dead would rise. Before Andorhal fell completely, those who remained entombed Lord Uther the Lightbringer on the hill’s high ground. His burial gave the hill its sorrowful name. Plague cauldrons across the region have corrupted Sorrow Hill. Soldiers and citizens buried here now roam among the headstones as skeletal flayers and ravenous ghouls. Skeletal mages and a Scourge commander hold the crypts in the southeast.

The cemetery lies on the road between Chillwind Camp and Andorhal. The Alliance and the Argent Dawn send patrols to cut down the undead and hold their foothold in the region.

subzone:sorrowmurk.text: Sorrowmurk. Green dragonkin guard the way to the Sunken Temple in Sorrowmurk. East of the Pool of Tears, this wetland remains one of the most perilous reaches of the eastern marshes. Along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, you reach Sorrowmurk where the mire meets the Forbidding Sea. Green dragonspawn and towering drakes patrol its waters and tangled boughs. They are remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence makes these sodden reaches perilous for any traveler.

subzone:south-seas.text:
South Seas. Merchant ships and pirate crews contend across the South Seas, between southern Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale border these tropical waters, where reefs and other dangers threaten every voyage. The South Seas stretch south from the Great Sea and the Maelstrom, washing against Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale. The Great Sundering shattered the primeval continent ten thousand years ago, leaving remote tropical islands and waters rich with ocean life.

Independent merchant networks cross these seas. Goblin shipping cartels work from havens such as Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay to keep the lanes open. Corsairs and Bloodsail buccaneers prey on passing ships, while dangerous sea life threatens vessels far from shore. Beyond the coastal trade lanes lie legendary islands and dangers beneath the waves. Zandalar, the ancient troll island, and the produce-rich shores of Tel'Abim are scattered across the South Seas. Cutthroats are not the only danger: giant squids, primeval sea turtles, and naga haunt the deeper waters. The naga guard ancient ruins swallowed by the waves. Captains need experience, reliable charts, and substantial firepower to cross these seas.

subzone:southern-savage-coast.text: Southern Savage Coast. Along the Southern Savage Coast, jungle opens onto beaches and South Seas waters. Travelers face danger from wildlife, naga, and raiders. The Southern Savage Coast follows the western edge of southern Stranglethorn. Warm South Seas currents meet the mainland, and the Vile Reef with its submerged ruins divides this shore from the northern Savage Coast. Inlets lie near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring; the coast then runs past Booty Bay to Janeiro's Point. The beaches give you more room than the jungle, but reptilian predators prowl the sand, naga hunt in the shallows, and corsairs watch for easy prey.

subzone:southfury-river.text: Southfury River. Mount Hyjal's waters run south through central Kalimdor in the Southfury River. Along the way, the river divides Azshara from Ashenvale and Durotar from the Barrens, then reaches the Great Sea near Ratchet. The Southfury River starts high on Mount Hyjal and rushes through central Kalimdor. Its waters divide Ashenvale from Azshara, then Durotar from the Barrens. Only a few bridges cross its swift current. One guards Orgrimmar's rear gates, while another links Durotar to the Barrens. Near Ratchet, the river plunges over a waterfall into the Great Sea. The Southfury gives the Horde a barrier and a route through the region. It shields Durotar's western approaches, including Orgrimmar, from immediate ground assault. Its waters also carry fresh mountain runoff through dry country. Just north of the western crossing into Orgrimmar, Ashenvale, Azshara, Durotar, and the Barrens meet. Holding the river keeps supply lines between Orgrimmar and outlying Horde settlements intact.

subzone:southmoon-ruins.text: Southmoon Ruins. Dunemaul ogres camp among the Southmoon Ruins in southern Tanaris, north of the Valley of the Watchers. Their stones preserve the remains of an ancient troll civilization that once ruled the desert. Weathered pillars and altars rise from the sands at Southmoon in southern Tanaris. Nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade share their age, their stones worn by thousands of years of wind and grit. Dunemaul ogres have often camped among these old structures. They claim the stones for shelter and territory, with little regard for the craft that shaped them. Southmoon’s stones are unmistakably trollish, though little is recorded of who raised them or why they left. Whatever remains lies beneath the drifting sand. The Dunemaul ogres camp among the pillars without concern for it.

subzone:southpoint-tower.text: Southpoint Tower. Forsaken scouts watch the Alliance from Southpoint Tower, near Hillsbrad's western edge. The ruined Lordaeron post overlooks the road into Silverpine Forest. Southpoint Tower overlooks the highway between Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills. The Kingdom of Lordaeron built it to guard the way between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. After the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Now the tower is roofless and crumbling, a remnant of human rule in fractured lands. Forsaken agents watch Alliance patrols from the ruined tower. Deathstalker Lesh is stationed there, watching nearby human settlements in Hillsbrad Fields and travelers on the main road. Though its walls have fallen, the tower's vantage remains valuable. So near hostile territory, this lonely post often becomes a flashpoint for skirmishes.

subzone:southridge-beach.text: Southridge Beach. Along Azshara’s southern coast, Southridge Beach borders the turbulent Bay of Storms. Its broken ruins now shelter naga, murlocs, and towering sea giants. On Southridge Beach, the southern shore meets the turbulent Bay of Storms. Thousands of years ago, this coast belonged to Eldarath, a magnificent Highborne city. The Great Sundering broke the land and drowned most of its palaces. Crumbling marble pillars and weathered stone pavilions still dot the sand. Spitelash naga, prowling makrura, vicious hydras, and scavenging murloc tribes now contest the shore. Even massive sea giants sometimes wander ashore from the deep.

subzone:southshore-town-hall.text: Southshore Town Hall. At Southshore Town Hall, Magistrate Henry Maleb directs the town’s affairs and defenses. It is one of Lordaeron’s last centers of civil authority as the Alliance struggles to hold ground in the plagued north. Southshore Town Hall keeps human rule alive amid Lordaeron’s ruin. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from his office and works with officials such as Kundric Zanden to secure supplies and keep order. Undead press from nearby lands, Syndicate rogues threaten the region, and fierce skirmishes mark Hillsbrad’s border. From the hall, town leaders guide Southshore’s fight to survive.

subzone:southwind-village.text: Southwind Village. In Southwind Village, fallen defenders haunt the ruins beneath Silithus’s sands. The qiraji destroyed the night elf outpost during the War of the Shifting Sands, and silithid still prowl the dunes.
