During the War of the Shifting Sands, a thousand years ago, Southwind Village held a night elf stronghold. When qiraji legions broke through its defenses, Valstann Staghelm led a detachment to hold the village. He was the son of Archdruid Fandral Staghelm. The defenders were overwhelmed and slaughtered, and General Rajaxx dragged Valstann away into captivity. The village lay in ruins, its buildings fractured beneath the sun. A thousand years after the fall, Southwind Village still bears the marks of the assault. The slain night elf Sentinels and druids could not move on. Driven mad by the horror of their final moments, their spirits roam the crumbled stone walls without end, led by the Shade of Ambermoon. They lash out at anyone who enters, while predatory silithid swarm across the surrounding dunes.

subzone:splinterspear-junction.text:
Splinterspear Junction. Horde sentries hold Splinterspear Junction where the Swamp of Sorrows road forks. North lies the Harborage and Fallow Sanctuary; south, the road passes Stonard toward the Blasted Lands. At Splinterspear Junction, the road through the Swamp of Sorrows divides. The northern trail leads toward the Lost One refuge of the Harborage and the Fallow Sanctuary. South, the road passes Stonard on its way to the Blasted Lands.

An ancient orcish watchtower overlooks the fork. Horde troops hold it and patrol the roads. For Horde travelers, the tower offers a secure point in a treacherous marsh. For Alliance travelers, it is a deadly ambush on an unforgiving trail.

subzone:stagalbog.text: Stagalbog. Along the southern mountains, Stagalbog remains an untamed stretch of marsh, south of the Pool of Tears. Below the southern crags, stagnant water gathers among drooping reeds and tangled growth. The tainted Pool of Tears borders Stagalbog to the north, with the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar just beyond. Rough wildlife roams the mire, where civilization has made no foothold. Beside the Pool of Tears, Stagalbog lies under the shadows and corruption seeping from the Sunken Temple.

subzone:stagalbog-cave.text: Stagalbog Cave. Marsh murlocs shelter in Stagalbog Cave, deep in the eastern Swamp of Sorrows. In the eastern Swamp of Sorrows, the Marsh murlocs shelter from the rain in Stagalbog Cave. They guard its winding chambers under their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog, their gurgling calls cross the mossy banks and warn travelers away from their nesting grounds.

subzone:staghelm-point.text: Staghelm Point. In northeastern Silithus, Staghelm Point keeps watch over the desert and Twilight's Run. Its ancient night elf tower looks over encroaching dunes, while old threats linger in nearby caverns. Staghelm Point rises above the dry flats of northeastern Silithus. A lone night elf tower keeps watch over the wasteland, with cultists in nearby caves such as Twilight's Run. Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher guards the outpost, and a bronze drake circles overhead. The tower bears the Staghelm name, recalling the great sacrifices the Kaldorei made during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands.

subzone:starfall-village.text: Starfall Village. Night elves shelter travelers at Starfall Village, the Alliance outpost on Winterspring’s snowy road. It offers supplies in the frozen valley and watches over a nearby barrow den. Northwest of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock, Starfall Village gives wayfarers shelter in Winterspring’s harsh mountain cold. Its timber lodges offer supplies and a warm hearth. The village is the Alliance’s only outpost in the valley, and a quiet barrow den nearby stands empty.

subzone:steamwheedle-port.text: Steamwheedle Port. Steamwheedle Port keeps Gadgetzan linked to the eastern shore of Tanaris. The neutral Steamwheedle Cartel runs its docks and holds open a sea route across the South Seas, though Southsea Pirates press nearby. On Tanaris's eastern shore, the docks give Gadgetzan a direct route to maritime trade. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs the settlement, where dockhands, traders, and sea captains face treacherous waters. Supply vessels sail between the port and distant goblin trading posts, bringing mechanical components, luxuries, and raw materials into southern Kalimdor. Southsea Freebooters raid goblin shipping from Lost Rigger Cove, just south along the coast. They steal cargo and contest control of the shoreline, while dockworkers haggle and merchants seek to recover stolen shipments. The port also shelters unusual travelers. Among them is Yeh'kinya, a troll scholar studying the world's ancient and ominous spirits away from prying eyes.

subzone:stonard.text: Stonard. In the southern Swamp of Sorrows, Stonard holds a fortified Horde foothold. The outpost dates to the First War and watches the Blasted Lands from the marsh. Stonard began as an Old Horde post in the marsh beyond the Dark Portal. When the invaders crossed into what was then the Black Morass, Stonard and Rockard anchored their lines. Both posts were damaged and abandoned after the Second War. Thrall's New Horde rebuilt Stonard and placed a garrison there. Its Great Hall and fortified burrows now hold a Horde presence amid the dangerous swamp. Scouts and cartographers range from Stonard into the surrounding swamp. They chart its waters and watch for hostile beasts, lost draenei wanderers, and the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar to the east. North of the shattered Blasted Lands, the outpost also gives the Horde a staging ground. The dormant Dark Portal remains under watch.

subzone:stonemaul-ruins.text:
Stonemaul Ruins. Firemane dragonspawn hold Stonemaul Ruins, the old home of the Stonemaul ogres. Driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north and left its village to the brood. Stonemaul Village rose in the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh after the ogres came to Kalimdor. The beastmaster Rexxar won their respect by surviving the clan's deadly trials, killing their chieftain Kor'gall, and rallying the ogres to defend the young Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces.

After the war, Rexxar left Mok'Morokk in command. But the ogre ruled for himself, and the village fell. Then the black dragonflight ambushed and shattered it. The survivors fled north and founded Brackenwall Village. Onyxia's brood claimed the ruins. Firemane dragonspawn now infest the ruins in Dragonmurk and tend the brood's nearby nesting grounds. Overlord Mok'Morokk has grown cowardly and is content to remain in Brackenwall. Older, prouder clan members Tharg and Draz'Zilb refuse to give up their homeland. From Brackenwall, they urge Horde champions to kill the dragonspawn and smash the dragonflight's eggs. They hope the Stonemaul will march back and reclaim their ancestral village.

subzone:stonewrought-pass.text: Stonewrought Pass. Iron gates bar Stonewrought Pass between Loch Modan and Searing Gorge. Franclorn Forgewright cut the tunnel through the southern mountains, joining the Valley of Kings to Dustfire Valley and shielding dwarven lands from the volcanic dangers beyond. Franclorn Forgewright carved Stonewrought Pass through the bedrock. The master architect also built the massive Stonewrought Dam. The tunnel runs from Loch Modan near the Valley of Kings, through the mountain ridge, and down into Dustfire Valley. Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts threaten travelers in Searing Gorge. So the Ironforge mountaineers keep heavy gates locked at both ends, guarding the way north into Loch Modan.

subzone:stormrage-barrow-dens.text: Stormrage Barrow Dens. Beneath Moonglade, druids sleep in the Stormrage Barrow Dens. Their bodies rest here while their spirits journey through the Emerald Dream. Beneath Moonglade, the Stormrage Barrow Dens hold druids in deep sleep. Barrow dens across night elven lands guard their bodies while their spirits journey through the Emerald Dream. These earthen halls bear the name of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage. Clintar Dreamwalker still sleeps in one of their alcoves. Malfurion is absent, and his brethren keep watch over the quiet chambers. The Stormrage Barrow Dens nearly fell during the Third War. Tichondrius and the Burning Legion sought to destroy the sleeping druids before they could rally. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind fought demons and corrupted wildlife in the tunnels, then sounded the Horn of Cenarius. The call woke Malfurion Stormrage in time. After Archimonde fell at Mount Hyjal, Malfurion's spirit returned to the Emerald Dream. His brethren still watch over the dens.

subzone:stormwind-city.text:
Stormwind City. Stormwind City leads the Kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance from its seat of power. Rebuilt after the First War, it is Azeroth's greatest remaining human stronghold since the northern kingdoms fell. Stormwind City rose over a thousand years ago, founded by Arathi descendants who migrated south. Its coastal ramparts sheltered a flourishing capital, where swift rivermills powered the city. In the First War, the Orcish Horde broke through its defenses and burned Stormwind to the ground.

Sir Anduin Lothar led the surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Alliance won the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt the capital with white stone, canals and towering spires. The fortress now stands north of Elwynn Forest. Stormwind City is mankind's chief refuge and stronghold after the Scourge shattered Lordaeron and the Third War left Dalaran heavily ruined. The disciplined Stormwind City Guard patrols its broad avenues and defensive walls. The Cathedral of Light's spires guide faith across the southern kingdoms.

Yet political troubles linger beneath the orderly districts and ceremonial gates. King Varian Wrynn has mysteriously vanished, and his young son Anduin sits on the throne. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs as regent, with the whispered counsel of royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor.

subzone:stratholme.text:
Stratholme. Scourge forces hold Stratholme, and its ruins still burn. Once the jewel of the Eastweald and Lordaeron’s second greatest city, it became the place where Prince Arthas Menethil ordered the culling of citizens who had eaten grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath. Stratholme rose with the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald centuries ago. It became Lordaeron’s second-largest settlement, famed for holy shrines and sacred water that resisted dark sorcery. Before the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city’s chapel and founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand.

Among its first legends was Uther the Lightbringer. During the Second War, Stratholme served the Alliance of Lordaeron as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery. The Old Horde assaulted it, but victory brought the city’s rebuilding. The Cult of the Damned carried infected grain from Andorhal into Stratholme’s markets. Unaware of the taint, thousands ate the flour. Prince Arthas arrived with Uther and Jaina Proudmoore, but the infection had spread too far to cure.

He judged slaughter the only way to deny Mal'Ganis an entire army and ordered every citizen killed. The atrocity drove Uther and Jaina away and began the prince’s descent into madness. His forces set the city ablaze. Then the Scourge took its smoking ruins for their regional capital.

subzone:stratholme-classic.text:
Stratholme (Classic). Scourge and Scarlet Crusade forces fight through Stratholme's burning ruins. Once northern Lordaeron's jewel and the birthplace of the Silver Hand, the city now lies divided between them. Stratholme once held great power in northern Lordaeron and gave birth to the Knights of the Silver Hand. During the Third War, Prince Arthas purged the city after infected grain carried plague through its gates. He slaughtered his own subjects. The city smoldered in ruins, then the Scourge claimed it.

Kel'Thuzad holds overarching authority, while Baron Rivendare commands the undead forces in the field. From Stratholme, they direct Scourge power across the Plaguelands. Two vicious factions wage an unending war through Stratholme. In the west, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade holds Crusaders' Square and the Scarlet Bastion under Grand Crusader Saidan Dathrohan. In the east, Scourge slaughterhouses and necropolises stand behind towering ziggurats. The death knight Baron Rivendare guards them.

Burning tenements and restless spirits surround anyone who enters. Across the city, both sides trade blows.

subzone:stratholme-main-gate.text: Stratholme Main Gate. Ruined avenues beyond Stratholme Main Gate lead toward King’s Square and the Scarlet Bastion. The gate stands in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands, at the entrance to Lordaeron’s northern metropolis. Stratholme was once northern Lordaeron’s pride and the birthplace of the Order of the Silver Hand. Its great arched gates now mark the edge of a nightmare begun during the Third War. Here, Prince Arthas turned against his mentor, Uther the Lightbringer. He purged his own citizens before the Plague of Undeath could claim them. The city has burned ever since and is now the region’s chief Scourge stronghold. Beyond the main gate, the road passes through the ruins of King’s Square and Market Row toward the fortified Scarlet Bastion. Scarlet Crusade zealots entered here to reclaim the city and purge the dead, then made an encampment in the ruins. Overwhelming undead surround them. The crusaders fight an attrition war against the dark forces directing Stratholme’s defense, and they cannot win.

subzone:stratholme-service-entrance.text: Stratholme Service Entrance. At Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands, the Scourge holds Stratholme's eastern quarter. The Service Entrance cuts through the city's fortified wall. Stratholme's Main Gate opens into King's Square, with a road toward the Scarlet Bastion. At Eastwall Gate, the Service Entrance breaks through the eastern fortification. Beyond it lie Elders' Square and blighted paths to Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses. The Service Entrance gives a shorter way into Stratholme's eastern districts. The Scourge holds the alleys and ziggurats, guarded by gargoyles, crypt fiends, and cultists. The Argent Dawn and bold adventurers gather here before striking at the Lich King's commanders.

subzone:stromgarde-keep.text:
Stromgarde Keep. In the Arathi Highlands, Stromgarde Keep is divided between its royal defenders, the Syndicate and Boulderfist ogres. The fallen kingdom's battered capital holds only part of its fortress. Strom began as the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor. King Thoradin founded it nearly three millennia ago. From this fortress, humanity prepared its victory over the forest trolls. Here, high elven magi taught the first hundred human spellcasters and began the long history of human wizardry.

Dalaran, Lordaeron and Stormwind rose as younger sister kingdoms while Strom's influence waned. The stubborn Trollbane dynasty remained and renamed the city Stromgarde. Through the Second War, it stood as a proud warrior bastion and an anchor of the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde. The devastation of the Third War brought mounting disasters and treachery, and Stromgarde finally broke. Its majestic stone city is now split into three warring sectors. Aristocratic Syndicate traitors hold the grand inner keep, while Boulderfist ogres have overrun the former sanctum of the mage district.

Prince Galen Trollbane and the battered Stromgarde military hold the remaining quarter. They wage a hard, bloody war on several fronts to keep their ancestral home from vanishing into memory.

subzone:sundown-marsh.text: Sundown Marsh. In the Wetlands' far west, deep water and stagnant pools make Sundown Marsh dangerous. An eccentric pair keeps a solitary home along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh spreads through the Wetlands' deepest western reaches. Deep water and thick mud conceal giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls in the mist. Most travelers stay on the cobblestone road between Menethil Harbor and Ironforge, leaving this corner largely untamed. A lonely stone cottage and churning windmill stand among the marsh's hazards. The gnome Fradd Swiftgear and the dwarf Wenna Silkbeard make their living scavenging the bog. They sell travelers curiosities and rare trade recipes recovered from the mire, though reaching them means braving its aggressive denizens.

subzone:sunnyglade.text:
Sunnyglade. Twilight's Hammer zealots now occupy Sunnyglade's ruins in the Riverglades. Once a wealthy human settlement under Stormwind, it was devastated during the First War and abandoned as the Horde advanced. Before the First War, Sunnyglade was a wealthy human town. Then the Old Horde invasion shattered its peace. Orc raiders attacked and enslaved the residents who survived. Only a wizard's tower remained intact, for human conjurers to study the arcane arts.

Stormwind forces tried to free the captive peasants and rebuild Sunnyglade. But the Horde kept advancing through the Riverglades. Stormwind's commanders judged the outer province lost and drew resources back to defend the homeland. The town was left in ruins. Sunnyglade lies far beyond the safe borders of Stormwind's restored realm. Its stone mage tower survived the First War and the years of abandonment. The peaceful township around it is gone, and Twilight's Hammer zealots now occupy the secluded ruins. They use the once-prosperous valley for their own designs.

subzone:swamplight-manor.text:
Swamplight Manor. In Witch Hill, 'Swamp Eye' Jarl cooks strange fare at Swamplight Manor. The crooked shack is his home, and his unusual tastes are known across the mire. Its garden draws the attention of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. In Witch Hill, a crooked wooden shack shelters the recluse 'Swamp Eye' Jarl. Fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts surround his home, far from any lordly estate. Jarl lives alone and spends his days making strange local dishes from marsh creatures.

Travelers come for his eccentric cooking or shelter from the spirits. Jarl also recruits them to hunt unusual ingredients, including marsh frog legs and creature eyes.

subzone:swarming-pillar.text: Swarming Pillar. Winged silithid circle Swarming Pillar, south of Cenarion Hold. Their swarm has carved and reshaped the rock into a hive in central Silithus. In central Silithus, Swarming Pillar rises from the dunes, its natural rock carved into burrows and coated with the swarm’s resin. It lies just south of Cenarion Hold. From it, winged worker and soldier broods pour out in dark clouds that fill the desert air and warn travelers away. Swarming Pillar is only the visible tip of a vast underground network. Deep tunnels and cavernous breeding chambers beneath its stony exterior anchor one of the region’s largest hives. The Cenarion Circle watches with concern as active broods threaten its druidic operations and expose the coordination behind the silithid menace.

subzone:tabetha-s-farm.text: Tabetha's Farm. In the Quagmire, Tabetha keeps her homestead apart from the marsh's dangers. In western Dustwallow Marsh, a weather-worn hut, garden plots, and a dock mark the farm. The dock opens onto the swamp's waterways, while the homestead lies far from the rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Tabetha, a reclusive human sorceress, lives here in near-total seclusion. She studies arcane and fel power beyond the reach of Dalaran and local authorities. Mages and warlocks travel from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to seek Tabetha's aid. Mages come to master raw arcane surges. Warlocks ask her to help cleanse volatile artifacts such as the Orb of Orahil.

subzone:tahonda-ruins.text:
Tahonda Ruins. Salt and sand cover Tahonda Ruins, where Saltstone basilisks stalk the remains of an ancient tauren settlement in the Shimmering Flats. Tahonda Ruins lie in the southern Shimmering Flats, near the pass into Tanaris. Salt crusts cover the weathered remains of this abandoned tauren village, and strange marks scar the surviving structures.

Two sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge. No one knows whether Saltstone basilisks drove the villagers away. The marks point to a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders, before the desert claimed what remained.

subzone:tainted-scar.text:
Tainted Scar. In the southwestern Blasted Lands, demons gather beneath Lord Kazzak’s command. Fel magic has made the Tainted Scar their stronghold. Where the Black Morass once spread, the Tainted Scar now cuts through the land as a lifeless trench stained like dried blood. Fel energies from the Dark Portal drained the wetlands and twisted the ground. After Archimonde fell at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, the surviving Burning Legion forces rallied in the south.

The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Scar for his stronghold. Elite demons hold its blackened rises, while lieutenants such as Razelikh the Defiler command the wasted red soil. Most mortals avoid the Tainted Scar, where death comes in agony. Yet fel energies draw those who practice the dark arts. Daio the Decrepit, an eccentric human warlock, lives beside a ruined demonic altar that overlooks the horrors.

He uses the fiends around him in dark rituals. There, he teaches aspiring warlocks to summon and bind dread infernals.

subzone:talonbranch-glade.text: Talonbranch Glade. Night elves find a rare refuge at Talonbranch Glade in northern Felwood. South of Timbermaw Hold, the glade offers a moonwell, shelter, and hippogryph flights amid the blighted woods. Talonbranch Glade watches over the high ground near the tunnel to Timbermaw Hold. It is the Alliance’s northernmost bastion in Felwood, gathered around a sheltered night elf lodge and a working moonwell. Scouts, Sentinels, and travelers rest here before venturing deeper into the tainted woods or setting out for Winterspring and Moonglade. Hippogryphs carry travelers from Talonbranch Glade to Auberdine in Darkshore and Everlook beyond Timbermaw Hold. The outpost keeps watch against the Shadow Council’s encroaching shadows and the feral beast packs roaming the corrupted vales.

subzone:temple-of-arkkoran.text: Temple of Arkkoran. On Azshara’s northeastern cliffs, the Temple of Arkkoran looks out over the Shattered Strand. Elune’s old sanctuary now belongs to Arkkoroc and his aquatic thralls. Elune, the moon goddess, was once honored at the Temple of Arkkoran. The Sundering shattered the ancient night elf empire and left the temple in ruin. Now tidal monstrosities crowd its marble steps and broken colonnades. Arkkoroc rules from the highest level, with loyal makrura and vicious murlocs at his side. Together, they defend the nearby coast from land-dwelling intruders.

subzone:temple-of-atal-hakkar.text: Temple of Atal'Hakkar. The Temple of Atal'Hakkar lies drowned beneath the Swamp of Sorrows, its halls still touched by corruption. Exiled troll priests raised it for Hakkar, and Ysera's green dragons sank it beneath the marsh centuries ago. More than a thousand years ago, civil war broke the Gurubashi Empire after the Atal'ai priesthood tried to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer. Exiled north, the surviving priests built a great stone temple in the Swamp of Sorrows to finish their work. Ysera, the Dragon Aspect, learned of their scheme and drove the temple deep into the mire. Its halls flooded beneath the Pool of Tears, while green dragon wardens remained to guard the ruins and keep Hakkar from returning. The flooded halls gave the Atal'ai the seclusion to continue their sacrifices. Over the centuries, corruption took hold of the guardians. The green dragon sentinels fell into madness, while the Atal'ai, led by Jammal'an the Prophet, prepare the way for Hakkar's avatar. The Horde and Alliance watch the sunken temple uneasily as rumors rise from the swamp's depths.

subzone:temple-of-zin-malor.text: Temple of Zin-Malor. Spitelash naga hold the Temple of Zin-Malor in the Ruins of Eldarath. Warlord Krellian commands them from this ancient night elven sanctuary in Azshara. Before the Great Sundering, the Temple of Zin-Malor rang with worship of Elune. Its graceful stonework recalls the nearby Temple of Arkkoran and the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, both built in the old night elven style. Now the marble lies weathered and broken. Spitelash naga have claimed the holy grounds and made them a stronghold for their forces. The Crystal of Zin-Malor once rested in the temple. Long ago, it was carried away to Kel'Theril in Winterspring.

subzone:terrace-of-repose.text: Terrace of Repose. At the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose remains green and clear amid Tirisfal Glades. The Scarlet Crusade tends this courtyard garden, untouched by the Plague of Undeath. Just north of the Scarlet Monastery's grand entrance, the Terrace of Repose is a green garden amid the blight. Beyond its hedges, grey mist hangs over Tirisfal Glades, where the soil is corrupt and the bogs lie stagnant. Here, a fountain runs with fresh, uncontaminated water, and the Scarlet Crusade tends the garden. Its zealots take these grounds as proof of their divine righteousness and purity. They believe holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

subzone:terror-run.text:
Terror Run. In Terror Run, predators stalk the open shelf beneath Un'Goro Crater's southwestern rim. The land lies west of the Slithering Scar, with devilsaurs and diemetradons below and pterrordax overhead. Beneath Un'Goro Crater's mountainous rim, Terror Run spreads across the southwestern shelf. Pterrordax wheel overhead as diemetradons, stegodons, and apex devilsaurs roam the low brush. The Slithering Scar's strange mounds lie close by.

Along Terror Run's eastern edge, the ruins of a camp mark where Williden Marshal's expedition was caught unprepared. The crater's primeval predators closed in before they could escape. Naturalists and adventurers come to Terror Run for Red Power Crystals, which rise from its fertile soil. Their crimson formations hum with primeval energy, like the blue, green, and yellow crystals found elsewhere in the basin.

Yet gathering them means facing the plains' strongest hunters. Apex devilsaurs nest in the deep south and brook no trespassers.

subzone:terror-wing-path.text: Terror Wing Path. Black dragonflight whelps and dragonkin patrol Terror Wing Path in the eastern Burning Steppes. The rocky canyon is a dangerous route to the region’s remote northeastern corner. Black dragonflight broods prowl Terror Wing Path’s ash-covered foothills. They guard their clutches and hunt anything that enters the canyon. Ash and soot coat the trails beneath its craggy walls, making the passage treacherous. Black drakes patrol the valley, and the rare magma giant Volchan sometimes wanders through. Few adventurers risk the journey alone. This path is the only way to reach Slither Rock, a hidden cave in the far northeastern corner of the Steppes.

subzone:terrordale.text: Terrordale. Terrordale’s streets lie in ruin beneath restless dead, beside Plaguewood and Terrorweb Tunnel. In the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands, Scourge horrors and tormented spirits haunt what remains. Terrordale fell to the Scourge with the rest of Lordaeron. Near Terrorweb Tunnel’s mouth, restless shades and wandering undead fill the ruined village streets. Plaguewood’s trees press against its rotting timber. A few eccentric residents still dare to stay. Augustus the Touched is a peculiar merchant, while Egan hunts ghosts and seeks to free the tortured spirits caught between worlds. Terrordale’s spirits remain in agony, bound to the earth by their tragic ends. Their anguish disturbs the spirit realm so deeply that the physical world buckles beneath it. Seasoned paladins come under the guidance of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. Through rites of judgment and sacrifice, they seek to banish the torment. The work tests their holy discipline.

subzone:terrorweb-tunnel.text: Terrorweb Tunnel. Crypt fiends swarm through Terrorweb Tunnel, the mountain way between Terrordale and the Thondroril River. Terrorweb Tunnel cuts through the mountains beside the Thondroril River. It runs from Terrordale to the riverbanks south of the village. Crypt fiends fill the passage where ghouls or skeletal sentries might be found. These mummified nerubian arachnids were raised to serve the Lich King. The tunnel shortens the route around the mountain slopes, but thick webs and towering Nerubian Overseers make the dark way dangerous to cross.

subzone:thalanaar.text: Thalanaar. At Feralas's eastern edge, Thalanaar shelters Alliance travelers and watches the road from Thousand Needles. Its hippogryph roost links the mainland with Feathermoon Stronghold. From the east, Thalanaar is the first night elf outpost you meet at Feralas's edge. Here, Thousand Needles' sandstone gives way to forest canopy, with sturdy pavilions and sentinels on watch. Alliance scouts, couriers, and craftsmen find shelter before entering the forest. Beasts, ogres, and Horde forces roam southern Kalimdor, so the outpost is a refuge and a place to gather before venturing in. Thalanaar's hippogryph master connects Feralas with Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh, Gadgetzan in Tanaris, and Feathermoon Stronghold to the west. These routes cross a region where overland travel is perilous, linking the wilderness to destinations across southern Kalimdor. Craftsmen also come here to seek master leatherworkers, who teach the ancient art of working wild hides beneath the woodland boughs.

subzone:thalassian-base-camp.text:
Thalassian Base Camp. On a ridge in northern Azshara, the blood elf expedition at Thalassian Base Camp digs through ancient ruins for arcane relics. Their pact with the Horde is broken. East of Ursolan, the blood elf expedition once promised not to threaten travelers from Orgrimmar. Magus Rimtori offered the Horde a share of any magical riches in return for supplies, funding, and an armed escort through Azshara’s wildlands.

Once the camp was fortified and the first relics were recovered from the elven ruins, Rimtori broke the pact and drove away the Horde emissaries. She now searches deeper reaches with an armed retinue. Magister Hawkhelm guards the ridge and camp against retribution.

subzone:thandol-span.text: Thandol Span. At Thandol Span, the surviving bridge lies under attack. Its stone arches link the Wetlands of Khaz Modan with the Arathi Highlands of southern Lordaeron, but Dark Iron infiltrators have sabotaged one crossing. Ironforge Mountaineers guard the surviving bridge. They fight to hold the roadway and drive back Dark Iron sappers, though the defense costs them dearly. If the bridge falls, northern trade and military movements will rely almost entirely on sea routes. Alliance forces in the Arathi Highlands will lose their immediate reinforcement.

subzone:thelgen-rock.text: Thelgen Rock. In the Wetlands, Thelgen Rock’s caverns draw miners after volatile Incendicite Ore. Venomous spiders fill the passages. Thelgen Rock cuts into the mountain wall between the Wetlands and Loch Modan. Aggressive spiders crowd its web-choked passages, and their venom makes every step perilous. Still, miners and adventurers brave the tunnels for the valuable Incendicite Ore in the rock.

subzone:theramore-isle.text:
Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle shelters refugees from Lordaeron behind the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Lady Jaina Proudmoore founded the fortified port, now the Alliance's chief stronghold in southern Kalimdor. After the Scourge ravaged Dalaran and Lordaeron in the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore led survivors across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. There, humans, dwarves, and high elves fought beside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal.

After the victory, Jaina's coalition withdrew to the misty edge of Dustwallow Marsh. On an island just off the coast, they raised a harbor city with stone ramparts and Jaina's citadel, sheltering what remained of the northern kingdoms.

subzone:thistleshrub-valley.text: Thistleshrub Valley. In southwestern Tanaris, giant cacti and living thistleshrubs crowd a canyon. The hostile plants lash out at travelers who cross their thorn-choked ground. Giant blooming cacti rise above the sand, crowding a canyon where much of Tanaris lies bare. Living thistleshrubs give the valley its name. They strike travelers who come near with sharp spines, making the crossing perilous. Their thorny brush blocks the way past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates. Travelers have long wondered how animated plants survive in such a dry land. The thistleshrubs fiercely guard their ground. Forgotten elemental energies may have awakened them, or they may have adapted to Tanaris's harsh climate. Towering cacti offer little cover from desert predators and venomous serpents in the canyon.

subzone:thondroril-river.text:
Thondroril River. At Thondroril River, plague taints the waters between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. It rises near Terrorweb Tunnel in Northern Lordaeron and flows south into Darrowmere Lake. Once a route for trade and travel through the fallen kingdom, its banks now shelter monstrous Scourge beasts and a legendary hermit. Before Lordaeron fell, traffic followed Thondroril north toward the kingdom's holdings and south to Darrowmere Lake. Now the river marks a dangerous divide between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands.

Plague taints the water. Giant maggots, plaguebats, diseased bears, and predatory snapjaws infest the banks. Where a scenic riverbed once offered passage, travelers now face a deadly crossing.

subzone:thoradin-s-wall.text: Thoradin's Wall. At Thoradin's Wall, broken stone divides the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. King Thoradin ordered it built long ago to shield early humanity from Amani troll incursions. Thoradin's Wall once guarded Strom's western frontier. Nearly three thousand years ago, King Thoradin raised it across the valley corridor to shield humanity's young settlements from Amani forest troll raids. Strom stood at the heart of Arathor, the first unified human empire. The wall protected its heartland, giving humanity room to survive and challenge troll supremacy in the north. Thoradin's Wall now lies in severe disrepair. Great breaches split its ramparts, worn down by weather, warfare, and abandonment. Arathor splintered into rival kingdoms, and neighboring Lordaeron later fell to the Scourge. No central realm remains to maintain the masonry. Travelers and roaming bandits pass freely through the broken archways between Hillsbrad and the untamed Arathi Highlands.

subzone:thorium-point.text:
Thorium Point. At Thorium Point, the Thorium Brotherhood holds its ground against Dark Iron kin who serve the Firelord and Emperor Dagran Thaurissan. The outpost welcomes Alliance and Horde travelers who will gather ore or fight in the volcanic wastes. Thorium Point clings to the northern bluffs above the scorched slag heaps of the Searing Gorge. The Thorium Brotherhood holds this mountain camp. Its Dark Iron dwarves broke from their enslaved kin in Shadowforge City and refuse to bow to the Firelord or Emperor Dagran Thaurissan.

An open-air forge, a busy flight master, and guarded walls give the Brotherhood a foothold northeast of Firewatch Ridge. They struggle to survive and seek mastery of smithing. With few allies, they open the camp to both Alliance and Horde travelers, who can dig ore from the ash or fight the Dark Iron dwarves. Thorium Point gives the Brotherhood a base for war against its kin and a safe crossing through the Redridge mountain chain. The camp overlooks a volcanic basin where ravenous spiders and fire elementals prowl.

Flight links reach Ironforge and forward camps across the Badlands and the Burning Steppes. Mercenaries, prospectors, and crafters seeking the secret favor of master dwarf smiths find a safe hearth on this smoky cliffside.

subzone:thunder-axe-fortress.text: Thunder Axe Fortress. Burning Blade cultists hold Thunder Axe Fortress in northwestern Desolace. They guard the wastes from its stone barracks and watchtowers, with darkened caves below. In northwestern Desolace, Burning Blade cultists keep watch over the wastes from Thunder Axe Fortress. Stone barracks and watchtowers fortify the compound, and deep caverns run beneath it. Far from Kalimdor’s major cities, the cult gathers fel energies and summons lesser demons. Its members scheme to bring more dangerous entities into the world.

subzone:thunder-bluff.text:
Thunder Bluff. On Mulgore’s high mesas, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren and gathers their scattered tribes. Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after the Third War, giving them refuge and a place to keep their traditions. Above Mulgore, rope bridges join Thunder Bluff’s stone mesas, and wooden elevators carry travelers up from the plains. For generations, the tauren wandered central Kalimdor as centaur raiding parties pursued them. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined Warchief Thrall and the New Horde.

Together, they drove back the centaurs and claimed Mulgore’s fertile grasslands. Cairne gathered the scattered tribes and founded the city atop the mesas. The heights offered shelter above the plains, along with a place for the tauren to trade and gather in worship. Cairne Bloodhoof’s followers share Thunder Bluff with tauren who follow other ways. Magatha Grimtotem and her kin dwell on the Elder Rise. Beneath the city, spirit walkers and shaman seek the ancestors’ will at the Pools of Vision. Tribal rivalries persist, yet Thunder Bluff remains a spiritual pillar of Kalimdor’s Horde. Hunters return from the Barrens, artisans travel through, and druids come to commune with the Earth Mother.

subzone:tidefury-cove.text: Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove’s reefs and wrecks still make these waters perilous for sailors. Makrura roam the shallows, while solitary anglers seek the quiet shore. At the far end of Dustwallow Bay, Tidefury Cove lies between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have wrecked many vessels over the years, leaving rotting hulls half-submerged along the tide line. Makrura crawl over the wreckage, and the cove remains a dangerous, isolated shore. Hardy scavengers and quiet hermits come here to escape Theramore’s busy docks. During the invasion of Durotar, Tidefury Cove became a battleground. Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s Kul Tiran expedition fortified the coast with a fortress and guard towers to command the approaches to Theramore. Thrall united the young Horde to break that hold. Orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren joined Rexxar and the Stonemaul ogres in an assault on the shore. They dismantled the Kul Tiran beachhead, then pressed toward the island fortress.

subzone:timbermaw-hold.text: Timbermaw Hold. Within Timbermaw Hold, a furbolg tribe still resists demonic corruption. Its tunnels link Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. Deep beneath the mountain, the Timbermaw guard their home while corruption spreads through the forests above. During the Third War, the Burning Legion tainted neighboring furbolg tribes, but the Timbermaw endured in these stone corridors. From below, they watched their beloved forests warp. Now they distrust outsiders and defend every tunnel entrance, expecting violence from anyone coming in from the infected woods. Timbermaw Hold is the only direct passage through the mountain between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. Its sentries let outsiders pass only after they prove their goodwill. Those who oppose the corrupted furbolg clans may find steadfast allies among the Timbermaw. They share their ancient shamanic knowledge and leathercrafting traditions.

subzone:timbermaw-post.text: Timbermaw Post. Winterfall furbolgs hold Timbermaw Post in central Winterspring. The camp lies southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of Lake Kel'Theril. Winterfall furbolgs crowd Timbermaw Post in central Winterspring. You find the camp southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of frozen Lake Kel'Theril. Though it bears the Timbermaw name, the hostile Winterfall tribe controls the outpost. Demonic corruption has driven them mad and violent, and they press toward the central road.

subzone:tkashi-ruins.text: Tkashi Ruins. Bloodscalp trolls guard the Tkashi Ruins southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, crumbling stones mark an ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. The Bloodscalp tribe now occupies the ruins and fiercely defends its territory. Among the vines and decayed stone, they practice shamanistic rituals. Hemet Nesingwary wrote that he passed through without trouble, but travelers now face Bloodscalp guards protecting tribal relics buried in the rubble.

subzone:tower-of-arathor.text:
Tower of Arathor. Boulderfist ogres hold the Tower of Arathor among the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. The spire once served Archmage Trelane in the former mage district, southwest in the keep. In Stromgarde Keep's mage district, the spire rises above ruins and bears the name of the ancient Empire of Arathor. It once served the realm's sorcerers, most notably Archmage Trelane. He devised a magical defensive grid keyed to enchanted gemstones to guard the sanctum.

After the Third War, the Syndicate and the Boulderfist ogre clan assaulted Stromgarde, and the kingdom fractured. Trelane tried to hold the tower with his arcane wards, but the ogres overwhelmed him. He fled the city for his life and left his most prized arcane artifacts behind. Now the Boulderfist brute Ruul Onestone and his followers hold the spire.

subzone:tower-of-eldara.text:
Tower of Eldara. At Azshara’s far northeastern edge, the Tower of Eldara keeps its sealed doors above the Bay of Storms. Though long abandoned, its stone endured the Sundering, while beasts prowl the coast below. On a remote cliff northeast of the Bay of Storms, the Tower of Eldara recalls the kaldorei empire that once ruled this coast. Like other ruins in Azshara, it fell into disuse after the Great Sundering. Its entrance remains barred, revealing nothing of the chambers or relics within.

Along the surrounding shores, murlocs wander, makrura claw across the rocks, and hydras hunt. Few travelers dare approach.

subzone:twilight-base-camp.text: Twilight Base Camp. At Twilight Base Camp, the Twilight's Hammer gathers in Silithus to summon elemental powers and advance its apocalyptic cause. Wind stones mark the camp, and armed cultists stand ready. Twilight Base Camp is one of several Twilight's Hammer enclaves in Silithus. Zealots, geomancers, and stonecallers gather among jagged ritual stones to summon elemental forces. Twilight Keeper Havunth and Twilight Lord Everun direct their efforts to hasten Azeroth's end. Cenarion Hold forces seek to restore balance to the region, but the cult openly defies them. Lesser and greater wind stones stand throughout the outpost. The Twilight's Hammer uses cryptic incantations and cult regalia at these monuments to draw chaotic elemental spirits into the physical realm. Travelers and scouts work to disrupt the rites before the cult's influence spreads across Kalimdor.

subzone:twilight-outpost.text: Twilight Outpost. At Twilight Outpost, the Twilight's Hammer gathers in southwestern Silithus. Its Wind Stones summon elemental horrors near the Scarab Wall. In southwestern Silithus, Twilight Outpost is one of the Twilight's Hammer's great strongholds. You find it northwest of the Scarab Wall and west of the Bronzebeard Encampment. Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers fill the camp. Twilight Keeper Exeter and the rare Twilight Lord Everun lead these zealots in service to their apocalyptic masters. Wind Stones stand scattered through the camp, from Lesser to Greater. The Twilight's Hammer uses enchanted regalia and foul incantations to tear open paths to the elemental planes. Abyssal commanders and elemental lords emerge through those breaches. Disrupting the summons is one way to strike back at the cult's hold in the desert.

subzone:twilight-post.text:
Twilight Post. Twilight Post holds the Twilight's Hammer in a fortified camp in northwestern Silithus. Far west of Cenarion Hold and northwest of Twilight Base Camp, its cultists use wind stones to contact otherworldly forces. Adventurers here face zealous defenders and the stones that serve their rites. Twilight Post is a fortified outpost in northwestern Silithus. Heavily armed defenders and ritualists fill the camp, among them Twilight Avengers, Geolords, and Stonecallers. Twilight Keeper Mayna leads them, with the rare fanatic Twilight Lord Everun at her side.

At the heart of the post stand Lesser, regular, and Greater Wind Stones. Through dark rites and communion with the elements, the cultists use them to call elemental horrors from realms beyond and bind them. Such rites threaten the fragile peace the Cenarion Circle keeps in the region.

subzone:twilight-s-run.text:
Twilight's Run. Beneath Staghelm Point in northern Silithus, Twilight's Run shelters the Twilight's Hammer. Its cavern walls shield their rituals and forces from the desert winds. Beneath Staghelm Point, Twilight's Run opens into the northern cliffs of Silithus. The Twilight's Hammer has made its tunnels a stronghold, sheltered from desert winds and the silithid hives that roam the dunes. Its cultists gather to commune with dark forces, guard ritual materials, and marshal their forces.

Vyral the Vile and other overseers direct the cultists. They keep a hostile watch and stand ready to strike down any traveler or scout who comes too close.

subzone:twin-colossals.text: Twin Colossals. The Twin Colossals rise above northwestern Feralas, marking the way north into Desolace. In western Feralas, the Twin Colossals rise above the forest. Travelers coming south from Desolace know these great cliffs at once. Their lower slopes meet the jungle and the lands near the Forgotten Coast, while their summits stand apart above the forest floor. No footpath climbs the sheer cliffs, but Marli Wishrunner helps travelers reach the eastern peak. A quiet pond rests atop the mesa, home to Diamond Head, an unusually large makrura. Kalin Windflight offers sturdy parachutes for the descent into the jungle canopy.

subzone:tyr-s-hand.text:
Tyr's Hand. In the southeastern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands, Scarlet Crusaders hold Tyr's Hand as their chief stronghold and supply hub. The city was once sacred to the Church of the Holy Light, and its walls remain heavily fortified. Tyr's Hand rises from the old Eastweald, once a green land in Lordaeron, as one of humanity's most ancient sacred sites. Shrines and holy buildings stand across its grounds, giving it the name “city of churches.” The land around it has rotted under blight, yet Tyr's Hand remains remarkably preserved behind thick walls and formidable stonework. The Scarlet Basilica towers above the city. Lord Valdelmar kept Tyr's Hand standing through military vigilance and faith as the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War. After the Knights of the Silver Hand split into rival factions, Tyr's Hand joined the Crimson dawn of the Scarlet Crusade. High General Brigitte Abbendis and Valdelmar lead the city from its impenetrable base.

Elite crusaders train in the abbey. Heavily guarded couriers keep contact with Scarlet forces holding Stratholme, while the city ruthlessly rebuffs outsiders at its gates.

subzone:tyr-s-hand-abbey.text: Tyr's Hand Abbey. In Tyr's Hand, the Scarlet Crusade keeps the abbey for worship and study. The fortified city stands in the southeastern Eastern Plaguelands, where the abbey supports the grand Scarlet Basilica. Tyr's Hand Abbey gives the Scarlet Crusade a quieter place for worship and martial teaching. The Scarlet Basilica rises over the city's skyline, while the abbey follows a design familiar from Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Its Main Hall stands between the Hall of Arms and Library Wing. Though horrors plague the land, the Crusade keeps the abbey in careful repair and guards its cloisters fiercely from outsiders.

subzone:uldaman.text:
Uldaman. In Uldaman, rival excavators and troggs now clash within the sealed halls. Beneath the northern Badlands mountains, this ancient titan vault holds the buried origins of the dwarven race, with stone sentinels still on guard. Titan watchers built Uldaman beneath the earth as a refuge and a place of research. Their first attempts to shape living stone made the misshapen troggs. They sealed them in stasis chambers, then tried again and created the stone-skinned earthen.

The deepest halls hold vital records, including the fabled Discs of Norgannon. Stonekeeper Archaedas and the giantess Ironaya guarded the vault. Dwarven legend says the earthen gave rise to the dwarven race, whose cradle lay buried and forgotten beneath the hills.

subzone:uldum.text: Uldum. In Tanaris’s southern mountains, Uldum’s colossal gates remain sealed. Ancient wards and machinery hide the Titan research compound from explorers. Uldum’s great stone gateway still bars the way in the southern mountains of Tanaris. The Titans built the compound while ordering ancient Kalimdor. It was a vast facility for shaping and overseeing the planet’s biosphere. Titan wardens and defensive constructs once guarded its bounds. Today, only the massive arches can be seen; what lies beyond remains out of mortal reach. Dwarven scholars study the clear signs of Titan craft at Uldum, but they have found no key or mechanism to open the complex. Legend points to the lost Plates of Uldum as the means to reach its secrets. For now, the scholars can only look toward an empire they cannot enter.

subzone:undercity.text: Undercity. Beneath Capital City, the Forsaken hold their underground stronghold, ruled by Sylvanas Windrunner. Its halls began as Scourge work and now shelter the free-willed undead. Before the Third War, sewers, royal catacombs, and dungeons lay beneath Capital City. As Lordaeron fell, Prince Arthas Menethil ordered the Scourge to enlarge them into an underground seat of power. The Lich King summoned Arthas to Northrend before the work was finished. During the civil war in the Plaguelands, Sylvanas Windrunner rallied undead who had escaped the Lich King's grip. She overthrew the dreadlords and drove out rival forces, and the Forsaken claimed the underground complex. They finished the maze of catacombs the Scourge had begun and fortified it beneath the silent ruins of their former kingdom. Now the Dark Lady rules her people from its poisoned halls.

subzone:undercroft.text: Undercroft. In the southwestern hills of the Eastern Plaguelands, undead trolls have taken an old Lordaeron tomb. Zaeldarr the Outcast commands them, and a false grave in the catacombs bears Tirion Fordring’s name. You find the Undercroft carved into the bluffs southwest of Corin's Crossing. Lordaeron built it for its honored dead, but the kingdom's fall left the tomb open to undead trolls. Zaeldarr the Outcast leads them from its underground halls. They stalk the Plaguelands and raid the grave pits at Light's Hope Chapel, taking newly buried corpses for their grim practices.

subzone:uplands.text: Uplands. In the northeastern Alterac Mountains, the Syndicate holds the Uplands and its camps. These hills once fed Alterac's mountain fortresses, but now shelter the band's strongest base. Before the Second War broke Alterac apart, grain and livestock from the Uplands fed its mountain fortresses. When the kingdom fell into ruin, honest folk left their farms behind. Dispossessed nobles and cutthroats formed the Syndicate, set on taking back what they believed was stolen from them by force. Its camps, patrols, and outposts now fill the hills. Dandred's Fold lies along the western borders. The Syndicate keeps its strongest forces in the Uplands. There, high-ranking conspirators oversee its operations, including Baron Vardus, who is aligned with the shadowy leaders guiding Alterac's remaining nobility. From these hills they direct brigands, raid neighboring valleys, and resist both the Alliance and Horde. Travelers on the northeastern ridges meet entrenched highwaymen who claim the range as their sovereign soil.

subzone:ursolan.text:
Ursolan. In western Azshara, Ursolan shelters the Timbermaw furbolgs east of Timbermaw Hold. Its ravine cuts through a stronghold named for the bear Ancient Ursol, where uncorrupted furbolgs defend their ground. Across a deep ravine in western Azshara, Ursolan climbs both rims. The Timbermaw hold this eastern branch of their territory. Through Timbermaw Hold, it links to Bear's Head in the south.

The camp takes its name from the bear Ancient Ursol. Here, furbolgs who have resisted the demonic corruption consuming many of their kin across Kalimdor have found a haven. They guard their borders against outsiders, including researchers from the night elven camp of Talrendis.

subzone:uther-s-tomb.text:
Uther's Tomb. On Sorrow Hill in the Western Plaguelands, Uther's Tomb remains untouched by the blight. His followers raised it after Arthas slew him near Andorhal. South of Andorhal's ruins, Uther's Tomb marks the resting place of Uther, who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. After Lordaeron fell, he made his last stand in Andorhal. There he defended King Terenas Menethil II's urn of ashes from Prince Arthas Menethil and the Scourge.

Arthas killed his former mentor and took the urn to carry Kel'Thuzad's remains. Surviving soldiers recovered Uther's body and laid him in a stone sanctuary. Though the surrounding land is corrupted, the tomb remains untouched by decay under High Priest Thel'danis's watch. The Path of Uther leads to a grand stone effigy of the paladin. A tome of the Holy Light rests in one hand, and his warhammer in the other. Pilgrims brave these roads to pay homage, pray, or reflect on the devotion that shaped the first paladins.

subzone:valley-of-bones.text: Valley of Bones. In Shen'dralas, the Valley of Bones lies choked with dust and ancient remains. Restless dead haunt its canyon, where centaur necromancers patrol among the colossal ribs of two Dead Goliaths. Skeletal horrors walk the dusty ravines of the Valley of Bones, a canyon in the south. Centaur necromancers raise them with dark sorcery and command them. The spirits of the Magram centaur clan wander there too, bound to the barren earth long after their violent deaths. Two immense skeletons, called the Dead Goliaths, slump against the rocky cliffs. Scholars and travelers do not know where they came from.

subzone:valley-of-fangs.text:
Valley of Fangs. In the Badlands, a small camp keeps to the Valley of Fangs while predators roam nearby. The Valley of Fangs runs between two great stone formations in the heart of the Badlands. Feral crag coyotes, prowling cougars, and vicious wolves stalk its dusty floor, so lone travelers face danger in the pass.

A handful of wayward figures camp there. Martek the Exiled, a banished orc, keeps company with the goblins Rigglefuzz and Jazzrik. Far from the regional outposts, they tinker in seclusion.

subzone:valley-of-spears.text: Valley of Spears. In western Desolace, the Maraudine guard their stronghold in the Valley of Spears. Beyond the valley lies Maraudon, the sacred burial ground of all centaurkind. The Maraudine hold the Valley of Spears in western Desolace. On foot, you can enter only through narrow mountain passes from the south and east. Rocky chokepoints guard those approaches, while hostile nomad camps fill the way to the clan’s most revered holy site. At the valley’s southwestern end, an entrance opens into Maraudon. The sacred cavern holds the tomb of Zaetar, father of the centaur, and Princess Theradras dwells within. The Maraudine defend the canyon fiercely from rival clans and outsiders. Gnome cartographer Melizza Brimbuzzle and scouts who wander in unaware may be captured or slain.

subzone:valley-of-the-watchers.text: Valley of the Watchers. At Tanaris’s southern edge, the sealed gate at the Valley of the Watchers keeps Uldum beyond reach. Stone sentinels and lumbering giants guard the ancient complex. At the valley’s southern end, a massive stone gate bars the way. It is believed to guard Uldum, a subterranean facility of the enigmatic Titans. Dune Smasher mountain giants roam the dusty approach, keeping travelers, tomb robbers, and scholars from disturbing what lies beneath the sands. The valley marks Tanaris’s southern boundary, where shifting desert sands meet the continent’s mountainous edge.

subzone:valor-s-rest.text: Valor's Rest. At Silithus's eastern edge, Valor's Rest gives travelers shelter beside its cemetery. At Silithus's eastern border, Valor's Rest stands beside the ramp down from Un'Goro Crater. The Cenarion Circle keeps the camp neutral. Alliance and Horde travelers gather there before crossing into the arid wastes. Its graveyard marks those lost to the desert, where insectoid horrors and ancient threats endanger even the hardiest travelers.

subzone:valormok.text: Valormok. Valormok keeps a Horde foothold in northwest Azshara. North of the Haldarr Encampment, the outpost sends scouts and travelers toward the cursed ancient ruins along the coast. Autumn-colored trees ring Valormok, where the Horde holds a foothold in a hostile and largely forsaken land. Nearby satyrs, nagas, and prowling beasts threaten the lightly fortified camp. Its warriors hold their ground despite the danger. Wind riders connect Valormok with Orgrimmar and the wilder reaches of northern Kalimdor.

subzone:venture-co-base-camp.text: Venture Co. Base Camp. In northern Stranglethorn, Venture Co. Base Camp cuts into the jungle. Goblin overseers and laborers harvest timber, hunt wildlife, and search nearby waterways for tumbled crystals. Venture Co. Base Camp sends crews into the jungle for profit. Steam-powered machines and rough goblin shacks break through the ancient canopy. Armed mercenaries guard the camp. Foremen and workers direct the gathering of resources across nearby valleys. They search the waterways for tumbled crystals and clear jungle that blocks their work.

subzone:vice.text:
Vice. Deadwind ogres hold the Vice beside the road to Karazhan. Their camps and earthen mounds mark a bleak, scarred stretch of Deadwind Pass, where travelers face brute strength and dark magic. The Deadwind ogres hold camps across southern Deadwind Pass, beside the road toward Karazhan. Their rough mounds rise among barren earth and jagged rock. Vengeful ghosts and scavenger vultures haunt much of the canyon, yet the ogres defend their camps with fierce violence.

Travelers on the road between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows must cross their territory. No one knows why the clan chose this bleak, magically scarred waste. Deadwind ogres fight with heavy weapons and dangerous arcane magic. Among them, Deadwind warlocks practice crude but lethal fel sorceries among the earthen mounds. Their camps lie close to Karazhan, the abandoned seat of Medivh.

The road through the canyon is perilous for wandering scholars and solitary scouts.

subzone:vile-reef.text: Vile Reef. Murlocs guard Vile Reef beneath the Great Sea, just off Stranglethorn Vale near Grom'gol Base Camp. Coral, troll ruins, shipwrecks, and giant clams fill its waters. Beneath the Great Sea, Vile Reef lies just offshore from Grom'gol Base Camp. Vivid coral grows across the seabed beside weathered troll ruins and the Altar of the Tides. Territorial murlocs lurk among the coral and shattered ship timbers. They defend the shallows and prey on divers seeking giant clams and rare blue pearls.

subzone:wailing-caverns.text: Wailing Caverns. Steam wails through the bluffs above Lushwater Oasis. Beneath them, Naralex's hope of restoring the Barrens has turned the Wailing Caverns into a place of corruption and danger.

subzone:warpwood-quarter.text: Warpwood Quarter. In Dire Maul, twisted growth and demonic corruption now overrun the Warpwood Quarter. Once its gardens nurtured nature, but frenzied plants and corrupted satyrs have taken the eastern district of Eldre'Thalas. The Warpwood Quarter's grand gardens are now a choking tangle of twisted ancients and lethal lashers. Alzzin the Wildshaper, a satyr, turned dark magic against the ancient Fruit of Fertility. Under his influence, the plants grew grotesque and predatory. Vile Felvine shards now saturate the halls, where demons, rebellious imps and demonic thralls have gathered. Most explorers enter the district through Dire Maul's central Broken Commons. To the east, an overgrown passage runs beneath the Lariss Pavilion, though Alzzin's warped guardians make the way dangerous. The mischievous imp Pusillin brings another peril. His thievery sends pursuers racing toward secluded reaches of the ruins.

subzone:waterspring-field.text: Waterspring Field. At Waterspring Field in northern Tanaris, stolen pumps leave Gadgetzan without water. Beneath the Tanaris sands, pumps draw water for Gadgetzan. The Steamwheedle Cartel goblins built them to supply their growing trade hub. Now the Wastewanders hold the field. These human outlaws and desert marauders guard the pumps, while Gadgetzan seeks hired blades to reclaim its water.

subzone:wavestrider-beach.text: Wavestrider Beach. Burning ships still clash offshore from Wavestrider Beach on Tanaris's eastern coast. The shore stretches between Steamwheedle Port and Lost Rigger Cove, where crustaceans roam the sand and pirates command the nearby waters. Steeljaw Snappers and Desert Crawlers scuttle over the baking sand. Wavestrider Beach follows eastern Tanaris from Steamwheedle Port in the north to the cliffs above Lost Rigger Cove. Offshore, burning vessels remain locked in combat. Their flames mark the violence that grips these pirate waters.

subzone:weazel-s-crater.text: Weazel's Crater. Saltstone basilisks now sun themselves in the deep hollow of Weazel's Crater, while its origins remain unknown. Weazel's Crater cuts deep into the northern Shimmering Flats. Experimental goblin and gnome rocket-cars still race across the blinding salt, pushing mechanical limits. Scorched earth, debris, and impact hollows mark the plain, but none match the crater's size and depth. No one knows what formed it. The wreckage has largely settled, and aggressive Saltstone basilisks now sun themselves in the hollow.

subzone:weeping-cave.text: Weeping Cave. Toxic blight seeps through Weeping Cave in the northeastern hills of the Western Plaguelands, just west of the Thondroril River. Grotesque fungal beasts and oozes shelter in its tunnels. Above the Thondroril River, moisture trickles through Weeping Cave’s rocky ceiling. The Scourge’s plague has poisoned the soil overhead, and foul runoff drains into the dark tunnels. Rotting horrors and decaying behemoths roam there with caustic oozes. A corrupted elemental called The Husk dwells in the cave as well.

subzone:whispering-gardens.text:
Whispering Gardens. In northeastern Tirisfal, the Whispering Gardens lie on the hillside south of the Scarlet Monastery. Early crusade defenders fought a host of the Scourge here. Now Scarlet crusaders patrol the overgrown paths, where faint voices linger. Before the Scarlet Crusade withdrew behind the Monastery walls, the Whispering Gardens saw fierce fighting. Undead pressed across the terraces, and countless lives were lost on both sides.

At twilight, travelers crossing the gardens report soft murmurings on the wind. Many believe these are echoes of the soldiers and priests who died defending the holy grounds. The Scarlet Crusade keeps watch over the Whispering Gardens. Scouts, magicians, and preservers guard the trails against intruders from the lower glades.

For zealots in the nearby monastery, the overgrown steps guard their approach. They also recall the unceasing war against the undead.

subzone:wild-shore.text:
Wild Shore. Bloodsail Buccaneers anchor along Wild Shore, where Stranglethorn Vale's jungle meets the South Seas. At Stranglethorn Vale's southern tip, you reach the Wild Shore and the South Seas. Booty Bay's fortified inlet lies northwest, while a shallow strait separates the mainland beach from Jaguero Isle to the east. The shore runs northeast toward the Crystal Shore. Blackwater Raiders' cannons cannot reach this coast directly, so pirates gather here among wild dangers. Bloodsail Buccaneers hold much of the shore. Their wooden ships anchor in the surf, and their camps spread across the sand. They stage operations here, store illicit cargo, and plan strikes against their goblin rivals.

Prowling beasts also haunt the beaches. Gorlash, a colossal sea giant, stomps through the surf and crushes anyone who lingers along the tide line.

subzone:windbreak-canyon.text: Windbreak Canyon. Wind serpents hunt travelers along the northern road through Windbreak Canyon. The canyon lies between Freewind Post and the Shimmering Flats. East of Freewind Post, Windbreak Canyon cuts through the sheer northern walls above the canyon floor. Whistling winds race between the stone spires, leaving little shelter. Wild wind serpents perch among the rocks, lay clutches on the ledges, and strike travelers who stray from the main road. Winding trails climb through the canyon toward the Weathered Nook.

subzone:winterfall-village.text:
Winterfall Village. In Winterfall Village, furbolgs have turned against travelers east of Everlook. Once peaceful kin to Kalimdor’s other ursine tribes, they now live in madness and violent corruption under High Chief Winterfall. Snowy terraces east of Everlook hold Winterfall Village, the main settlement of the Winterfall furbolgs in Winterspring. Like their cousins across northern Kalimdor, these bear-folk were warped and driven mad by the foulness left by the Burning Legion’s invasion.

High Chief Winterfall leads the tribe from a secluded cavern atop the village’s highest tier. The furbolgs have abandoned their ancestral communion with the wild spirits of the snow. Now they assault travelers, patrol the mountain passes, and threaten anyone who comes near their frost-bitten home.

subzone:witch-hill.text: Witch Hill. Mirefin murlocs camp around Witch Hill, where Swamplight Manor stands near the path to Theramore. Rumors of hauntings trouble the lonely rise. Witch Hill rises from the waters of Dustwallow Marsh, about a third of the way down the peninsula toward Theramore Isle. Mirefin murlocs claim the waters around it, and their camps make the swamp dangerous. Near the hill's center stands Swamplight Manor, home to the hermit known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl. Travelers report eerie sights and dark presences across the rise.

subzone:witherbark-village.text:
Witherbark Village. In the southeastern Arathi Highlands, Witherbark Village shelters hostile forest trolls beside a secluded lake. The tribe raids Stromgarde's Alliance remnants and the Horde outpost at Hammerfall. Witherbark trolls hold the shore and paths around their mountain lake. Fishers, axe throwers, and witch doctors live in huts along the water. Zalas Witherbark and the tribe's shadow hunters direct their people from a great cavern behind the settlement.

The Witherbark have joined forces with the Boulderfist ogres to claim more of the highlands. They have also taken a firm foothold in the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. Any outsider who enters their territory risks a fierce attack.

subzone:woodpaw-den.text: Woodpaw Den. Woodpaw gnolls hold their den beneath Feralas’s dense canopy, just north of Darkmist Ruins. Their fiercest alphas guard the pack’s home, and travelers crossing the southern wilderness face their threat. Woodpaw Den is held by the seasoned alphas of the local gnoll pack. Unlike the smaller scout camps along the jungle tracks, this encampment is defended in force. The gnolls fight to keep their territory from intruders and the encroaching wilderness. Just north of the elven remnants at Darkmist Ruins, the den threatens travelers crossing this part of Feralas.

subzone:woodpaw-hills.text:
Woodpaw Hills. In southeastern Feralas, silithid swarms and mountain giants press into Woodpaw Hills. The Woodpaw gnolls have lost ground in their old territory. Woodpaw gnolls hold the forests of Woodpaw Hills, though their grip on the slopes has weakened. Silithid swarmers broke through the earth at the Writhing Deep, southeast of the hills, and drove the clan back. Their chieftains have retreated deeper into Woodpaw Den.

Mountain giants also roam these woods. They were summoned from the mountains during the Third War to repel the Burning Legion. Now they crush travelers and Horde interlopers who cross their path.

subzone:workshop-entrance.text: Workshop Entrance. Past the Train Depot, Workshop Entrance offers another way into Gnomeregan. The passage skirts the front gates and reaches the Engineering Labs in the irradiated city. Past the Train Depot, Workshop Entrance crosses the cavernous workshop floor toward Gnomeregan’s industrial heart. The opening to the Loading Room lies on one side. The passage runs straight to the Engineering Labs, away from the fortified gates near the surface. There, leper gnomes and troggs contest the way. Those seeking to reclaim the underground capital can use this side door to bypass the first perimeter.

subzone:writhing-deep.text: Writhing Deep. In southeastern Feralas, the Writhing Deep’s hive keeps growing and threatens nearby wildlife and encampments. Zukk'ash silithid widen their burrow, upsetting the forest’s balance. Across southeastern Feralas, the Zukk'ash swarm spreads through the lowlands. Silithid dig winding tunnels and guard their resinous eggs. As the hive grows, wild creatures grow restless and nearby gnoll packs stir. Displaced predators press close to Horde paths and native sanctuaries.

subzone:writhing-haunt.text: Writhing Haunt. East of the Ruins of Andorhal, plague vapors drift from the Writhing Haunt across the Western Plaguelands. The Scourge seized this farmstead, once fertile land that fed Lordaeron, and turned it into a source of disease. During the Third War, the Writhing Haunt fell swiftly, like many human homesteads around Andorhal. Its fields now yield rot instead of crops. The Scourge planted an enormous plague cauldron in the tilled earth, where it continually vents diseased vapors. Rotting ghouls, freezing ghouls, and fetid zombies wander the overgrown furrows. Cauldron Lord Razarch commands them and guards the machinery. The cauldron's choking miasma has not driven everyone away. Mulgris Deepriver, a tauren druid, lingers inside one of the dilapidated farmhouses. He came to heal nature's wounds, but the plague has stricken him too. Unable to cure the suffering beasts, he asks capable travelers to grant the diseased wolves and other wildlife a swift, merciful release.

subzone:wyrmbog.text: Wyrmbog. Black dragons hold Wyrmbog, south of the Dragonmurk in Dustwallow Marsh. Their caves cut into the ridges, where Onyxia and Emberstrife keep their lairs. Black dragons patrol the scorched mire beneath towering bones. Whelps and mature drakes fill the air, while toxic fumes and wild beasts make the bog perilous to cross. Onyxia's Lair and Emberstrife's cavernous den lie within these reaches. The black dragonflight holds the southern marsh, and few travelers can pass safely through its territory.

subzone:yojamba-isle.text:
Yojamba Isle. On Yojamba Isle, Zandalari emissaries seek champions to face horrors awakening in Zul'Gurub. Their camp lies off Stranglethorn Vale's northwestern coast, near the waters leading to Westfall, and calls on Horde and Alliance alike. The Zandalar Tribe keeps an uneasy peace on Yojamba Isle, though most trolls in Stranglethorn Vale are hostile to outsiders. As priests and lorekeepers of troll civilization, the Zandalari have watched the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub turn to Hakkar the Soulflayer.

A fully summoned blood god threatens the world, so the Zandalari have traveled far from their ancestral home to establish a staging ground. They call on capable adventurers from either faction to help curb the danger. Yojamba Isle lies northwest of the Vile Reef and the haunted ruins along the mainland beaches. Ironclad Cove's massive hidden sea-gate lies to the north, and wandering sea beasts frequent the shallows. Though its position is precarious, the Zandalari camp offers a quiet refuge. Exotic rituals, sacred altars, and ancient knowledge give solace and power to those preparing to march into the jungle's darkest ruins.

subzone:zalashji-s-den.text: Zalashji's Den. Along Tanaris's eastern shore, Zalashji keeps to a lonely cave in the bluffs. Zalashji lives alone in a cave on Tanaris's eastern shore. While naga across Kalimdor gather in war parties or coastal outposts, he has made his home in this isolated cavern, far from the region's settlements and desert ruins. Travelers following the surf should approach the cave mouth with caution. Why Zalashji chose this place is unknown.

subzone:zul-farrak.text: Zul'Farrak. In northwestern Tanaris, Sandfury trolls hold Zul'Farrak behind guarded gates. Long cut off from their kin, they rely on dark voodoo and an army of the dead. Inside Zul'Farrak, Sandfury trolls endure the harsh wastes of Tanaris. Little survives of the city's distant past beyond troll legend. Across the desert, its people are known for their ruthlessness. Their priests dig up their own dead and raise them as a shambling army within the sun-bleached stronghold. In Gadgetzan, whispers tell of treasures and terrors behind Zul'Farrak's guarded gates. Troll lore speaks of Sul'thraze the Lasher, a legendary broadsword broken into two blades and hidden somewhere in the city. More troubling are the tales of Sergeant Bly and his band of mercenaries, captured after entering the city. Other rumors tell of Gahz'rilla, an ancient hydra demigod said to sleep in a sacred pool at the city's heart.

subzone:zul-gurub.text:
Zul'Gurub. In northeastern Stranglethorn Vale, Zul'Gurub's jungle trolls scheme to summon an ancient entity into the world. The ruined temple city once stood at the heart of the Gurubashi Empire. Thousands of years ago, Zul'Gurub was the vibrant capital of the Gurubashi Empire. Its stone ziggurats rose over a realm united under Gurubashi rule. Then civil war came, roughly fifteen hundred years before the Dark Portal opened.

The Atal'ai, a radical sect of priests, tried to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer and claim absolute power. Loyalist tribes joined forces and defeated them. The Atal'ai were banished north to the Swamp of Sorrows. The war broke the empire, and Zul'Gurub became a violent shadow of its former grandeur.

subzone:zul-mashar.text:
Zul'Mashar. In northeastern Eastern Plaguelands, the Mossflayers cling to Zul'Mashar and its ruins. Their ancient capital was broken by wars with human kingdoms, then ravaged by the Plague of Undeath. Before the Scourge crossed northern Lordaeron, Zul'Mashar was the seat of power for the Mossflayer forest trolls. Years of border skirmishes with Lordaeron's humans broke their lands into fragments. Then the Plague of Undeath swept through the region, striking trolls and humans alike.

Mazra'Alor's great stepped ziggurat still rises above the ruins, though little else remains of the capital's former glory. Warlord Thresh'jin and Zul'Brin Warpbranch command the surviving trolls, who cling to their ancient home. Many do not see the Scourge beginning to turn their own kin into rotting monstrosities.

zone:alteracvalley.text:
Alterac Valley. In Alterac Valley, the Frostwolves and Stormpike dwarves fight for control of the snow. The dwarves seek riches and relics they believe link them to their ancestors, while the Frostwolves fight to drive them out. Each side presses through towers and graveyards toward the other's general: Vanndar Stormpike in Dun Baldar or Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep. Gul'dan exiled Durotan's Frostwolf clan for defying him, and the orcs found refuge in this cold valley. They made it their home. Long afterward, young Thrall found his father's people here and learned shaman ways from Drek'Thar, the elder.

Thrall now leads the Horde in Kalimdor. Many Frostwolves remain in the valley under Drek'Thar's guidance, guarding their homeland fiercely. Led by Vanndar Stormpike, the Stormpike Guard is an expedition of Ironforge dwarves based at the northern fortress of Dun Baldar. They came for the valley's mines and for relics they believe link them to their ancestors.

They have dug in with bunkers and towers, holding fast with stubborn pride. The Frostwolves call them invaders; the dwarves claim the valley's secrets by right of discovery. The battle for Alterac Valley pits one army against another. Fighters storm towers and bunkers, seize graveyards, and claim the valley's mines for their side.

Each side must break through to the enemy general and bring them down. The Horde faces Vanndar Stormpike in Dun Baldar; the Alliance faces Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep.

zone:arathibasin.text:
Arathi Basin. In Arathi Basin, the League of Arathor and the Defilers fight over the valley's wealth. The League seeks to reclaim Arathor's lost lands for Stormwind, while the Forsaken aim to cut the humans off from their dwarven allies to the south. Its farm, stables, lumber mill, blacksmith and gold mine feed the war. Long before the Third War, Arathi Basin's fields, mills and mines fed Stromgarde, heir to ancient Arathor. When Lordaeron fell and Stromgarde crumbled, the valley was left almost undefended, though its farmsteads and workshops still stood.

Whoever holds them now commands grain, timber, iron and gold. Those stores keep an army in the field, and make this quiet valley one of the most fought-over places in the highlands. The League of Arathor is an Alliance company formed from Stromgarde's survivors and their friends. Backed by Stormwind, they work from Refuge Pointe and have sworn to reclaim the lands their forebears built.

The Defilers are the Forsaken's answer: hardened troops of the Undercity under Varimathras's watchful eye. They fight alongside the Horde at Hammerfall. Their aim is to take the basin's riches and sever the road joining the northern humans to the dwarves of the south. Five strongpoints decide the battle: the farm, the stables, the lumber mill, the blacksmith and the gold mine. Each side races to raise its banner over them and defend what it claims. Every strongpoint held adds to its store of resources.

Raiders slip between the points to seize one while the enemy is busy elsewhere. The side that gathers enough resources first wins the basin, for a time.

zone:darkspearislands.text:
Darkspear Islands. The Horde and Alliance fight across the Darkspear Islands off Kalimdor's coast. The ceremonial isles are sacred to Vol'jin's trolls, while the Alliance seeks a foothold on the shore and a chance to strike at the Horde's pride. Victory goes to the side that holds the strongpoints, seizes the Darkspear Islands flag and gathers 2000 resources first. The Darkspear are an island people. Driven from Stranglethorn Vale by larger, crueler rivals, they made their lives among the islands of the southern seas. They keep these isles off Kalimdor's coast for their rites and the loa they honor.

On islands like these, Thrall's storm-wrecked fleet found Sen'jin's people beset by Kul Tiran sailors, murlocs and a sea witch. There, the trolls first swore themselves to the Horde. To a Darkspear, an enemy banner over the ceremonial grounds means desecration as well as defeat. For the Horde, holding the isles is a debt of honor. The Darkspear stood with Thrall when the Horde had little else, so orcs, tauren and Forsaken fight beside them to keep the trolls' holy ground. For the Alliance, these islands are a foothold off Kalimdor's coast and a way to strike where Horde pride runs deepest. Neither side speaks of peace. Every landing is answered, and every fallen camp is fought over again. Numbers alone cannot hold the islands. The fighting runs from the Camp and the old Ruins to the Abandoned Tower and Shipwreck Cove. Each side builds up its store of resources by capturing and holding the strongpoints. Seizing the Darkspear Islands flag can turn the tide. The first side to gather 2000 resources wins the day and drives its enemies back to their ships, until the next landing.

zone:hyjal.text:
Mount Hyjal. On Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil still crowns the sacred mountain above the second Well of Eternity. In the last battle of the Third War, night elves, humans and orcs held the slopes against the Burning Legion until Archimonde fell at the World Tree's roots. The battle scarred the mountain, and the wounded tree still stands over the Well. Ten thousand years ago, after the Great Sundering, Illidan Stormrage poured stolen waters from the first Well of Eternity into a lake atop Mount Hyjal. There he made a second Well. The Dragon Aspects raised the World Tree Nordrassil over its waters to guard it. Their blessings gave the night elves immortality and bound them deeply to the Emerald Dream. For millennia, the kaldorei watched over the mountain while their druids slept in the barrow deeps beneath it. During the Third War, Archimonde led the Scourge and the Burning Legion up Mount Hyjal to drain the Well and destroy the World Tree. Jaina Proudmoore's humans and Thrall's Horde set aside old hatreds to stand with Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage.

They held the slopes while Malfurion prepared a trap. When Archimonde reached Nordrassil, Malfurion sounded the Horn of Cenarius. Thousands of wisps swarmed the demon, and the tree's stored power tore him apart. The night elves lost their immortality, and Nordrassil was scorched. Beneath Mount Hyjal lie the barrow deeps, where the Druids of the Claw slept in bear form for thousands of years. Malfurion woke them with the Horn of Cenarius to fight the Legion. Today, the barrow deeps and hyjal summit, high on the mountain, rank among Kalimdor's most perilous places. Only great war bands of seasoned heroes can face them.

zone:warsonggulch.text:
Warsong Gulch. At the border of Ashenvale and the Barrens, Warsong Gulch is where the Horde and Alliance fight without pause. Warsong orcs cut timber for the Horde, while the night elves of Silverwing Hold defend their sacred forest. Fighters of many races raid the opposing stronghold to seize its banner. The Horde builds its home in Kalimdor with wood, much of it cut in Ashenvale. The Warsong clan, Grom Hellscream's warriors, have felled trees here since the Horde first landed. Their Warsong Mill at the gulch's end supplies the Horde's camps and walls. The night elves see each fallen tree as a wound to a forest they have guarded for ten thousand years. They also remember that Grom's warriors slew Cenarius in these woods. The Horde's fighters are the Warsong Outriders, supplied from Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern edge of the Barrens. There, Kelm Hargunth keeps them armed and fed. The Silverwing Sentinels of Silverwing Hold stand against them.

These night elf warriors are sworn to drive every invader from Ashenvale, and Illiyana Moonblaze supplies them at Silverwing Grove. Allies also flock to the gulch: dwarves and humans beside the Sentinels, and tauren, trolls and Forsaken beside the Outriders. The Warsong Mill stands at one end of the gulch, and Silverwing Hold at the other. Each stronghold keeps its side's banner. Fighters raid the enemy's hold, seize its flag and race back as defenders hunt them down. Every banner carried home strikes at the enemy's pride. The side that captures the most wins the day.
